item.title: [dailybulletin.com] Mookie Betts stays hot as Dodgers hammer Giants
item.dc:creator: Doug Padilla
item.description: LOS ANGELES — Mookie Betts is showing that the view from the top offers a wide range of possibilities. item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES — Mookie Betts is showing that the view from the top offers a wide range of possibilities.
Hitting in Shohei Ohtani’s leadoff spot for the second consecutive game, Betts’ four-hit performance Saturday topped his three-hit output from Friday and started some serious downhill momentum toward a 10-4 victory over the San Francisco Giants.
The victory kept the Dodgers two games behind the Milwaukee Brewers for the best record in the National League with seven games remaining. That includes four games against the Giants, who continue to limp toward the finish line of a miserable, injury-riddled season.
Betts couldn’t be feeling better, with his past two games part of a run of 10 hits over the last three games he has played. After more than two months of looking for an offensive leader, Betts has charged into the role, while reaching base five times Saturday.
“It’s good; It’s fun,” Betts said. “But the main thing is doing it when it counts. So right now, we just keep laying the foundation, and then when playoffs come, we just need it to show up (offensively).”
The Dodgers expect Ohtani to return for the playoffs as he makes progress from biceps and knee discomfort. Betts, though, is proving to be a more-than-adequate emergency replacement.
“You know, I couldn’t tell you that I saw this (coming), but I just felt that he was stronger,” manager Dave Roberts said. “He’s worked hard on that. He looks great. He’s not going to stop working, and just for it to come together has been great, and I think for me it’s just trying to keep him confident.”
The Dodgers also have been transformed by the emergence of Will Smith, who returned at the start of September after three months away because of neck inflammation. He had a home run among his three hits to give him homers in consecutive games, with three over his past eight contests.
“He’ll play two or three that last series (at San Francisco), but yeah, after that, he’ll be our guy (for the playoffs),” Roberts said.
There is also 21-year-old rookie Josue De Paula, who has continued to operate with ease since arriving in the major leagues last week. De Paula had a two-run single Saturday and walked twice while scoring two runs.
All of it overshadowed Tarik Skubal’s ninth start for the Dodgers. The two-time American League Cy Young Award winner was far from his best, allowing four runs on eight hits over five innings. His three strikeouts were his least in an outing with his new club.
Skubal unleashed his frustrations in the dugout by throwing his glove and cap at the bench, while firing an empty sports drink bottle at the wall.
“Sometimes you get frustrated and you got to get it out,” Skubal said. “It’s no good just keeping it pent up. So yeah, I’m a believer in getting that stuff out and kind of just moving on from the moment. The frustration is based on execution and knowing who I am and I’m just not doing that.”
Skubal blamed a lack of fastball command for the inability to shut down the Giants.
“Not driving it up and in (and) kind of pulling the ball down at times, pushing it up at times,” Skubal said. “I think pitching is almost all fastball command and mine wasn’t great today.”
And yet the offense allowed Skubal (11-7) to pick up the win, while improving to 4-2 with a 2.95 ERA for the Dodgers.
“That’s our job. That’s what we’re supposed to do,” Betts said. “So sometimes it’s them, sometimes it’s us. As long as we win.”
Kyle Tucker provided a scare when he fouled a ball off the side of his right knee early in the game then departed in the seventh with the Dodgers up six runs. Tucker reached base twice Saturday after collecting six hits with two home runs the previous two games.
“Whatever’s working at the time, you just ride it out, whether or not it’s the way you want to go about it,” said Tucker, who expects to play Sunday. “If it’s working, it’s working. You just try to go up there and put up competitive at-bats and just do your part on defense.”
The offense was not only productive, it was steady. The Dodgers scored runs in each of the first six innings and when they were held scoreless in the seventh, Betts still reached base with a walk.
Betts opened the game for the Dodgers with a leadoff double and scored on a Max Muncy double. Betts brought home his own run with an RBI single in the second.
The Dodgers received Smith’s home run in the third and got an RBI double from Betts in the fourth but were still tied 4-4 heading into the bottom of the fifth. They blew the game open from there, getting a go-ahead two-run single from Tommy Edman and an RBI pinch-hit single from Miguel Rojas for a 7-4 lead.
They scored three more times in the sixth, getting a Smith RBI single followed by a two-run single from De Paula.
“I think this is the first time, seems like all year, that we’ve had four or five hitters swing the bats well for four or five games,” Roberts said. “So it’s been really good to see. Obviously, Mookie is a big part of it, but everyone else is doing their part.”
The Dodgers now have a 5-4 lead in the Giants in the season series and are in line for a sweep Sunday, which would be their first against their longtime rival since April of 2024.

item.title: [New York Post] Mookie Betts thriving batting first: Should he hit leadoff for Dodgers instead of Shohei Ohtani?
item.dc:creator: Jack Harris
item.description: Plan A, as always, is Shohei Ohtani. But over the last couple nights, Plan B has looked pretty good too. item.content:encoded:
Plan A, as always, is Shohei Ohtani.
But over the last couple nights, Plan B has looked pretty good too.
Whenever Ohtani returns from the injured list, the two-way star will likely reprise his customary role as the Dodgers’ leadoff hitter –– one he has held since halfway through his debut 2024 season with the team.
Likely, however, was as far as manager Dave Roberts was willing to describe it on Saturday.
Because in Ohtani’s absence, Mookie Betts has made a case to spearhead the team’s order, too.
Over the last week, a red-hot Betts has served as the Dodgers’ leadoff hitter three times. In each of those contests, he delivered a vintage performance.
There was a 2-for-4 display with an RBI and a double in Miami last week.
A 3-for-4 outburst with two home runs (including one to lead off the game) against the San Francisco Giants on Friday night.
Then, a 4-for-4, three-double, two-RBI, one-walk masterpiece in another 10-4 rout of the Giants on Saturday, a victory that lowered the Dodgers’ magic number to clinch a first-round playoff bye down to four with eight days remaining in the season.
“I just think he’s physically in a better spot than he has been,” Roberts said after Saturday’s outburst, which pushed Betts’ season average up to .261 and OPS to .785. “The ball’s coming off the right way.”
Of course, Betts has been crushing the ball regardless of where he’s been in the order lately. Since Aug. 5, he is batting .336 in 39 games with nine home runs, 12 doubles, 31 RBIs and a 1.008 OPS.
It has marked the former MVP’s best extended stretch since early in the 2024 season. It has been a reminder that there’s still plenty of life left in his previously slumping bat.
“I know I’m still capable of it,” the 33-year-old Betts said. “I know it was in there somewhere.”
Added Roberts: “It just doesn’t matter where you hit him, who he’s facing, [what’s] the situation –– he’s taking good at-bats.”
Betts’ impact at the top of the lineup specifically, however, has been impossible to ignore over the last week; especially when juxtaposed with the ongoing uncertainty surrounding Ohtani, who is expected back next week from right arm and left knee injuries but still doesn’t figure to be 100% physically.
That’s why, after writing Betts’ name in at the leadoff spot for a second-straight day Saturday, Roberts was asked if it’s still a certainty that Ohtani will remain in the leadoff spot upon his return.
“Yeah, I mean, I think that’s my first kind of thought,” Roberts said. “But until he gets back, or when he gets back, then I’ll kind of potentially read and react.”
Much will obviously depend on how Ohtani looks, which will be the biggest question after a 6-for-52 slump leading up to his IL stint.
Roberts also cited other factors like trying to match up against either right- or left-handed pitching, leaving the door open to some game-by-game tinkering in October.
“I haven’t really thought too much about it [yet],” he insisted.
The way Betts is going, though, it might soon become a critical lineup-construction decision.
Run the risk with a potentially diminished but ever-dangerous Ohtani? Or give the most at-bats as possible to the team’s hottest current hitter?
Granted, Betts hasn’t pushed to take over the leadoff spot, saying Friday that “I’ll hit wherever” and “there’s a guy that’s named Shohei that needs to be up there and to get us going.”
But if the Dodgers need to pivot among Ohtani’s ongoing ailments, he is quickly emerging as their best fallback option –– especially with their initial leadoff replacement, the switch-hitting Tommy Edman, mired in a brutal 2-for-39 slump.
“Going back up there, it is fun,” Betts acknowledged, having played almost 1,100 career games as a leadoff hitter over his 13-year career. “Kind of feels like home.”
“You do got to kind of prepare for whatever,” Roberts added, “and I just think that Mookie’s swinging the bat well, has hit there many times throughout his career, so it just kind of makes sense.”
For now, the Dodgers’ bigger priority will be making sure Betts keeps swinging the bat well, whether that’s in the No. 1 spot or somewhere else in the heart of the order.
His late-season surge has been one of the biggest reasons the team has survived Ohtani’s absence –– winning 13 of its last 16 despite the superstar slugger playing in just one of those contests.
“It’s good. It’s fun. But the main thing is doing it when it counts,” Betts said of his recent success. “Right now, just keep laying the foundation, and then when playoffs come, just need it to show up.”
Still, given how things are trending at the moment, it might not be a surprise if the Dodgers’ first at-bat of the playoffs belonged to their streaking shortstop.
“I couldn’t tell you that I saw this [coming],” Roberts conceded. “But he’s got stronger. He’s worked hard on that … And just for it to come together has been great.”

item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.description: Mookie Betts, Dodgers stay hot in romp over Giants (Photo credit: Jayne Kamin) Mookie Betts tied a season high with four hits, Tommy Edman delivered a go-ahead two-run single and the Los Angeles Dodgers stayed within two games of the best record in the National League with a 10-4 victory over the visiting San Francisco Giants on Saturday. item.content:encoded:
Mookie Betts, Dodgers stay hot in romp over Giants
(Photo credit: Jayne Kamin)
Mookie Betts tied a season high with four hits, Tommy Edman delivered a go-ahead two-run single and the Los Angeles Dodgers stayed within two games of the best record in the National League with a 10-4 victory over the visiting San Francisco Giants on Saturday.
Betts has 10 hits over his past three games, including seven in the past two while operating out of the leadoff spot in place of an injured Shohei Ohtani. Will Smith hit a home run as the Dodgers (95-60) won for the fifth time in six games and improved to 13-3 since Sept. 3.
Tarik Skubal (11-7) gave up four runs on eight hits over five innings with three strikeouts. The left-hander is now 4-2 with a 2.85 ERA in nine starts for Los Angeles after a trade from the Detroit Tigers on Aug. 2.
Victor Bericoto hit a home run among his two hits for the Giants (64-91) while Yunior Marte (0-1) gave up six runs on eight hits over 4 2/3 innings in his fourth career appearance and second start.
San Francisco lost for the sixth time in its past eight games in its next-to-last road game of the season.
Max Muncy had an RBI double in the first inning to score Betts as the Dodgers started a stretch in which they scored in each of the first six innings. Betts had an RBI single in the second.
The Giants tied the score in the third on Bericoto's fifth home run over his first 35 career games.
Los Angeles went back on top 3-2 in the third on Smith's leadoff home run. Both teams scored in the fourth, with San Francisco tying the score 4-4 in the fifth on a double from Jung Hoo Lee.
Edman's two-run single in the fifth gave the Dodgers the lead for good and they added another in the inning for a 7-4 lead on a Miguel Rojas single.
In the sixth, Smith added an RBI single, while rookie Josue De Paula followed with a two-run single for a 10-4 advantage.
Los Angeles has a 5-4 advantage in the season series with four games still remaining between the teams.
Smith went 3-for-5 as the Dodgers collected 15 hits.
Lee went 2-for-4 for the Giants and drove in a run. The Giants had two hits in a dozen at-bats with runners in scoring position.
--Field Level Media

item.content:encoded:
Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said after Saturday's game that there's a "good chance" Ohtani (knee/biceps) will be activated during next week's series against the Padres, Fabian Ardaya of The Athletic reports.
Ohtani ran the bases on the field prior to Saturday's game and also advanced to taking simulated at-bats against the team's Trajekt machine. It sounds like the Dodgers are pleased with Ohtani's progress, enough so that he's penciled in to return during the homestand. If Ohtani is activated Wednesday when first eligible, he could play in up to five games before the end of the regular season.

item.content:encoded:
Mookie conecta cuatro hits y los Dodgers se llevan la serie ante Gigantes
This browser does not support the video element.
LOS ÁNGELES -- La manera en que Mookie Betts ha estado bateando últimamente recuerda a sus mejores días como jugador de los Dodgers.
Betts remolcó dos carreras y anotó otras dos en una actuación de cuatro hits, mientras Los Ángeles superaba a San Francisco, 10-4, la noche del sábado en el Dodger Stadium, preparando el escenario para una oportunidad de barrer la serie del fin de semana.
En enfrentamientos directos de todos los tiempos, los Dodgers tienen una ventaja de un juego, 1,293-1,292, con 17 empates, sobre sus rivales de muchos años.
Días antes, antes de que los Dodgers aseguraran su 13er título de la División Oeste de la Liga Nacional en las últimas 14 temporadas, el manager Dave Roberts evaluó la situación de su equipo con la postemporada cada vez más cerca. Elogió el desempeño de su cuerpo de lanzadores y destacó las mejoras en la defensa y el corrido de bases. Pero también señaló un área por mejorar: la ofensiva, que ha sido inconsistente durante buena parte de la temporada.
“Creo que, para mí, se trata de poder liquidar a los equipos cuando tenemos oportunidades”, dijo Roberts, haciéndose eco de sentimientos similares que había expresado durante los últimos tres meses.
Los Dodgers aprovecharon esas oportunidades el sábado, y su tercera victoria consecutiva mantuvo su ventaja de cuatro juegos sobre los Bravos por el No. 2 en la Liga Nacional.
En una noche en la que Tarik Skubal batalló durante sus cinco innings y permitió cuatro carreras, su mayor cantidad desde el 24 de junio, su ofensiva estuvo ahí para respaldarlo. Todo comenzó con Betts como primer bate, un puesto que ha sido una especie de puerta giratoria con Shohei Ohtani en la lista de lesionados.
Betts se embasó en sus cinco apariciones al plato por primera vez desde el 16 de abril de 2024. Conectó tres dobles, marcando la primera vez que registra tres extrabases en un juego desde el 7 de julio de 2023. Y ha conectado al menos tres hits en tres juegos consecutivos, igualando la racha más larga de su carrera, también del 11 al 17 de julio de 2021.
No han sido solamente tres buenos días para Betts. En septiembre, batea para .397/.493/.794, con 20 carreras impulsadas, la mayor cantidad del equipo. Si nos remontamos aún más, tiene un OPS de 1.008 en sus últimos 39 juegos.

item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES – Andy Pages went through the paces Saturday afternoon, grinding through an intense on-field workout in the clearest sign yet that he will be ready to return Tuesday to open the final home series of the regular season.
Pages wore a fitness tracker, similar to what soccer players use to monitor all aspects of physical fitness. Coaches and staff put Pages through an estimated five simulated innings all in a compressed window of time.
The All-Star center fielder not only tested his broken left hand, but he also pushed his physical fitness to the limits.
Pages went from hitting to defense to base running and then doing it all over again to make sure he is ready for the rigors of play next week. His return is expected to come in the opener of a three-game series against the San Diego Padres.
While that kind of energy output is typically done in a rehab game, there aren’t many minor league options remaining this late in the season.
One thing Pages will not get is the chance to hit off a pitcher at full velocity.
“I think that from what I understand, we don’t have really any available arms,” manager Dave Roberts said about the prospect of a live batting practice session. “A lot of our guys are playing in playoff games in the minors, and we have (Eric) Lauer, who’s on the IL. So, we don’t really have anyone.”
It is not ideal for a player coming off the uncertainty that comes with a hand injury. But Pages did show that his hand soreness has subsided enough to hit multiple balls over the outfield wall.
“I’m expecting good at-bats,” Roberts said. “I can’t speak to the performance. I just want him to have good at-bats, and I’m not sure where he’s going to hit. Somewhere middle to the bottom (of the order), I think. I think I’m waiting just like you guys are waiting to see how it looks.”
The Dodgers close the season with six consecutive games, including the season-ending series at San Francisco next weekend.
“Six in a row, and that seems pretty aggressive (for Pages),” Roberts said. “So, I think that we do want to get him as many at-bats as possible, but we have to make sure that his legs are under him, feeling good, so we don’t go backward or get injured in that respect. It is going to be a balancing act and just keeping a keen eye on Andy, for sure.”
Regardless of what his swing looks like, the Dodgers still trust him in center field. After all, his World Series-saving catch in Game 7 last season came as a late-inning defensive replacement.
“Playing a premium position and playing it well is hugely important,” Roberts said.
ROTATING THE ROTATION
Left-hander Blake Snell is not expected to pitch in the upcoming series against the Padres, but he has not been ruled out for the series against the Giants next weekend.
Snell left his start Thursday after one inning at Cincinnati because of groin discomfort.
“He’s trending very well,” Roberts said about Snell’s recovery in recent days.
Right-hander Roki Sasaki is expected to pitch in the upcoming series against the Padres, although his role has not yet been specified. There is a chance Sasaki could start a game against San Diego, or come out of the bullpen, which had been his expected role in the postseason.
“it will be multiples for sure,” Roberts said about Sasaki’s innings count. “I just don’t know exactly when.”
A LEADING MAN
Shohei Ohtani is still expected to return to play before the regular season ends next Sunday, although there remains no target date.
In the meantime, the Dodgers continue to weigh their options in the leadoff spot. Tommy Edman was there immediately after Ohtani went on the injured list earlier this month, Josue De Paula took a turn there and Mookie Betts has been the latest to stake a claim.
Betts hit two home runs from the leadoff spot Friday and was back at the top of the lineup Saturday.
“Yeah, I think that certainly there is an uncertainty with Shohei, all the while expecting him to be back,” Roberts said. “But you do got to kind of prepare for whatever, and I just think that Mookie’s swinging the bat well, has hit there many times throughout his career, so it just kind of makes sense.”
Betts had three hits Wednesday at Cincinnati and three more Friday against the Giants in the leadoff spot, including two home runs. He is batting .356 with six home runs and 18 RBIs in 15 September games.
ALSO
The Dodgers are expected to select a pitcher to pick up bulk innings Sunday in a hybrid bullpen game against the Giants, but the exact plan remains undetermined.
UP NEXT
Giants (TBA) at Dodgers (TBA), Sunday, 1:10 p.m.), SportsNet LA, 570 AM, 1020 AM

item.content:encoded:
【ロサンゼルス19日（日本時間20日）＝横山尚杜】米大リーグ、ドジャースの大谷翔平投手（32）が実在する投手の投球軌道を再現できる打撃マシン「トラジェクトアーク」に対する打撃練習を再開した。ベイツ打撃コーチは「強度は100％」と患部の回復とスイング改善を強調。ロバーツ監督は、復帰を見据える大谷に対し、適切な過程を踏み、「実戦に近い打席の経験」を復帰条件として、コーチ陣に厳命していることを明かした。
「強度は100％と言っていいだろう」。大谷のリハビリの進展具合を打撃コーチが証言。この日から実在する投手の球筋を再現できるマシン「トラジェクトアーク」に対する打撃練習を開始したと明かし、そのスイングは完全に近い状態とした。
「ケージの中のコントロールされた中ではいい状態にある。ここまでは全て順調で、予定通り進んでいると言っていいと思う」
前日から2日連続で大谷の打撃練習を確認したベイツ打撃コーチがリハビリの〝舞台裏〟を語った。15日にスイングと打撃練習を再開した大谷は17日にコーチが投じる球を打ち返す練習を始め、この日はさらに強度が上がる高性能マシンに対する打撃に移行。また、試合前の打撃練習中には、屋外でベースランニングもこなした。
ただ、大谷の復帰時期は依然、不透明。9日に「右上腕二頭筋の炎症」で負傷者リスト（IL）入り以降、慎重を期してリハビリはスローペースで推移している。23日（同24日）パドレス戦の最短復帰は厳しい状況だ。ロバーツ監督は「フィールドでの打撃を見たい。コーチが投げる球を打ち、トラジェクトアークの球を打ち、実戦に近い打席を経験する。その過程を想定して、コーチにも強く伝えている」と言及。万全に近い状態で出場した試合から1カ月以上要しており、実戦勘の鈍化や強度の高いプレーによる体への耐久の懸念も持っている。
ベイツ打撃コーチは大谷の打撃で〝危険サイン〟がないか注視していると明かした。「左膝より、右腕の方が大きな懸念だった。片手のフォロースルーはショウヘイが何か不安を抱えているサイン」。スイング後に右手一本になるスイングは患部に違和感がある証左とし、現状は両腕のフォロースルーになっているという。
この日で地区シリーズの初戦まで2週間を切った。「限られた時間で彼が成功できる可能性を最大限に高めないといけない」と指揮官。多くの不確実性が伴う状況で、3連覇を狙うポストシーズンが迫っている。

item.title: [DodgerBlue.com] Mookie Betts, Will Smith rescue Tarik Skubal from worst start with Dodgers

item.description: The Los Angeles Dodgers blew three separate leads and Tarik Skubal had his worst start with the team, but the end result was another comfortable win over the San Francisco Giants. item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers blew three separate leads and Tarik Skubal had his worst start with the team, but the end result was another comfortable win over the San Francisco Giants.
Mookie Betts once again was a catalyst from the leadoff spot, and he received help from Will Smith as they combined for seven hits and four RBI in the Dodgers’ win.
Next for the Dodgers is an opportunity to sweep the Giants heading into an off day before their final home series of the regular season begins.
Dodgers 10, Giants 4: key takeaways
Leadoff hitter Mookie Betts
Coming off a multi-homer night, Betts went 4-for-4 with two runs scored and two RBI. He reached base safely in all five plate appearances.
Betts’ double in the first inning led to the Dodgers jumping out to an early lead, and he then extended it to 2-0 with an RBI single in the second inning.
Betts continued to swing a hot bat as his RBI double in the fourth inning put the Dodgers up 4-3. He then hit a leadoff double in the sixth to help spark the Dodgers’ second three-run inning of the night to break the game open.
Despite all of his recent success, Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said he hasn’t given much thought to keeping Betts in the leadoff spot once Shohei Ohtani returns from the 15-day injured list.
Will Smith power swing
Smith’s first contribution was a leadoff home run in the bottom of the third inning that broke a 2-2 tie. The homer was Smith’s second in as many games.
He then led off the fifth with a single, and the Dodgers went on to score three runs.
Tarik Skubal’s struggles
Skubal stranded baserunners in the first and second innings before running into some trouble in the third. Victor Bericoto’s two-run homer tied the game, and the Giants started the fourth inning with back-to-back singles. However, they only scored one run in that instance due to merely relying on two sacrifice bunts in a row.
Bericoto made hard contact off Skubal again in the fifth inning, with his leadoff double setting the table for Jung Hoo Lee’s extra-base hit.
The four earned runs Skubal allowed marked his most in nine starts for the Dodgers. The five innings pitched matched his shortest outing since being traded to the team.
Magic number update
With their win, the Dodgers magic number to clinch at least the No. 2 seed in the National League is now down to four. They must finish with a better record than the Atlanta Braves due to not holding the head-to-head tiebreaker.

item.content:encoded:
After sim game, Pages on track to return for next series
This browser does not support the video element.
LOS ANGELES -- Four hours before first pitch, Andy Pages was putting on a one-man show at Dodger Stadium.
Pages took part in an extended simulated game before Saturday night's contest against the Giants, rotating between hitting off the machine, running the bases and playing defense. The All-Star center fielder came away feeling good, manager Dave Roberts said, and is lined up to return from the injured list as soon as Tuesday's opener against the Padres.
Pages' season hit an abrupt pause on Aug. 21, when he sustained a fracture in his left hand after being struck by a pitch. After a minor procedure on his hand, which involved inserting a compression screw to speed healing, Pages has progressed through rehab on schedule. His expected return will give him six regular-season games to get back up to speed.
"I think that we do want to get him as many at-bats as possible, but we have to make sure that his legs are under him, feeling good, so we don’t go backward or get injured in that respect," Roberts said. "It is going to be a balancing act and just keeping a keen eye on Andy, for sure."
This browser does not support the video element.
Saturday's simulated game is the closest thing Pages will get to real game action before being activated from the 10-day IL, as the Triple-A regular season ends Sunday. Pages won't face live pitching either, because the Dodgers' injured pitchers have not progressed to the point of throwing to hitters, and their prospects have been pitching in the Minor League playoffs across various levels.
The Dodgers aren't entirely sure what kind of hitter they'll get back in Pages, coming off a hand injury with limited opportunities to build up. He was hitting .272 with a .796 OPS at the time of his injury, and his 80 RBIs remain tied for the team lead with Shohei Ohtani, who is also expected back from the IL at some point next week.
While Pages' bat could be questionable, the Dodgers feel great about getting his glove back. Pages has developed into an excellent center fielder, ranking in the 94th percentile among qualified defenders with eight outs above average, according to Statcast.
As much as the Dodgers would love for Pages to make an impact at the plate when he returns, he would provide the value they need by holding down center field. Run prevention is always important, but it's especially key in the postseason, when runs are even harder to come by.
"The defense is a big reason why he’s still a valuable player, even coming off the IL, with the uncertainty of the offense, which we’ll still bet on," Roberts said. "But playing a premium position and playing it well is hugely important."

item.content:encoded:
ナ・リーグ西地区優勝を決めたドジャースは、ジャイアンツと対戦する。先発は左腕スクバル。大谷翔平投手（32）はIL入りしているが、試合前に復帰へ向け走塁練習を行った。
1.目指すは「首位バイ（不戦勝）」の獲得（IT'S ALL ABOUT THE BYE）
地区優勝と第1ラウンド免除：ドジャースは金曜日のジャイアンツ戦に勝利し、今季最後となる本拠地での連戦を最高の形で滑り出しました。これにより、ポストシーズン第1ラウンド（ワイルドカード・シリーズ）の免除（バイ）を確保し、10月3日（土）から始まるナショナル・リーグ地区シリーズ（NLDS）第1戦を本拠地で開催するための「マジックナンバー」を「5」としました。
シード順位の争い：レギュラーシーズン残り8試合の時点で、ドジャースはアトランタ・ブレーブスに4ゲーム差をつけており、ナ・リーグ全体の第1シードであるミルウォーキー・ブルワーズを2ゲーム差で追っています。
偉大な連続記録：ドジャースは木曜日に5年連続となるナショナル・リーグ西地区優勝（過去14シーズンで13回目）を達成しました。また、メジャーリーグ記録に並ぶ14シーズン連続でのポストシーズン進出を果たしており、これは1991年～2005年のアトランタ・ブレーブスが樹立した快挙に並ぶ記録です。
2.圧倒的な本塁打攻勢（NOW THAT'S A TIP OF THE CAP）
祝節目の勝利：伝説的な「4+1連続本塁打劇」から20周年の記念日に、ドジャースはジャイアンツを8－2で下しました。この試合でチームは計5本の本塁打を記録し、そのうち4本（2者連続本塁打が2回）は8回裏の攻撃に集中しました。
グラスノーの快投：タイラー・グラスノーが今季最多の10奪三振、6回2失点の好投を見せ、今季5勝目（1敗）を挙げました。
ベッツの偉業：ムーキー・ベッツが今季初（通算53回目）となる先頭打者本塁打を放ち、殿堂入り選手のクレイグ・ビジオに並ぶMLB歴代4位タイの記録となりました。ベッツは8回にも本塁打を放ち、今季3回目（通算34回目）の1試合複数本塁打を達成しています。
8回の集中砲火：8回裏、マックス・マンシー（29号）とカイル・タッカー（17号）の連続本塁打、続いてムーキー・ベッツ（22号）とウィル・スミス（8号）の連続本塁打が飛び出し、一挙5得点を奪って試合を決定づけました。
3. 9月の打撃陣の調子（SEPTEMBER SLUGGING）
ムーキー・ベッツ：9月の15試合で打率.356、出塁率.457、長打率.729、OPS 1.186、6本塁打、18打点と驚異的な成績を残しています。
カイル・タッカー：9月の17試合で6本塁打、13打点、OPS 1.088を記録。特に直近9試合では打率.438、5本塁打、11打点と絶好調です。
テオスカー・ヘルナンデス：8月30日以降の17試合で打率.377、4本塁打、19打点を記録し、自身のシーズン打率を.245から.265まで大きく上昇させました。
4.先発スクーバルの分析（SATURDAYS WITH SKUB）
移籍後の活躍：8月2日にデトロイト・タイガースからトレード移籍して以来、ドジャースで9回目の先発登板となります。移籍後は3勝2敗、防御率2.52、57奪三振に対しわずか11与四球と抜群の制球力と安定感を誇ります。
「9月」の強さ：スクーバルはキャリアを通じて通算26試合で9勝5敗、防御率2.60を記録しており、終盤戦の9月に非常に強い特徴を持っています。
5.その他のニュース
大谷翔平の現状と節目：ちょうど2年前のこの日（2024年9月19日）、大谷翔平はマイアミで6打数6安打、3本塁打、10打点という歴史的パフォーマンスを披露し、MLB史上初の「50本塁打－50盗塁（50－50）」を達成しました。現在の大谷は右二頭筋の炎症により15日間の負傷者リスト（IL）に入っていますが、9月23日には復帰可能となる見込みです。

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Shohei Ohtani takes key step in Dodgers return, with help of new technology
item.dc:creator: Jack Harris
item.description: Shohei Ohtani has taken another step forward in his recovery from right arm and left knee injuries. On Saturday afternoon, the two-way star did base-running drills on the field during Dodgers batting practice — and began taking simulated at-bats against the team's Trajekt Arc pitching machine behind the scenes in the clubhouse batting cages. The former was the more visible development, marking the first time Ohtani had been seen on the field performing physical activities since he went on the in
item.content:encoded:
Shohei Ohtani has taken another step forward in his recovery from right arm and left knee injuries.
On Saturday afternoon, the two-way star did base-running drills on the field during Dodgers batting practice — and began taking simulated at-bats against the team's Trajekt Arc pitching machine behind the scenes in the clubhouse batting cages.
The former was the more visible development, marking the first time Ohtani had been seen on the field performing physical activities since he went on the injured list at the end of last week's homestand.
His work in the hitting cages, however, was a more telling sign of how quickly he might be able to return to action, representing a significant step in what has thus far been a setback-free ramp-up process.
At the start of the week, Ohtani resumed hitting activities with incremental steps. First, he hit off a tee. Then, he took soft tosses from coaches. In recent days, he had begun swinging off a pitching machine, too.
But the Trajekt machine is different; offering players augmented reality at-bats in which a video screen displays a specific pitcher's windup before firing a ball out of a slot from their hand.
In recent years, the technology has become ubiquitous around MLB clubhouses.
And in lieu of a minor-league rehab stint — impossible now with the minor-league season ending — it will be Ohtani's best way to hone a game-ready swing again.
"You hope it bridges the gap a little bit," hitting coach Aaron Bates said. "So between machine, live pitching, Trajekt, somewhere in between that, that's the best you can do."
Bates has been part of the group overseeing Ohtani's recent cage work. He said the slugger has looked "great" and shown no signs of his injuries while returning to full-intensity reps.
"In the cage, in a controlled setting, he's been really good. It's 100% intensity," Bates said. "Once he gets out to the field, if he does a live BP or something like that, and the intensity ramps up, it'll be a good test to see what happens. But in the cage, in the controlled setting, he's been really good."
Before Ohtani went on the injured list, it was evident to the Dodgers' hitting staff that the two-way star "looked extremely compromised," as Bates acknowledged.

Home delivery: Sign up here!Page Six Hollywood: Sign up here!
One key sign: Ohtani was following through on more of his swings with a one-handed finish, something Bates noted is "always kind of a tell for Shohei, whether he's going through something or not, just because he is disconnected a bit from his back side."
Lately, however, Ohtani's two-handed finish has returned in his swing — as has the Dodgers' optimism that he will be able to provide production in their lineup, despite the 6-for-52 slump he was mired in previously.
"I think everything's been good so far," Bates said.
When Ohtani will be activated remains unclear, with his 15-day stint not up until next Wednesday. But manager Dave Roberts and president of baseball operations Andrew Friedman have said they expect him to be back before the end of the regular season.
Bates echoed that sentiment Saturday, saying Ohtani appears to be "on schedule" while deferring any more specific timeline to the training staff.
Ohtani has not asked to get a specific number of simulated at-bats before being activated, Bates added.
"He just kind of goes how he feels," he said. "And the rehab guys will have kind of the exact quantity kind of laid out for them in that sense."
Time will still tell, of course, whether Ohtani will actually look like himself when he returns, or if he the months he spent playing through his injuries have left him too diminished to make his typical impact with the bat.
As Bates noted, it's possible Ohtani could get a live batting practice session against a pitcher before returning (although the organization is short on arms at the moment capable of doing that, Roberts said Saturday). But beyond that, his Trajekt at-bats will likely account for the bulk of his hitting preparation before returning to game action.
"You kind of fire them out there and see what happens," Bates said. "Just like spring training, it kind of takes guys a little bit of time to get their footing. But it depends on the person. Every guy is a little bit different with how much time they need. Some guys don't need a lot."
Ohtani, Bates said, is in that latter category.
And so far, at least, his hitting progression is going about as well as they could have hoped.

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Mookie Betts Could Take Shohei Ohtani’s Leadoff Spot When Dodgers Star Returns
item.dc:creator: Nelson Espinal
item.description: Los Angeles Dodgers manager Dave Roberts addressed the team's lead-off position as Shohei Ohtani sits and Mookie Betts thrives. "I mean, I think that's my first kind of thought," Roberts said to the media, including Dodgers Nation. "But until he gets back, or when he gets back, then I'll kind of po
item.content:encoded:
Los Angeles Dodgers manager Dave Roberts addressed the team's lead-off position as Shohei Ohtani sits and Mookie Betts thrives.
The Shohei Ohtani lead-off question
On Saturday, September 19th, Roberts was asked directly whether Ohtani would lead off when he returned from the injured list, Dodgers Nation's Noel Sanchez reports.
"I mean, I think that's my first kind of thought," Roberts said to the media, including Dodgers Nation.
"But until he gets back, or when he gets back, then I'll kind of potentially read and react if it's a left-right situation. I haven't really thought too much about it."
Ohtani is on the IL with right arm/bicep soreness, which surfaced during his pitching work. He's also battling left knee soreness.
The Dodgers hope rest will help Ohtani, who looked like a shell of his best self in his last few at-bats before sitting out.
Over the last few days, Ohtani has been doing light baseball work and is trending in a good direction, according to Dave Roberts, leaving the door open for him to get some plate appearances before the postseason.
Why Ohtani may not lead off
As the Dodgers found out, a compromised Ohtani cannot touch the same heights as a fully healthy one. As the injuries racked up and the wear led to a hampered swing, Ohtani was not delivering at a level to merit the lead-off spot.
Ohtani hit just .186/.324/.390 in his last 15 games, with production looking really bad over the last seven games: .077 with a .250 OBP.
While Ohtani has dropped off, Mookie Betts has started heating up and is now taking over the leadoff spot in Ohtani's absence.
Mookie Betts is challenging Ohtani
For most of Ohtani's time out injured, which has been a few weeks now, Tommy Edman has handled most of the lead-off work.
However, Edman is now hitting .135/.274/.231 at lead-off, and Betts is really getting going.
Betts is hitting .356 with a .457 OBP over his last 15 games. Over 30 games, Betts is hitting .298/.384/.529.
Roberts talked about deploying Betts at leadoff for a second straight game, even against a righty pitcher
"I think that certainly there is uncertainty with Shohei, all the while expecting to be back. But you do have to prepare for whatever," Roberts said to the media, including Dodgers Nation.
"I just think Mookie swinging the bat well and has many times throughout his career. It just kind of makes sense."
If Betts keeps this up and Ohtani returns still limited, Roberts will have to think hard about moving the batting order to improve the team's three-peat odds.

Ohtani (knee/biceps) did some base-running during the Dodgers' on-field batting practice Saturday, Jack Harris of the California Post reports.
This marks the first time Ohtani has worked out on the field in front of the media since he went on the 15-day injured list last week. His stint was backdated to Sept. 8, meaning Ohtani is eligible to return this coming Wednesday, though it's uncertain if he will be ready by then. Ohtani figures to push to play in at least a few more regular-season games as a final tuneup before the playoffs.

item.title: [Dodgers Way] Josue De Paula drawing Juan Soto comparisons hints Dodgers were right to bid low
item.dc:creator: Katrina Stebbins
item.description: Josue De Paula has cooled down a bit since his statement game against the Miami Marlins on September 13, but the Los Angeles Dodgers still have a lot to love about their No. 1 prospect. item.content:encoded:
Josue De Paula has cooled down a bit since his statement game against the Miami Marlins on September 13, but the Los Angeles Dodgers still have a lot to love about their No. 1 prospect. It took him 12 at-bats to suffer his first major league strikeout, and he's only struck out once more since then.
De Paula took his knowledge of the strike zone to another level during the Dodgers' latest series opener against the Cincinnati Reds. He got to a 2-2 count against Reds starter Nick Lodolo in the top of the fifth. Lodolo put a sinker low and away that home plate umpire Tom Hanahan called a ball.
Reds catcher Tyler Stephenson was quick to challenge, but at the same time, De Paula had gotten into a crouch and shook his head as if to say, "That one was definitely out of the zone."
De Paula was right, and the Reds lost their one remaining challenge. He went on to walk on the next pitch, and then steal second.
It wasn't quite a Soto shuffle, but it was close enough to draw comparisons. He responded, "Hey, I'm not mad about it."
Revisiting the Dodgers' Juan Soto pursuit as Josue De Paula draw comparisons
The Dodgers were involved in Juan Soto's free agent market in the 2024-25 offseason and went as far as to offer $600 million, which was, of course, eclipsed by the New York Mets' $765 million and even the New York Yankees' $760 million.
At least part of LA's hesitance to offer him a $700-plus million contract was rooted in keeping Shohei Ohtani atop the payroll and not supplanting their star player, but De Paula, though still a very distant eventuality, was on the horizon as well.
Soto and De Paula's prospect profiles are startlingly similar — 70-grade hit, 65 power, 50 run, arm, and field for Soto, and 65-grade hit, 60 power, 40 run and field, and 50 arm for De Paula. Both, as Paula has already put on display, have an advanced understanding of the strike zone.
The Dodgers don't plan well enough around their prospects to try to make a claim that they exited the Soto bidding because they had De Paula in the chamber, but it's certainly been a happy development that the one massive free agent the Dodgers didn't go all-in on happens to be reflected in their No. 1 prospect two years later.

item.title: [webスポルティーバ] 「翔平は翔平」──走る姿に表れていた大谷翔平の異変 ドジャースの判断の是非と、間近で見ていたふたりのコーチの視点
item.dc:creator: 奥田秀樹
item.description: 故障者リスト入りし、今後の成り行きに注目が集まる大谷翔平 photo by Getty Images ロサンゼルス・ドジャースが14年連続のポストシーズン進出を決めた。９月14日（日本時間15日）、敵地でシンシナティ・レッズを４対１で破り、メジャー最長記録に並ぶ14年連続のプレーオフ進出。試合後には選手たちがスパークリングワインで乾杯し、10月への切符を手にした喜びを分かち合った。 だが、そのフィールドに大谷翔平はいなかった。左ひざと右上腕二頭筋に問題を抱え、ドジャース移籍後初めて15日間の負傷者リスト（IL）に入っている。遠征にも同行せず、ロサンゼルスに残った。 15日にはIL入り後、初めてティー打撃を再開したが、最短で復帰できる23日（日本時間24日）の時点でレギュラーシーズンは残り５試合しかない。デーブ・ロバーツ監督はシーズン中の復帰を見込んでいるものの、具体的な日はまだ決まっていない。ポストシーズンでも100％の状態に戻らない可能性がある。なぜ、ここまで来てしまったのか。 その兆候は１カ月前、野球で最も基本的な動作である「走る」ことに、すでに表れていた。 ８月、大谷は左ひざにつ
item.content:encoded:
故障者リスト入りし、今後の成り行きに注目が集まる大谷翔平 photo by Getty Images
ロサンゼルス・ドジャースが14年連続のポストシーズン進出を決めた。９月14日（日本時間15日）、敵地でシンシナティ・レッズを４対１で破り、メジャー最長記録に並ぶ14年連続のプレーオフ進出。試合後には選手たちがスパークリングワインで乾杯し、10月への切符を手にした喜びを分かち合った。
だが、そのフィールドに大谷翔平はいなかった。左ひざと右上腕二頭筋に問題を抱え、ドジャース移籍後初めて15日間の負傷者リスト（IL）に入っている。遠征にも同行せず、ロサンゼルスに残った。
15日にはIL入り後、初めてティー打撃を再開したが、最短で復帰できる23日（日本時間24日）の時点でレギュラーシーズンは残り５試合しかない。デーブ・ロバーツ監督はシーズン中の復帰を見込んでいるものの、具体的な日はまだ決まっていない。ポストシーズンでも100％の状態に戻らない可能性がある。なぜ、ここまで来てしまったのか。
その兆候は１カ月前、野球で最も基本的な動作である「走る」ことに、すでに表れていた。
８月、大谷は左ひざについて興味深い話をしていた。痛みそのものはそれほど強くない。しかし、トップスピードまで上げることが難しく、ベースを回る際には普段より外側に膨らんでしまう。また、自分では間に合うと思って走ったのに予想以上に際どいプレーになったり、アウトになったりする。自分の感覚と実際のスピードとの間に「ズレ」が生じているというのだ。
そこで、その走りを最も近い場所から観察しているふたりのコーチに聞いた。一塁ベースコーチのクリス・ウッドワードと、三塁ベースコーチのディノ・イベルである。
ウッドワードは、大谷の変化をはっきり認識していた。
「トップスピードが少し落ちていることには、間違いなく気づいています。この前、数字も確認しました。正確な数値は覚えていませんが、以前より落ちているのは確かです」
ただし、原因をひざだけに求めることには慎重だった。投打の二刀流を続け、長いシーズンを戦ってきた蓄積疲労かもしれない。32歳という年齢もある。複数の要因が考えられるとしたうえで、「ひざを痛めたことがプラスに働かなかったのは確かでしょう」と話した。特に目についたのは、減速する時だった。
「最も難しいのは止まることです。どんな故障でも、止まる動作が一番難しい」
走塁は単に速く走ればいいわけではない。加速し、ベースへ向かい、角度を変え、再び加速し、最後には止まる。その一連の動きのなかで、大谷の左膝は100％ではなかった。それによってもうひとつの問題も生じていた。
「今の彼は、自分が実際よりも速いと思っているところがある」
大谷は長年、自分ならどこまで行けるのかを身体で覚えてきた。投手のモーション、捕手の送球、外野手の位置を見れば、盗塁できるのか、一塁から三塁へ行けるのかを瞬時に判断できる。
しかし、トップスピードがわずかに落ちれば、その体内時計にも狂いが生じる。実際、本人はセーフになったと思った盗塁がわずかな差でアウトになり、驚く場面があった。ウッドワード自身も「これはセーフになっていないとおかしい」と感じたプレーがあったという。それでも、大谷はプレーを続けた。そしてウッドワードは、今振り返ると非常に重い言葉を口にしていた。
「もし試合に出ず、リハビリに専念し、スピードをイチから作り直すことができていれば、以前に近いスピードまで戻っていたかもしれません。でも、彼は打線に残ることを望みました」
これは９月に大谷がIL入りしたあとの話ではない。８月中旬時点での証言である。
1 / 3
- 1963年、三重県生まれ。関西学院大卒業後、雑誌編集者を経て、フォトジャーナリストとして1990年渡米。NFL、NBA、MLBなどアメリカのスポーツ現場の取材を続け、MLBの取材歴は26年目。幅広い現地野球関係者との人脈を活かした取材網を誇り活動を続けている。全米野球記者協会のメンバーとして20年目、同ロサンゼルス支部での長年の働きを評価され、歴史あるボブ・ハンター賞を受賞している。

item.title: [USA Today] ‘It’s like a movie:' Josue De Paula embraces spotlight in Los Angeles
item.dc:creator: Andrés Soto
item.description: ‘It’s like a movie:' Josue De Paula embraces spotlight in Los Angeles When the Los Angeles Dodgers were in Cincinnati on the second leg of their most recent road trip, manager Dave Roberts approached Josue De Paula. Sure enough, the raucous 48,000 fans -- a light crowd by Dodger Stadium standards -- packed inside Chavez Ravine for his home debut on Friday, Sept. 18 surpassed whatever the rookie's expectations
item.content:encoded:
‘It’s like a movie:' Josue De Paula embraces spotlight in Los Angeles
When the Los Angeles Dodgers were in Cincinnati on the second leg of their most recent road trip, manager Dave Roberts approached Josue De Paula.
"Just wait until we get back to LA," he recalled Roberts telling him. "It's different."
Sure enough, the raucous 48,000 fans -- a light crowd by Dodger Stadium standards -- packed inside Chavez Ravine for his home debut on Friday, Sept. 18 surpassed whatever the rookie's expectations were. Everything, from the environment to the deafening cheers that only seemed to grow louder as the Dodgers slugged their way to an 8-2 win over the hated rival San Francisco Giants, to the air itself, felt different.
"It's like a movie, man," De Paula told USA TODAY Sports.
De Paula, 21, has played his role perfectly through his first week in the big leagues.
The No. 6 prospect in baseball carries himself with a confidence that's rarely seen in someone as young as him. He's played in only eight games since being called up straight from Double-A Tulsa after Shohei Ohtani was placed on the injured list, or "just thrown into it" as he put it, but De Paula has relied on the skillset that got him here. He controls the strike zone, seeing the ball extremely well and is selective with what pitches he swings at, rarely chasing. That part of his game has transitioned seamlessly.
When De Paula does see a pitch he likes, his calm demeanor at the plate helps him stay centered and keeps him from jumping out ahead of the ball.
"I feel the adrenaline, but I feel like I just know how to pinpoint it and focus it," he said. "I'm so locked in, but I know how to calm myself down."
And when he does make contact, it's loud. So is De Paula.
That was seen in the bottom of the sixth inning on Friday. De Paula walked up to "Ima Boss" by Meek Mill (his third different walk-up song of the night by the way, this one was chosen by his mom). The triumphant horns on the 2011 anthem produced by Jahlil Beats had barely subsided over the loudspeakers when De Paula slapped a first-pitch slider from Giants reliever Jason Foley 107 mph into the gap in the right field for an RBI double that scored the go-ahead run from first.
Once he got to second base standing up, De Paula threw his hands in the air and hit the Dodgers' on-base celebration, swiveling his hips around before putting his own twist on it: pounding his chest and flexing toward his teammates in the dugout.
"He loves playing the game," Mookie Betts said. "He's full of life. When he gets on the field, it's like a quiet focus, but when he's off the field he likes joking ... and whatnot. He's a good kid."
Where does that unflappable joy come from?
"We got some swag in Brooklyn. We got some swag in the Dominican Republic. I just feel like I got a chip on my shoulder," De Paula said. "And it just comes out naturally."
That came out again in the bottom of the eighth when Giants reliever Philip Abner threw a first-pitch fastball up that was called a strike by umpire Louie Krupa. De Paula immediately tapped his helmet to challenge, and ABS showed the ball had missed the top of the zone 0.1 inches. The Dodger Stadium crowd got fired up as they watched the replay unfold on the jumbotron and the call was overturned to ball one, and De Paula nodded his head toward his teammates before working a two-out walk on four pitches.
Betts homered in the very next at-bat to break open a five-run lead. Will Smith then followed that up with the Dodgers' fourth long ball of the inning.
"Love De Paula," Roberts said. "I just love his at-bats. It's one of those things that we knew that coming up to the big leagues, he wasn't going to get overwhelmed, and it just helps when you control the strike zone. He takes his walks, when the ball is in the hitting zone, he can slug you, but he also knows how to get a base hit. It's been very professional."
De Paula finished his Dodger Stadium debut 2-for-3 with two runs, and RBI and a walk to bring his OPS up to .924. It's been a very small sample size, and baseball has a way of humbling even the most skilled hitters. It is, after all, a game of failure. But what he has been able to do in his first "trial run", filling in for the back-to-back National League MVP no less, might be indicative of something larger.
At the very least, he's played himself into the postseason roster conversation.
"To have (Roberts) believe in me so much," De Paula said. "I always have confidence in myself but to have someone like that believe in you, it just puts another oomph on your shoulder. It feels amazing."
For now, De Paula's just working. The weakest area of his game is his defense, and while the vast majority of this first stint in the majors will be as a designated hitter, he's using the opportunity get better. De Paula's taking advice from Roberts and the entire coaching staff. He's asking his teammates questions. He's shagging fly balls every day.
"I'm gonna shut a lot of people up with my defense very soon," he said. "It's gonna take some time."
That opportunity likely won't come for a while; Teoscar Hernández and Kyle Tucker are both getting hot and settling into their rhythms in the corner outfield spots in the final two weeks of the regular season. If De Paula does make the postseason roster after Ohtani comes back, it would probably be as a lefty bat off the bench.
Whatever happens over the next two weeks before October, De Paula's focused on the now, enjoying every moment he can. He got the ball back from his first Dodger Stadium hit – a leadoff single to right field in the fifth inning – and he knows exactly where to put it.
"I'm gonna give it to my parents," De Paula said. "I might give it to them right now."
If you purchase through our links, the USA Today Network may earn a commission. Prices were accurate at the time of publication but may change.

item.title: [MARCA] Ohtani ramps up hitting progression: Why Dave Roberts is bullish on star's October return
item.dc:creator: Adriano Boin
item.description: - Los Angeles Dodgers. Dodgers facing nightmare playoff decision over Edwin Díaz as October looms - Los Angeles Dodgers. “They basically lie”: Shohei Ohtani accused of hiding multiple injuries to avoid being placed on Dodgers' injured list Shohei Ohtani’s path back to the Los Angeles Dodgers lineup is becoming clearer, and manager Dave Roberts has provided another encouraging sign as the club prepares for October. Ohtani took coach-pitch batting practice Friday after beginning his hitting progre
item.content:encoded:
- Los Angeles Dodgers. Dodgers facing nightmare playoff decision over Edwin Díaz as October looms
- Los Angeles Dodgers. “They basically lie”: Shohei Ohtani accused of hiding multiple injuries to avoid being placed on Dodgers' injured list
Shohei Ohtani’s path back to the Los Angeles Dodgers lineup is becoming clearer, and manager Dave Roberts has provided another encouraging sign as the club prepares for October.
Ohtani took coach-pitch batting practice Friday after beginning his hitting progression with tee work earlier in the week. The Dodgers’ four-time MVP remains on the 15-day injured list with left-knee and right-biceps issues, but his recent activity has given the club reason for optimism.
Roberts said Ohtani came through the latest workout well and described the past several days as productive. However, the manager stressed that the slugger hasn’t yet advanced to live batting practice or work with the Trajekt pitching simulator.
“He came out of it well,” Roberts said. “I think for me, I'm just really waiting to hear when he's going to get on the field, let alone take live BP or Trajekt.
“And he's not there yet. But everything I've heard, it's been a really productive last three to four to five days. He's in a good spot.”
Before Ohtani returns to game action, Roberts wants him to face roughly 10 to 12 at-bats against pitching.
That timetable matters. Ohtani’s IL stint was backdated to Sept. 8, making Sept. 23 the earliest activation date. If he’s ready by then, he’ll have only five regular-season games to regain his timing before the postseason begins.
Dodgers’ offense keeps rolling without Ohtani
The Dodgers have managed his absence effectively, winning six of nine games and averaging 5.3 runs per contest during that stretch. Their latest victory showed just how much offensive depth remains available while Ohtani recovers.
Los Angeles defeated the San Francisco Giants 8-2 on Friday, with Mookie Betts homering twice and the Dodgers launching four home runs in the eighth inning.
Max Muncy and Kyle Tucker went back-to-back before Betts and Will Smith followed with consecutive blasts. Tyler Glasnow also delivered six innings with 10 strikeouts.
The performance underscored why the Dodgers can afford to be patient with Ohtani rather than rushing his return. Still, his presence would add another major dimension to a lineup already producing at a high level.
Before landing on the injured list, Ohtani hit .296 with 26 home runs and a .952 OPS across 110 games. He struggled over his final 24 games, batting .198 with a .690 OPS and 34 strikeouts, making the decision to pause his workload especially significant.
Ohtani’s return date remains unconfirmed, but the progression from tee work to coach-pitch batting practice represents another step forward.
With Los Angeles already having secured the NL West, the priority is getting its superstar healthy and ready to contribute when the games carry their greatest postseason significance.

item.title: [True Blue LA] The growing Dodgers 10-strikeout club
item.dc:creator: Eric Stephen
item.description: Tyler Glasnow on Friday night struck out 10 Giants in his six innings, his most in a start this season. Aside from securing Los Angeles-area folks a free Jumbo Jack with a purchase of a large drink for the 130th time this season and the 27th time in the last 28 days, Friday affirmed the Dodgers’ unique spot in double-digit strikeout games this season. The Dodgers now have a dozen individual 10-strikeout games this season. That’s not the most, it’s tied for fourth-most with the Toronto Blue Jays,
item.content:encoded:
Tyler Glasnow on Friday night struck out 10 Giants in his six innings, his most in a start this season. Aside from securing Los Angeles-area folks a free Jumbo Jack with a purchase of a large drink for the 130th time this season and the 27th time in the last 28 days, Friday affirmed the Dodgers’ unique spot in double-digit strikeout games this season.
The Dodgers now have a dozen individual 10-strikeout games this season. That’s not the most, it’s tied for fourth-most with the Toronto Blue Jays, behind the Milwaukee Brewers (16), Cleveland Guardians (15), and Philadelphia Phillies (14).
But what makes the Dodgers unique this season is that eight different pitchers have achieved double-digit strikeouts in a game:
- Yoshinobu Yamamoto (May 31, July 4, September 9)
- Emmet Sheehan (April 24, September 7)
- Blake Snell (August 11, August 29)
- Shohei Ohtani (April 15)
- Roki Sasaki (June 5)
- Justin Wrobleski (June 30)
- Tarik Skubal (August 22)
- Tyler Glasnow (September 18)
The next-closest team is the Minnesota Twins, with five different pitchers striking out at least 10 in a game this season. The Houston Astros, Brewers, New York Yankees, Pittsburgh Pirates, Texas Rangers, and Seattle Mariners have four pitchers each.
The Dodgers have eight different pitchers, which is at least one measure of their depth.
Eight pitchers with 10 strikeouts is the most the Dodgers have ever had in a season, two more than in 2022.
Saturday game info
- Teams: Dodgers vs. Giants
- Ballpark: Dodger Stadium
- Start time: 6:10 p.m.
- TV: SportsNet LA, MLB Network (out of market)
- Radio: AM 570 (English), KTNQ 1020 AM (Spanish)

item.title: [Sports Illustrated] Dodgers Boss Sets Clear Return Timeline for Shohei Ohtani
item.dc:creator: Ricardo Sandoval; Unknown
item.description: Los Angeles Dodgers president of baseball operations Andrew Friedman is confident Shohei Ohtani will return before the regular season ends. Friedman told reporters this week that he expects the designated hitter to return before the postseason. “I expect him back in the regular season,” Friedman declared. As for how he's doing, Friedman provided a positive update on the superstar. “He’s doing well,” Friedman said. “He’s progressing well.” Ohtani is eligible to return from the 15-day injured list
item.content:encoded:
Los Angeles Dodgers president of baseball operations Andrew Friedman is confident Shohei Ohtani will return before the regular season ends.
Friedman told reporters this week that he expects the designated hitter to return before the postseason.
“I expect him back in the regular season,” Friedman declared.
As for how he's doing, Friedman provided a positive update on the superstar.
“He’s doing well,” Friedman said. “He’s progressing well.”
Ohtani is eligible to return from the 15-day injured list on Sept. 23.
That target date leaves Ohtani with only five games remaining until the end of the regular season, and he appears to be on the right track.
“There’s no pain. He’s doing everything he needs to do,” manager Dave Roberts said. “I still don’t know when [the] time to return to play is. But everything that I hear is really positive.”
The 32-year-old is currently sidelined with injuries to his knee, biceps and neck.
Ohtani will focus exclusively on hitting for the rest of the season and into the playoffs after he was shut down from pitching earlier this month, right before he was placed on the IL.
Ohtani was shut down from pitching on Sept. 7, over two months since making his final pitching appearance of the season.
The Dodgers initially placed him on an indefinite pause from pitching on July 19 while he continued to serve as a designated hitter. The hope was he'd be able to return as a pitcher late in the year and into October.
Ohtani was stellar on the mound this season. In 14 appearances, the right-hander went 8-2 with a 1.79 ERA, 95 strikeouts and a 0.95 WHIP in 85.2 innings.
In three seasons as a Dodger, Ohtani has appeared on the mound only 28 times in the regular season.
Shohei Ohtani’s Bat Has Gone Cold Since August
Ohtani's performance was admirable for a few weeks, but since the start of August, his play has declined significantly.
From Aug. 1 until he was placed on the 15-day IL, Ohtani has a .231 batting average with 27 hits, six home runs, 13 RBIs and 19 runs.
Those numbers are far below what Ohtani usually produces at the plate.
Ohtani won't have much time to ramp up for the postseason. It's unlikely the four-time MVP will be back to 100% before October rolls around, but the team is hoping to get anything out of him in the playoffs.
Sign up for our free newsletter and follow us on X/Twitter and Facebook for the latest news.
Ricardo Sandoval is a freelance writer with On SI. He is a graduate of California State University, Northridge, and specializes in sports writing, particularly in MLB, NBA and NFL. He previously served as an Associate Editor for Dodgers Nation and has worked with Newsweek and The Sporting News.

item.title: [Dodgers Way] Edgardo Henriquez avoids the worst, but Dodgers still making promises they can’t keep
item.dc:creator: Evan Roberts
item.description: The Los Angeles Dodgers are constantly hoping for the best for their injured players, despite some signs that they might not be themselves come October. The National League West champions currently have back-to-back NL MVP Shohei Ohtani on the injured list, and Dave Roberts recently said that "he's feeling normal...ish" after reporting they are hoping to activate him when first eligible. Former Cy Young Award-winner Blake Snell also is dealing with an injury, and the Dodgers are hoping for the b
item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers are constantly hoping for the best for their injured players, despite some signs that they might not be themselves come October.
The National League West champions currently have back-to-back NL MVP Shohei Ohtani on the injured list, and Dave Roberts recently said that "he's feeling normal...ish" after reporting they are hoping to activate him when first eligible.
Former Cy Young Award-winner Blake Snell also is dealing with an injury, and the Dodgers are hoping for the best with him as well. First baseman Freddie Freeman is working through a knee injury that caused him to experience a major dip in production.
Freeman has looked more like himself in recent days, but the larger concern is the myriad contributors who are working their way back from injuries right before the playoffs. Dodgers fans should add the team's best reliever to that group of players that LA's coaching staff swears will be fine.
Edgardo Henriquez avoids the worst, but Dodgers still making promises they can’t keep
Edgardo Henriquez landed on the injured list last week with a low-grade back strain — the Dodgers correspondingly promoted Bobby Miller to the active roster — and it was reported that LA's right-hander has no structural damage. Unsurprisingly, the Dodgers still think he'll be back before the season ends!
Whether he could or he should, there is simply no way of knowing what the best path forward is for Henriquez and the Dodgers. Los Angeles needs him sharp and healthy once the calendar flips to October, but it seems that bringing him back before the playoffs will sacrifice one of those things.
Henriquez has been one of the best relievers in baseball this season, hands-down. He is one of 67 pitchers with 60-plus appearances this season -- of that group, Henriquez ranks 10th in FIP (2.52), fifth in batting average against (.177), second in slugging percentage (.239), fourth in OPS (.523), and is tied for first in home runs allowed (one).
While most fans assumed that Edwin Diaz and Tanner Scott would be the Dodgers most reliable relievers, the stats show that Henriquez and Alex Vesia have been far steadier coming out of the bullpen.

item.content:encoded:
Mookie Betts struggled through the first 2 1/2 months of this season for the Los Angeles Dodgers, and his batting average was below .200 on June 13.
But three months later, Betts is in top form as the Dodgers host the San Francisco Giants on Saturday night in the middle contest of a three-game series.
Betts went 3-for-4 with two homers and three RBIs in Friday's 8-2 victory to continue a torrid September in which he is batting .356 (21-for-59) with six homers and 18 RBIs in 15 games. The homers and RBIs are the most Betts has produced in any month this season.
Betts led off Friday's game with a homer and added a second blast in the eighth, when the Dodgers hit four home runs in the inning. Betts noted that he's batting leadoff solely because Shohei Ohtani (left knee swelling, right biceps inflammation) is on the 15-day injured list.
"Going up there is fun," Betts said of batting first. "It feels like home."
Betts has back-to-back three-hit games and is batting .254 for the season, with 22 homers and 65 RBIs.
The Dodgers led by just one run entering the bottom of the eighth on Friday before they put on a power show against Giants left-hander Philip Abner.
Max Muncy and Kyle Tucker hit back-to-back homers to start the frame. Two outs later, Betts hit a two-run blast and Will Smith followed with a solo shot.
Rookie Josue De Paula delivered the go-ahead double in the sixth and had two hits and scored twice as the Dodgers prevailed for the 12th time in the past 15 games.
"I just like to feel in control of it like I'm the man in the box and I control the moment," De Paula said of his approach.
Playoff-bound Los Angeles (94-60) trails the Milwaukee Brewers by two games in the battle for the National League's best record.
San Francisco (64-90) has lost five of its last seven games and is missing the playoffs for the fifth straight season and ninth time in the last 10. Management said earlier this week that manager Tony Vitello will return for a second season.
The Giants will use right-hander Yunior Marte (0-0, 2.45 ERA) as their starter on Saturday after ace right-hander Logan Webb (blister on right middle finger) was placed on the 15-day injured list.
Webb was an All-Star for the third straight season but is just 8-9 with a 4.31 ERA in 27 starts.
"It's been a weird season," he said before Friday's game. "It's been very up and down. I think as a team in general, but for myself, especially. It's been either really good or really bad. There's been way too many bad ones."
Marte, 23, will be making his fourth appearance and second start for San Francisco. In his last outing, he pitched five innings of scoreless relief in a loss to the San Diego Padres on Sept. 11.
Left-hander Tarik Skubal (10-7, 2.70) will start for Los Angeles on Saturday. He will make his ninth start for the Dodgers since being acquired from the Detroit Tigers at the trade deadline last month.
Skubal is 3-2 with a 2.52 ERA in 50 innings with Los Angeles. He has 57 strikeouts against 11 walks.
Skubal, 29, is slated to become a free agent following the season but continues to fit in with the Dodgers.
After Los Angeles clinched the National League West title on Thursday, Skubal and fellow lefty Blake Snell were celebrating when Skubal said: "It's going to be special. It's gonna be the first of many."
Skubal stood out in his last two outings, both victories over the Cincinnati Reds. He gave up two runs and seven hits over 14 1/3 innings, with the more recent outing coming Monday in a 4-1 win.
Skubal is 1-1 with a 2.79 ERA in two career starts against the Giants.

item.title: [bolavip.com] Dodgers’ Dave Roberts remains cautious but hopeful about Shohei Ohtani’s recovery
item.dc:creator: Matías Persuh
item.description: Shohei Ohtani is still recovering from the injuries that have kept him off the field in recent weeks. Dave Roberts hopes to have his star player back as the Los Angeles Dodgers look to complete the long-awaited three-peat. “He came out of it well,” Roberts said after Ohtani hit coach-pitch batting practice on Friday. “I think for me, I’m just really waiting to hear when he’s going to get on the field, let alone take live BP or Trajekt. And he’s not there yet. But everything I’ve heard, it’s been
item.content:encoded:
Shohei Ohtani is still recovering from the injuries that have kept him off the field in recent weeks. Dave Roberts hopes to have his star player back as the Los Angeles Dodgers look to complete the long-awaited three-peat.
“He came out of it well,” Roberts said after Ohtani hit coach-pitch batting practice on Friday. “I think for me, I’m just really waiting to hear when he’s going to get on the field, let alone take live BP or Trajekt. And he’s not there yet. But everything I’ve heard, it’s been a really productive last three to four to five days. He’s in a good spot.”
Days ago, the Dodgers clinched their spot in the postseason, and now all eyes are on making another trip to the World Series. For this team, having Ohtani available by then could be crucial.
Ohtani wants to return at 100%
Dodgers fans held their breath when Shohei Ohtani hit the 15-day injured list earlier this September after dealing with a pesky combination of right biceps inflammation and knee soreness. The two-way superstar officially went on the shelf on September 10 (backdated to September 8) after lingering discomfort kept him out of multiple lineups.
Shohei Ohtani #17 of the Los Angeles Dodgers in the dugout.
Fortunately, it looks like a short-term hit rather than a long-term disaster—Ohtani is eligible to return as early as September 23 for the final stretch of the regular season, though he’s putting his pitching program on pause to focus purely on bringing his massive bat back to the DH spot for October.
Dodgers’ final stretch
Before stepping into the October pressure cooker, the Dodgers are closing out the regular season with an all-NL West gauntlet that will test their postseason readiness. They wrap up their current home series against the San Francisco Giants at Dodger Stadium on September 19 and 20, before staying put in Los Angeles to host a high-stakes three-game clash against the San Diego Padres from September 22 to 24.
Finally, Chavez Ravine gets a breather as LA travels up north to Oracle Park for one last three-game rivalry rematch against the Giants from September 25 to 27. It’s a pure divisional stretch run to fine-tune the roster and tune up the bats before the real drama begins.

item.content:encoded:
Dodgers news: LA fans will love Dave Roberts' latest Shohei Ohtani update appeared first on ClutchPoints. Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here.
Shohei Ohtani continues progressing toward a possible regular-season return for the Los Angeles Dodgers after taking coach-pitch batting practice Friday.
Ohtani remains on the 15-day injured list with left-knee and right-biceps issues. He had already resumed tee work earlier in the week.
MLB.com's Sarah Wexler reported manager Dave Roberts' encouraging update on the two-way superstar's recovery as the Dodgers prepare for the postseason.
Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)
"He came out of it well," Roberts said. "I think for me, I'm just really waiting to hear when he's going to get on the field, let alone take live BP or Trajekt. And he's not there yet. But everything I've heard, it's been a really productive last three to four to five days. He's in a good spot."
Ohtani rejoined the Dodgers on Friday after remaining in Los Angeles for treatment during the team's seven-game road trip. He missed Thursday's NL West-clinching win vs. the Cincinnati Reds while continuing his rehabilitation.
The Dodgers star has not yet advanced to live batting practice or Trajekt work, and Roberts said he wants him to receive roughly 10 to 12 at-bats against pitching before returning to the lineup.
Los Angeles placed Ohtani on the injured list retroactive to September 8, making Wednesday the earliest possible activation date. If he returns then, the four-time MLB MVP would have no more than five regular-season games to regain his timing at the plate and rebuild game rhythm before the Dodgers begin their postseason run.
Ohtani is building back exclusively as a hitter and is not expected to pitch again this season after making his last mound appearance July 3. He hit .296 with 26 home runs and a .952 OPS through 110 games before hitting .198 with a .690 OPS and 34 strikeouts over his next 24 games.
The Dodgers have gone 6-3 without him, averaging about 5.3 runs per game. His progress remains encouraging, but the club has yet to announce a firm return date.
Related: Dodgers' 4 home run inning vs. Giants reminds fans of World Series ceiling

item.title: [DodgerBlue.com] Mookie Betts shares his hope for Dodgers mindset to finish the season
item.dc:creator: Blake Williams
item.description: The Los Angeles Dodgers have been on a hot streak in September, and it starts with their offense getting back on track after an awful month of August. Their lineup breaking out has coincided with Teoscar Hernandez, Kyle Tucker and Mookie Betts starting to produce at expected levels, and the return of Will Smith from the injured list. However, it has come without Shohei Ohtani as he’s currently on the 15-day injured list, and Freddie Freeman has been in a major slump due to right knee tendinitis.
item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers have been on a hot streak in September, and it starts with their offense getting back on track after an awful month of August.
Their lineup breaking out has coincided with Teoscar Hernandez, Kyle Tucker and Mookie Betts starting to produce at expected levels, and the return of Will Smith from the injured list. However, it has come without Shohei Ohtani as he’s currently on the 15-day injured list, and Freddie Freeman has been in a major slump due to right knee tendinitis.
Even without two of their biggest bats producing, the Dodgers have answered a lot of questions about their offense. They have taken better at-bats, they’re hitting the ball harder, and there is an increased focus and intensity with each pitch.
But with little left to play for after clinching the National League West and currently in a great spot to lock up the number two seed, that could lead to the Dodgers taking their foot off the gas in their final few games.
“We’re just playing good ball right now,” Betts said. “Just got to keep playing good ball and keep going through the end of the season. We don’t want any letups; we don’t want to try turning anything on once the postseason starts. We just want to play good ball and we want that to be our identity.”
The Dodgers are also starting to get healthy at the right time, which further boosts their confidence heading into October.
Andy Pages and Ohtani are both on the verge of returning, and Roki Sasaki should re-join the pitching staff soon as well. In addition, the Dodgers remain optimistic that Edgardo Henriquez will be back for the playoffs.
“It’s been good. We just have to keep playing,” Betts said. “Get guys to come back, like (Edwin) Díaz tonight. Get a couple more guys back and we should be ready to roll.”
What Mookie Betts thinks of Dodgers lineup
With nearly everyone in the lineup hitting well right now, Betts has seen both a positive and a negative effect from it. Betts described it as taking pressure off because you can trust the players behind you, but you’re also coming up to bat in RBI situations and big moments far more often because of the success of the hitters in front of you.
“It’s easier, but it’s also tough,” Betts began. “Because there’s constantly guys on base, so the constant need for that hit. But I think that’s the beauty in it. We just keep giving ourselves opportunities, and eventually something will crack like it did tonight.
“We just have to keep getting guys on base and giving ourselves a chance. The hits will fall.”

item.title: [Dodgers Nation] Josue De Paula Is Giving Dodgers Another Corey Seager-Type Decision
item.dc:creator: Nelson Espinal
item.description: Los Angeles Dodgers rookie Josue De Paula has shown a plate approach and swing that have translated directly to the big leagues. item.content:encoded:
Los Angeles Dodgers rookie Josue De Paula has shown a plate approach and swing that have translated directly to the big leagues. He has cemented himself as a postseason-caliber player.
In his Dodger Stadium debut on September 19th against the San Francisco Giants, De Paula went 2-for-3 with a double, an RBI, and a walk.
It was electric, and hitting in the No. 9 spot, he got on base and scored twice.
Since getting called up, De Paula is hitting .238/.448/.476 in eight games, with eight walks and two strikeouts. His OPS is .924, and while the sample size is limited, the results grow more undeniable game after game.
His production isn’t coming from something high-variance like a high batting average on batted balls; rather, he is delivering through a calculated plate approach, taking walks and never pressing the issue through his 29 plate appearances.
The problem with adding De Paula to the playoff roster
De Paula is “potentially” an option for the postseason roster, according to manager Dave Roberts.
For him to play in October, the team has to jump through hoops. The Dodgers would need to file an exemption with the Commissioner’s Office to add him to the postseason roster.
De Paula was not on the 40-man roster by September 1st, making him technically ineligible unless the Dodgers get the exemption.
They would need a player on the injured list as the reason, making outfielder Andy Pages and catcher Dalton Rushing the two possible postseason casualties.
Given Pages’ status on the team, there is no chance he does not get the nod. Rushing, meanwhile, is trying to swing the bat despite elbow irritation, though he is still a ways from returning.
Something worth noting: Andrew Friedman has a history of letting a hot prospect ride in the postseason.
The Corey Seager Parallel
Seager, at 21, the same age as De Paula, got a call-up on September 3rd, 2015, and he was a sensation from the outset.
He played 27 games and was one of baseball’s best hitters for about a month. Seager slashed .337/.425/.561 with 14 walks, 19 strikeouts, four home runs, and 17 RBIs.
His play earned him a postseason roster spot, where he started. He struggled, hitting .188/.250/.485 with eight strikeouts and 1 walk.
That year, the Dodgers were bounced out by the New York Mets in a five-game thriller. Seager played in all five games.
While Seager struggled, there are reasons to believe that De Paula thrived. He has better discipline and chases less than the young shortstop.
Additionally, De Paula has much more talent and experience around him than Seager did.
With Shohei Ohtani returning, DePaula would be a pinch hitter who is tasked with getting on base. DePaula has success against both left- and right-handed pitching, so that he can be a versatile bat off the bench.
If he keeps performing as he has, Friedman will have another clear decision on his hands — give the young guy a chance to show what he can do.

item.title: [New York Post] Dodgers figuring out how to score runs without Shohei Ohtani
item.dc:creator: Dylan Hernandez
item.description: Super Mario ran into a mushroom. Popeye devoured a can of spinach. The Dodgers are scoring runs in bunches again. Say what you want to say about the quality of opposition or small sample size, but the numbers are the numbers. Ninety-seven runs in their first 17 games of September. Nineteen home runs in their last nine games, including five in their 8-2 win over the Giants on Friday night.
