item.content:encoded:
Super Mario ran into a mushroom. Popeye devoured a can of spinach.
The Dodgers are scoring runs in bunches again.
Say what you want to say about the quality of opposition or small sample size, but the numbers are the numbers.
Ninety-seven runs in their first 17 games of September.
Nineteen home runs in their last nine games, including five in their 8-2 win over the Giants on Friday night.
With a little more than a week remaining in the regular season, the Dodgers are finally starting to resemble the team they were expected to be.
Even without Shohei Ohtani.
The Dodgers doing this with Ohtani on the 15-day injured list is the most promising aspect of their recent offensive resurgence.
Because they will likely have to do something like this to give themselves a chance to complete their three-peat.
Manager Dave Roberts reported Ohtani was “in a good spot” as a result of “a really productive last three to four to five days,” but the reality is that the Dodgers have no credibility on this subject whatsoever.
Remember when general manager Brandon Gomes said earlier this month that Ohtani might pitch again this season? Or when Gomes said “nothing has indicated” Ohtani would have to be placed on the IL the day after a game in which he was shaking his arm and looking as if he was hitting on one leg?
Knowing Ohtani, he will be in the Dodgers’ lineup when the playoffs start, but his presence will be more a reflection of his willpower than of his health. The Dodgers can’t count on him to produce, at least not with any consistency.
Which is why it was important that Mookie Betts homered twice on Friday night.
Or that Max Muncy, Kyle Tucker and Will Smith also went deep.
Or that Ohtani’s replacement at designated hitter, 21-year-old rookie Josue De Paula, scored the run that tied the game in the fifth inning and doubled in the go-ahead run in the sixth.
“It’s a high-floor talent level,” Roberts said. “I just like the way we’re taking better team at-bats and making up for not having Shohei in there.”
The Dodgers have scored an average of 5.71 runs per game this month, an improvement from their average of 4.89 through Aug. 31.
They are doing what Betts previously called on them to do, to build momentum in September that can be taken into October.
“We just gotta keep playing good ball and want to keep going through the end of the season,” Betts said. “We don’t want any letups. We don’t want to try and turn anything on once the postseason starts. We just want to play good ball, and we want that to be our identity.”
Betts has played a major role in that, batting .333 with seven home runs and 23 RBIs over his last 25 games.
He isn’t the only player on a hot streak.
Tucker is batting .438 with five homers and 11 RBIs in his last nine games. Teoscar Hernandez is hitting .362 with three homers, three doubles and a triple this month.
De Paula has shown advanced plate discipline, as he’s registered an on-base percentage of .448 in his first eight major league games. He’s walked eight times in 29 plate appearances and struck out only twice.
“Nothing too different, to be honest,” De Paula said when asked to compare the major leagues to Double- A.
He continued, “I always felt like I was a good hitter. I know these pitchers know how to execute a little bit better and stuff, but I know I’m up for the challenge.”
Roberts said De Paula has played his way into consideration for a spot on the playoff roster. What Roberts didn’t say was that De Paula could be an insurance policy at DH in case Ohtani’s body doesn’t hold up over the postseason.
Roberts has insisted that when Ohtani returns, he will be slotted right back into the leadoff spot, but Betts could give the manager something to think about.
Twice in the last week, Roberts batted Betts at the top of the lineup, and Betts was a combined 5-for-8 in those games.
Of hitting first, Betts said, “It’s fun and kind of feels home. But there’s a guy named Shohei that needs to be up there to get us going.”
Roberts also made no effort to downplay Ohtani’s importance.
“Obviously, we’re a better team with him,” Roberts said. “But it is nice to see that there hasn’t been a drop-off with him not in the lineup.”
The Dodgers can’t expect Ohtani to shoulder as much of the offensive burden as he did last year in the playoffs, when he was responsible for eight of their 24 home runs.
When the team wasn’t hitting in July or August, that would have sounded like a death sentence. Now, a more balanced offense sounds like a possibility — or at least more possible than it was earlier in the season.

item.dc:creator: Miracle Dimwesh

Manager Dave Roberts said Ohtani took a full round of batting practice from a coach during the Dodgers' series against the San Francisco Giants. The next major step will be facing live pitching as the team continues to monitor his recovery. Ohtani has been sidelined since the Dodgers placed him on the 15-day injured list with right biceps inflammation and left knee swelling. Dave Roberts said Shohei Ohtani con
item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers are getting closer to having Shohei Ohtani back in the lineup.
Manager Dave Roberts said Ohtani took a full round of batting practice from a coach during the Dodgers' series against the San Francisco Giants. The next major step will be facing live pitching as the team continues to monitor his recovery.
Ohtani has been sidelined since the Dodgers placed him on the 15-day injured list with right biceps inflammation and left knee swelling.
Dave Roberts said Shohei Ohtani continues to progress in the right direction taking BP from a coach in the cage today.
Live BP would be a greater sign he is close to returning. #Dodgers
The IL stint was backdated to Sept. 8, making Ohtani eligible to return on Sept. 23. For now, the Dodgers are keeping his work focused on hitting.
The team had already stopped his throwing program after an Aug. 28 bullpen session. Ohtani has since progressed through dry swings and tee work before taking batting practice from a coach.
A live batting-practice session will give the Dodgers another important checkpoint. It should also provide a better indication of whether his knee can handle the movement involved in hitting against actual pitching.
Ohtani has been one of Los Angeles' most productive hitters when healthy. He is batting .277 with 25 doubles, four triples, 30 home runs, 80 RBI and 89 runs in 130 games.
He also owns a .380 on-base percentage and .522 slugging percentage while going 11-for-14 on stolen-base attempts.
Ohtani's abbreviated pitching work has been just as impressive. He is 8-2 with a 1.79 ERA, 95 strikeouts and a .180 opponent batting average across 14 starts and 85.2 innings.
The Dodgers have already clinched the NL West, giving them some flexibility with Ohtani's return. The priority now is getting him enough hitting work without creating another setback.
Los Angeles entered Saturday at 94-60 with eight regular-season games remaining. Ohtani's progression will remain one of the team's biggest storylines as the Dodgers prepare for October.

item.title: [El Nacional — La voz de todos] Josué De Paula, tres canciones de entrada y un gran doble marcan su memorable debut en el Dodger Stadium
item.source: El Nacional — La voz de todos
item.dc:creator: Agencia AP
item.description: Grandes Ligas Josué De Paula, tres canciones de entrada y un gran doble marcan su memorable debut en el Dodger Stadium En ocho partidos, el joven dominicano de 21 años suma cinco hits —el primero fue un jonrón de tres carreras contra Eury Pérez de los Marlins—, cinco carreras impulsadas y cuatro anotadas LOS ÁNGELES.— Josué De Paula dio mucho de qué hablar durante su primera semana en las Grandes Ligas con los Dodgers de Los Ángeles, y eso sin contar el uso de tres canciones de entrada en el mis
item.content:encoded:
Grandes Ligas
Josué De Paula, tres canciones de entrada y un gran doble marcan su memorable debut en el Dodger Stadium
En ocho partidos, el joven dominicano de 21 años suma cinco hits —el primero fue un jonrón de tres carreras contra Eury Pérez de los Marlins—, cinco carreras impulsadas y cuatro anotadas
LOS ÁNGELES.— Josué De Paula dio mucho de qué hablar durante su primera semana en las Grandes Ligas con los Dodgers de Los Ángeles, y eso sin contar el uso de tres canciones de entrada en el mismo partido.
“Fue increíble”, dijo, mostrando una sonrisa deslumbrante.
En su debut en el Dodger Stadium el viernes por la noche, De Paula, que bateó en novena posición como bateador designado, conectó dos hits en tres turnos al bate, anotando dos carreras y produciendo una carrera impulsada. En la victoria por 8-2 sobre los Gigantes de San Francisco, el equipo contrario.
“Tengo muchísima confianza en mí mismo y en mis capacidades”, dijo, “así que sé que cuando llegue el momento, voy a estar a la altura”.
De Paula debutó en las Grandes Ligas el viernes pasado en Miami. En ocho partidos, el joven de 21 años suma cinco hits —el primero fue un jonrón de tres carreras contra Eury Pérez de los Marlins—, cinco carreras impulsadas y cuatro anotadas. Ha recibido ocho bases por bolas y se ha ponchado solo dos veces. Su promedio de bateo es de .238 con un OPS de .924.
“Sabíamos que al llegar a las Grandes Ligas no se iba a sentir abrumado”, dijo el mánager Dave Roberts.
De Paula fue convocado después de que Shohei Ohtani, cuatro veces MVP, entrara en la lista de lesionados y se está ganando un puesto en la plantilla para la postemporada.
“Necesitamos a alguien que salga del banquillo. Él está entre los candidatos”, dijo Roberts. “Sin duda, está haciendo muchas cosas bien”.
De Paula nació y creció en Brooklyn, pero se mudó a la República Dominicana, país natal de su padre, cuando la pandemia de COVID-19 paralizó los deportes en Nueva York, para poder jugar béisbol durante todo el año. Vivió con sus tíos y se matriculó en una academia de béisbol.
Obtuvo la ciudadanía dominicana, lo que le permitió firmar con los Dodgers como agente libre internacional en 2022. Fue ascendido rápidamente a la Clase A al año siguiente, a los 18 años. En 2024, fue ascendido a la Clase A Avanzada.
El año pasado, representó a los Dodgers en el Juego de las Futuras Estrellas , donde conectó un jonrón de tres carreras y obtuvo el premio al Jugador Más Valioso.
De Paula es el primer jugador en ser ascendido directamente desde Doble-A durante los 12 años de Andrew Friedman como presidente de operaciones de béisbol. También es el primer jugador en la historia de los Dodgers en usar el número 95.
Extraoficialmente, podría ser el primer jugador del equipo en usar tres canciones diferentes de entrada al bate en el mismo partido. Como un guiño a sus raíces en Brooklyn —también el distrito neoyorquino donde se originaron los Dodgers— salió al plato en la segunda entrada con la canción "Notorious" de The Notorious BIG, otro nativo de Brooklyn.
“No esperaba que los aficionados me apoyaran tanto, ¡fueron increíbles!”, dijo.
De Paula abrió la quinta entrada con la canción "Ima a Boss" del rapero Meek Mill, en homenaje a su padre, y rápidamente conectó un sencillo para su primer hit en casa. Recibió la pelota y planeaba regalarle el recuerdo a sus padres. Su tercera canción de entrada fue para su madre.
Su doblete con dos outs en la sexta entrada rompió el empate a 2.
“Me encantan sus turnos al bate”, dijo Roberts. “Aprovecha las bases por bolas. Cuando la pelota está en la zona de bateo, puede conectar un jonrón, pero también sabe cómo conseguir un sencillo. Ha sido muy profesional”.
De Paula incluso ganó su desafío utilizando el sistema automatizado de lanzamiento y strike durante un turno al bate.
“Siento la adrenalina, pero creo que sé cómo controlarla y enfocarla”, dijo. “Estoy totalmente concentrado, pero sé cómo tranquilizarme”.
De Paula demuestra un swing sólido y un buen instinto para seleccionar los lanzamientos. En defensa, sabe que necesita mejorar en los jardines.
“Muy pronto voy a callar a mucha gente que se está defendiendo”, dijo.
De Paula ya ha impresionado a su compañero de equipo en los Dodgers y ex Jugador Más Valioso de la Liga Americana, Mookie Betts, quien dijo que era "realmente genial" ver a un jugador joven que puede enfrentarse a cualquier lanzador contrario.
“Le encanta jugar”, dijo Betts. “Cuando está en el campo, se concentra en silencio, pero fuera del campo le gusta bromear y reír. Es un buen chico”.

item.content:encoded:
With just over one week left in the regular season, the Los Angeles Dodgers are still looking to secure the No. 2 seed in the National League postseason bracket and perhaps more importantly, get to a better state of health.
Edwin Díaz returned from the injured list on Friday, but the Dodgers are still waiting on the likes of Andy Pages, Dalton Rushing, Roki Sasaki and Shohei Ohtani. Fortunately for L.A., there is optimism with that group, and Blake Snell as well after he came out his most recent start due to left groin tightness.
Dodgers updates
Blake Snell
Snell played catch from flat ground on Friday, getting out to 90 feet as signs point to avoiding the 15-day injured list.
“I’m very hopeful that he’ll make a start before the end of the season,” Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said.
Snell has a history of missing roughly one month because of adductor/groin strains, but he and the team believe the latest issue did not advance to being that significant.
“Don’t know the answer exactly,” Roberts said when asked what may have caused the tightness, “but happy that we caught it early.”
If — or when — Snell does pitch again, Roberts indicated it would be a normal start rather than an abbreviated final tuneup before the postseason begins.
Andy Pages
After previously sharing the expectation is for Pages to return during the homestand, Roberts offered a slightly more concrete timeline by saying that should come during the Dodgers’ series against the San Diego Padres.
Dalton Rushing
According to Fabian Ardaya of The Athletic, Rushing received a PRP injection in his right forearm.
Dalton Rushing got a PRP injection a week ago to address his flexor in his right arm. Still holding out hope he can be an option as a bat going forward — will hit off a machine in the coming days to test it out.
Surgery still doesn’t appear on the table yet.
— Fabian Ardaya (@FabianArdaya) September 18, 2026
Rushing had a brief return at the start of September after going on the 10-day injured list last month because of a slight tear in the UCL of his right elbow. The Dodgers have suggested a best-case scenario is to have Rushing available as a pinch-hit option off the bench in the playoffs.
Shohei Ohtani
Ohtani took swings against a coach pitching in the batting cage and “came out of it well,” per Roberts. Although the superstar talent is making progress, Roberts said more clarity won’t come until Ohtani faces live pitching or hits off the Trajekt machine.
“But everything I’ve heard, it’s been a really productive last three to four to five days. He’s in a good spot,” Roberts added.
Roki Sasaki
Roberts further confirmed Sasaki is nearing a return and will start despite the prior plan being to shift him into a bullpen role. Some of the change is due to the uncertainty that arose from Snell’s groin trouble.
However, Sasaki still figures to be utilized as a reliever in the postseason if the Dodgers rotation remains healthy.

item.title: [Los Angeles Times] Commentary: Dodgers have no choice. They must hope Tyler Glasnow can trust himself in the playoffs
item.dc:creator: Mirjam Swanson
item.description: - Click here to listen to this article - - The oft-injured Tyler Glasnow hasn’t had the greatest of seasons, but the Dodgers will need him to deliver in the playoffs if they want to win another World Series title. - Glasnow fought through early struggles to throw six innings and strike out 10 in an 8-2 win over the San Francisco Giants, but can he replicate that in the playoffs? - The veteran right-hander played a key role in the Dodgers’ 2025 World Series, and the team will need him to do
item.content:encoded:
- Click here to listen to this article
-
- The oft-injured Tyler Glasnow hasn’t had the greatest of seasons, but the Dodgers will need him to deliver in the playoffs if they want to win another World Series title.
- Glasnow fought through early struggles to throw six innings and strike out 10 in an 8-2 win over the San Francisco Giants, but can he replicate that in the playoffs?
- The veteran right-hander played a key role in the Dodgers’ 2025 World Series, and the team will need him to do the same this October.
The Dodgers are all in, going for a three-peat.
And they might not have an extra ace up their sleeve anymore, but when the postseason begins, they’ll still hope to play their quad of aces — four of a kind that will beat almost every other hand.
But do the Dodgers have four aces? Or three? Or just a pair, Yoshinobu Yamamoto and Tarik Skubal?
Could the left groin tightness that chased Blake Snell from his last start after an inning linger into the postseason? Snell isn’t the sturdiest of starters, having missed most of the season because of shoulder fatigue and loose bodies in his left elbow. But the Dodgers suggest he’s going to be OK; Snell is slated for one last regular-season start.
And what about Tyler Glasnow?
Tyler Glasnow gives up just three hits and strikes out 10, and Mookie Betts hits two home runs in the Dodgers’ 8-2 win over the San Francisco Giants.
Can the Dodgers trust the 6-foot-8 right-hander who missed three months because of back spasms?
Should they put their belief in the 11th-year pitcher who likely would be the odd man out in the postseason if Shohei Ohtani still were available to deal on the mound?
They’re going to have to trust Glasnow. And he’s going to have to trust himself.
“He’s a guy that you can’t put too much thought into him, or it starts getting in his own head,” said catcher Dalton Rushing, who is injured but enjoyed watching Glasnow find his footing in Friday’s 8-2 victory over the San Francisco Giants.
“It was a lot of fun to watch tonight,” Rushing said. “Looked like himself.”
After three suboptimal innings, Glasnow settled down in a trust-building exercise of an outing against the Giants and their triple A-caliber lineup.
He wasn’t the most efficient, the most pristine, the sharpest — but he was fit to throw 98 pitches and six innings.
To fight through after laboring with 59 pitches in the first three innings, to earn his second win since April and to help the Dodgers maintain their four-game buffer over the Atlanta Braves as they play to secure a first-round bye with eight games left.
There was no champagne hangover for Glasnow on Friday — he flew directly back to L.A. from Miami, skipping Thursday’s clubhouse party in Cincinnati, where the Dodgers celebrated clinching the National League West Division for the 13th time in 14 years — but how about a toast to good health?
Cheers to giving up just two runs, one each in the second and third innings. To walking only two batters and striking out 10. To giving up only three hard hits and producing 15 whiffs.
To feeling and pitching better.
“After that third inning, I just stopped trying to be quick,” Glasnow said. “Just go out and be athletic, and I think it started to feel a little bit more timed up.”
Glasnow came into Friday’s game — one of his final two regular-season starts — having given up eight runs on 11 hits and seven walks in his previous two starts, looking less than comfortable in both. Out of rhythm, out of sync.
“This is an important start, and he knows it,” manager Dave Roberts said before the game. “It’s certainly not do or die, but ... just to kind of get back feeling good.”
Afterward, Roberts wasn’t thrilled with how Glasnow started, but liked how he finished.
“You could see him fighting himself a little bit,” Roberts said. “The fastball command wasn’t great early. Got a lot of strikeouts. Curveball wasn’t sharp. But I thought he did a good job of making pitches when he needed to. The slider got better, fastball command got better as the game went on. Good to see him get through six innings.”
It’ll be better yet for the Dodgers’ odds if Glasnow can carry Friday’s progress into his next start — and then into the playoffs, where he proved himself as a Dodger last season after an elbow sprain sidelined him for the 2024 postseason.
The magic is indeed missing, and after two seasons of conjuring up postseason greatness, these back-to-reality Dodgers appear headed for an early fall.
In the Dodgers’ 2025 World Series run, Glasnow made six appearances, three of them starts. He had a 1.69 ERA and averaged 10.5 strikeouts per nine innings. The stuff of aces.
“Today was a step in the right direction,” said Glasnow, the formerHart High School star, before leaving the clubhouse in flip-flops. “I’d rather kind of feel it, work through some stuff, and have a good one right before playoffs.
“I think I’m in a good spot right now.”

item.content:encoded:
「肩が大木すぎ」大谷翔平じゃない…日本人の肉体に反響 ニヤリ笑顔「とってもハンサム」
MLB公式Xの投稿が話題
MLB公式X（旧ツイッター）が18日（日本時間19日）、突如として日本人メジャーリーガーの写真を投稿した。タンクトップ越しに伝わる肉体と笑顔にファンから熱い視線が注がれている。
筋肉の絵文字とともに「豪快なアーチを叩き込む準備ができているなら、笑顔を見せてくれ」と綴ってMLB公式Xが写真を公開したのは、練習中と思われるホワイトソックス・村上宗隆内野手だ。タンクトップ姿でバットを持ってカメラに笑顔を向けている。
日本人選手で、頻繁に肉体が話題となるのはドジャース・大谷翔平投手だ。トレーニング風景なども関心の的で、鍛え抜かれた肉体には日本ファン以外も注目している。そしてメジャー1年目から本塁打を量産している村上も、パワーを生み出す筋肉にファンの目が奪われたようだ。
MLB公式Xの投稿には「パワー」「ハンサムだ」「とってもハンサム」「腕というか肩が大木過ぎるwww」「メジャー顔になってるよね」などと反響が広がった。
村上はこの日のタイガース戦では4打数無安打1四球に終わり、2戦連発とはならなかった。チームもまさかの逆転負けを喫し、地区首位から後退している。

item.title: [bozemandailychronicle.com] Josue De Paula’s 3 walk-up songs and a big double mark his memorable Dodger Stadium debut
item.dc:creator: BETH HARRIS
item.description: LOS ANGELES (AP) — Josue De Paula made plenty of noise during his first week in the major leagues with the Los Angeles Dodgers, and that's not even counting his use of three walk-up songs in the same game. “It was awesome,” he said, flashing a dazzling smile. item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES (AP) — Josue De Paula made plenty of noise during his first week in the major leagues with the Los Angeles Dodgers, and that's not even counting his use of three walk-up songs in the same game.
“It was awesome,” he said, flashing a dazzling smile.
Batting ninth as the designated hitter, De Paula went 2 for 3 with two runs and an RBI in his Dodger Stadium debut Friday night, an 8-2 win over the San Francisco Giants.
"I have the utmost confidence in myself and belief,” he said, “so I know when the moment is up for it, I know I’m going to come through.”
De Paula debuted in the major leagues last Friday at Miami. In eight games, the 21-year-old has five hits — his first being a three-run homer off Eury Pérez of the Marlins — five RBIs and four runs. He’s drawn eight walks and struck out just twice. He’s hitting .238 with an OPS of .924.
“We knew that coming up to the big leagues he wasn’t going to get overwhelmed,” manager Dave Roberts said.
De Paula got called up after four-time MVP Shohei Ohtani went on the injured list and is playing his way into a shot at making the postseason roster.
“We need to have somebody coming off the bench. He’s in the mix,” Roberts said. “He’s certainly doing a lot of things well.”
De Paula was born and raised in Brooklyn, but relocated to his father's native Dominican Republic when the COVID-19 pandemic shut down sports in New York so he could play baseball year-round. He lived with his uncles and enrolled in a baseball academy.
He gained Dominican citizenship, which allowed him to sign with the Dodgers as an international free agent in 2022. He was quickly promoted to Class A the following year at age 18. In 2024, he was promoted to High-A.
Last year, he represented the Dodgers in the All-Star Futures Game, hitting a three-run homer and earning MVP honors.
De Paula is the first player to be called up directly from Double-A during Andrew Friedman's 12-year tenure as president of baseball operations. He's also the first player in Dodgers history to wear No. 95.
Unofficially, he may be the first player on the team to use three different walk-up songs in the same game. In a nod to his Brooklyn roots — also the New York borough where the Dodgers originated — he came to the plate in the second inning to “Notorious” by The Notorious B.I.G., another Brooklyn native.
“I didn’t expect the fans to be so supportive and they were awesome,” he said.
De Paula led off the fifth to “Ima a Boss” by rapper Meek Mill in a nod to his father and promptly singled for his first hit at home. He got the ball and planned to give the keepsake to his parents. His third walk-up song was for his mother.
His two-out double in the sixth snapped a 2-all tie.
“I just love his at-bats,” Roberts said. “He takes his walks. When the ball’s in the hitting zone, he can slug you — but he also knows how to get a base hit. It’s been very professional.”
De Paula even won his challenge using the Automated Ball-Strike system during one at-bat.
“I feel the adrenaline, but I just feel like I know how to pinpoint it and focus it,” he said. “I’m so locked in, but I know how to calm myself down.”
De Paula displays a solid swing and an instinct for good pitch selection. Defensively, he knows he needs some work in the outfield.
“I’m going to shut a lot of people up on my defense very soon,” he said.
De Paula has already impressed Dodgers teammate and former AL MVP Mookie Betts, who called it “really neat” to see a young player who can handle any opposing pitcher.
“He loves playing the game,” Betts said. “When he gets on the field, it’s like a quiet focus, but when he’s off the field, he likes joking and laughing. He’s a good kid.”

item.content:encoded:
シーズンを通して先発ローテーションを守り抜き、ドジャースのナ・リーグ地区優勝に貢献した山本由伸投手。鉄腕エースを巡り、米メディア『CLUTCH POINTS』は18日（日本時間19日）、「もっと注目されるべき」と訴えた。なぜ、過小評価されているのか。同メディアはその理由に言及した。
■「活躍が見過ごされている」
今季のドジャース先発投手陣は、ブレイク・スネル投手、タイラー・グラスノー投手が序盤から戦列を離れ、終盤を迎えて大谷翔平投手も負傷者リスト（IL）に入った。
エース格が不在となる中、ひとり先発ローテーションを守ったのが山本だった。今季27試合に先発登板し、14勝8敗。防御率2.51はメジャー全体5位、WHIP（1イニングあたりの被安打と与四球）は0.87で同2位、被打率.180は同3位につけている。
堂々たる成績だが、ナ・リーグのサイ・ヤング賞争いはジェイコブ・ミジオロウスキー投手（ブルワーズ）が先行。これにクリス・セール投手（ブレーブス）やクリストファー・サンチェス投手（フィリーズ）らの名前が続く。
この状況を歯がゆく感じているのが、『CLUTCH POINTS』のジョーイ・ミストレッタ記者。「ミジオロウスキーらの傑出したパフォーマンスにより、山本の活躍が見過ごされている」と指摘。その上で「過小評価されているとまでは言わないが、一番問題なのは（ロサンゼルスという）巨大市場を本拠地とするチームでプレーしているにもかかわらず、彼に向けられる注目が十分ではないということだ」と憤った。
■全体17位の奪三振数が影響か
同記者は注目度が高まらない理由について、「目を見張るような三振を奪っているわけではないからかもしれない」と推察。「山本はここまで178奪三振を記録しており、この時期としては立派な数字。しかし、リーグ全体では17位にとどまっている」と紹介した。
現在は最速104マイル（約167キロ）の剛速球を投げるミジオロウスキーが243奪三振でリーグトップに立ち、ブルージェイズのディラン・シース投手（236奪三振）、ガーディアンズのギャビン・ウィリアムズ投手（235奪三振）が全体の2、3位につけている。
同記者としては、山本が剛腕タイプではなく、制球力重視のスタイルであることが、成績に見合うだけの注目を得られない一因かもしれないと指摘した形だ。
また、同記者は「ドジャースには大谷をはじめ多くのスター選手が在籍しており、たとえ山本のような優秀な選手であっても見過ごされる傾向にある」とも主張した。
その上で、最後に「山本がサイ・ヤング賞を受賞することは難しいかもしれない。しかし、彼は現在受けている評価以上に注目されるべき存在であることは確かだ」と説いた。

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Edwin Díaz makes successful return, rookie Josue De Paula strong for Dodgers in win
item.dc:creator: Andrés Soto; USA TODAY
item.description: That's one way to start off the last homestand of the regular season. Forget the fact that it was against the lowly San Francisco Giants and their lineup featuring a who's who of ... "Who?" Forget the fact that five of the Los Angeles Dodgers' runs in their dominant 8-2 win on Friday night came off the relatively unknown Philip Abner. item.content:encoded:
That's one way to start off the last homestand of the regular season.
Forget the fact that it was against the lowly San Francisco Giants and their lineup featuring a who's who of ... "Who?" Forget the fact that five of the Los Angeles Dodgers' runs in their dominant 8-2 win on Friday night came off the relatively unknown Philip Abner. The Dodgers' lineup, without Shohei Ohtani, showed exactly what they're capable of offensively.
This is the version of the team Andrew Friedman envisioned when he signed Kyle Tucker to a four-year, $240 million contract and Edwin Díaz to a three-year, $69 million deal last winter.
"The talent," manager Dave Roberts said. "It's a high-floor talent level. I just like the way we're taking better team at-bats and making up for not having Shohei in there. Obviously, we're a better team with him, but it is nice to see there hasn't been a drop-off with him not in the lineup."
Here's a look at three winners from the Dodgers' victory over the Giants:
The Dodgers lineup is just fine
Mookie Betts started things off when he jumped on a low-90s fastball that San Francisco starter Cesar Perdomo left middle-middle and sent it over the fence in left center field for his 33rd leadoff home run as a Dodger. The bats went quiet briefly from there until the bottom of the fifth when Teoscar Hernández singled home Josue De Paula from third on a sharp liner to right field to tie the game at 2-2.
The rookie De Paula later drove in the go-ahead run on an RBI double in the sixth before a monster five-run eighth inning in which Max Muncy, Tucker, Betts and Will Smith all went yard to put the game out of reach.
"I think that's the beauty in it," Betts said. "We just keep giving ourselves opportunities and eventually, something will crack. It did tonight, so we just have to keep getting guys on base and giving ourselves the chances and the hits will follow."
Edwin Díaz looked good in return from IL
That set the stage for the trumpets to once again blare over the Dodger Stadium loudspeakers. Roberts said he wouldn't have put Díaz in if it wasn't for the six-run lead as he wanted to give Díaz some leeway in his first outing back from an IL stint after health and poor performance have plagued his season.
But Díaz took the opportunity and ran with it. In his first big league appearance since Aug. 17, he got two quick outs before giving up a base hit up the middle. Rather than let that snowball like it has many times in 2026, however, Díaz was able to buckle down and strike out Brett Harris on three pitches to seal a Dodgers win.
"I liked everything," Roberts said. "I liked his intensity; I liked the fastball velocity. The slider was good. It was just really good to get him back in the mix and that's something to build on."
Josue De Paula is different
The through line for the offense on Friday night was the 21-year-old De Paula. The No. 6 prospect in baseball according to MLB Pipeline finished the night 2-for-3 with a walk, two runs and an RBI, but it was the timing of each of those that made his Dodger Stadium debut so special.
De Paula led off the bottom of the fifth with a base hit, which Betts followed up with one of his own before he eventually scored the tying run on Hernández's RBI single. Two innings later, De Paula scored Tucker from first on a double that he put on a rope at 107 mph deep into the right field gap. As he reached second, De Paula pounded his chest and flexed.
Then, in that huge eighth inning, it was De Paula who kept it alive by working a four-pitch walk with two outs, his seventh in a week in the big leagues. Five pitches later, Betts blew the game open with a two-run homer.
"I just love his at-bats," Roberts said. "It's one of those things that we knew coming up to the big leagues, he wasn't going to get overwhelmed, and it just helps when you control the strike zone. He takes his walks, when the ball is in the hitting zone, he can slug you but he also knows how to get a base hit. It's been very professional."
This article originally appeared on USA TODAY: Edwin Díaz makes successful return, rookie Josue De Paula strong for Dodgers in win

item.title: [Los Angeles Times] Dodgers surge late to beat Giants as they work to get healthy for playoffs
item.dc:creator: Kevin Baxter
item.description: Dodgers surge late to beat Giants as they work to get healthy for playoffs - Click here to listen to this article - - Tyler Glasnow gives up three hits, two runs and strikes out 10 over six innings in the Dodgers’ 8-2 win over the San Francisco Giants. - The Dodgers hit four home runs in the eighth inning, including a pair of back-to-back homers. Mookie Betts finished with two home runs. With eight games left in the regular season, the Dodgers have already ticked off the most important box
item.content:encoded:
Dodgers surge late to beat Giants as they work to get healthy for playoffs
- Click here to listen to this article
-
- Tyler Glasnow gives up three hits, two runs and strikes out 10 over six innings in the Dodgers’ 8-2 win over the San Francisco Giants.
- The Dodgers hit four home runs in the eighth inning, including a pair of back-to-back homers. Mookie Betts finished with two home runs.
With eight games left in the regular season, the Dodgers have already ticked off the most important boxes on their postseason to-do list.
They clinched a playoff berth for a record-tying 14th straight season and won the division title for the fifth time in a row. And with Friday’s 8-2 victory over the San Francisco Giants, the Dodgers (94-60) also have an outside shot at their fourth 100-win season in six years.
But that doesn’t mean they don’t have a lot of work to do between now and the start of the playoffs — the most important task being determining exactly where and when they’ll open the postseason.
With Friday’s win and the Milwaukee Brewers’ victory in Baltimore, the Dodgers trail the Brewers by two games in the race for the league’s best record and the home-field advantage in the postseason that goes with it. They also lead the Atlanta Braves by four games for the league’s second-best record, which would give them a first-round playoff bye and an extra five days to get their sizable contingent of walking wounded healthy.
The magic is indeed missing, and after two seasons of conjuring up postseason greatness, these back-to-reality Dodgers appear headed for an early fall.
“To get one of these top two seeds is important. And our guys understand that,” Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said. “Winning the division is great, but I still think our best baseball is ahead of us.”
Achieving that, however, will require emptying an injury list that is almost as long as the team’s starting lineup. If the season ended today, the Dodgers would have at least seven players who wouldn’t be ready to play.
The Dodgers are also hopeful left-hander Blake Snell, who came out of Wednesday’s game after an inning with groin tightness, will be healthy enough to return for one more regular-season start.
Center fielder Andy Pages, who shares the team lead in RBIs with Shohei Ohtani despite missing a month with a fracture in his left hand, is expected to be activated for the series against the San Diego Padres, which begins Tuesday, while backup catcher Dalton Rushing is swinging a bat and will hit against a pitching machine this weekend.
Right-hander Roki Sasaki threw 48 pitches in a bullpen session Wednesday and could come off the IL next week but right-hander Edgardo Henriquez, second among Dodger relievers in innings and strikeouts, will miss the rest of the regular season with a back strain. He could join the team for the playoffs.
Then there’s Ohtani, the four-time MVP. He’s dealing with injuries to his left knee and right biceps. He has resumed taking batting practice and is eligible to come off the IL Wednesday. Roberts said he hopes to get Ohtani 10-12 at-bats before the playoffs.
“I’m just really waiting to hear when he’s going to get on the field, let alone take live BP,” Roberts said. “He’s not there yet. But everything I’ve heard, it’s been a really productive last three to four to five days.”
One player who did return was closer Edwin Díaz. Limited by multiple injuries to just 16 appearances this season, he was activated off the injured list Friday and threw 17 pitches in the ninth, giving up a single and striking out two batters.
For Roberts, the last month has looked like an episode of “The Pitt,” with medical crises piling up, one atop the other. Yet that’s hardly slowed the Dodgers, who opened their final homestand of the season having won 11 of their past 14 games.
Now the focus becomes continuing that momentum while getting as close to full strength as possible.
“They can go hand in hand,” Roberts said. “We have a lot of good players that are more than capable of helping us win baseball games, at the same time making sure we try to get our best players to optimum health when the postseason starts.”
The Dodgers got a big lift Friday from rookie Josue De Paula, a player who didn’t figure in their postseason plans until a week ago, when he was called up to take Ohtani’s place. In his Dodger Stadium debut, De Paula singled and scored on a Teoscar Hernández single in the fifth, then roped a double to the wall in right-center an inning later, scoring Kyle Tucker to put the Dodgers ahead to stay.
Tucker, Max Muncy, Mookie Betts and Will Smith all homered in a five-run eighth inning, turning a nail-biter into a comfortable win.
Dodgers owner Mark Walter and multiple insurance companies he owns are being sued for allegedly failing to disclose an ongoing federal probe to customers.
That gave right-hander Tyler Glasnow (5-1) his second win since April 23. Glasnow gave up just three hits in six innings, striking out a season-high 10 batters.
Hernández, who had two hits, is batting .368 with 17 RBIs in September; Tucker, who also had two hits, is hitting .424 with five home runs and 13 runs scored in his past 10 games; while Betts, with two homers Friday, has six hits in his past eight at-bats, lifting his average to a season-high .254.
That’s helped make up for Freddie Freeman’s struggles. Freeman, who went hitless in four at-bats Friday, striking out twice, has just six hits — and 13 strikeouts — in his last 48 at-bats.
“We still have a lot of work to do,” Roberts said before the game.
They have just over a week left to get it done.

Shohei Ohtani is progressing with his swing while on the injured list, although the Los Angeles Dodgers' designated hitter has yet to face pitching or the Trajekt kachine.
"He's not there yet," manager Dave Roberts said Friday, "but everything I've heard, it's been a really productive last three to four to five days. He's in a good spot."

Ohtani went on the IL just before the road trip with lingering pain in his right biceps, left leg and neck. He stayed back in Los Angeles to receive treatment and hit off a tee for the first time Tuesday.

item.title: [Orange County Register] Dodgers’ Shohei Ohtani making swing progress on IL
item.dc:creator: Janis Carr
item.description: LOS ANGELES — Dodgers star Shohei Ohtani casually strolled into the clubhouse on Friday, having received a positive report from his latest batting practice session that has progressed to taking pitches off coaches. “He’s in a good spot,” Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said before Friday’s opener against the San Francisco Giants. “He hit today and came out of it well. I’m just waiting to hear when he’s going to get on the field or take live BP or Trajekt. “He’s not there yet, but from everything I’
item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES — Dodgers star Shohei Ohtani casually strolled into the clubhouse on Friday, having received a positive report from his latest batting practice session that has progressed to taking pitches off coaches.
“He’s in a good spot,” Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said before Friday’s opener against the San Francisco Giants. “He hit today and came out of it well. I’m just waiting to hear when he’s going to get on the field or take live BP or Trajekt.
“He’s not there yet, but from everything I’ve heard it’s been a really productive last three to four to five days.”
Ohtani reunited with the team after their seven-game trip culminated with the Dodgers clinching the NL West title for the 13th time in 14 years with a win in Cincinnati on Thursday.
Ohtani, who went on the 15-day injured list just before the trip with right biceps and left knee issues, remained in Los Angeles to receive treatment. The four-time league MVP had been taking swings off a tee for several days before Friday.
He is eligible for activation as soon as Wednesday during the team’s final home series against the San Diego Padres, but when he rejoins the lineup will depend on his progress. Roberts is counting on Ohtani getting a few regular-season games before the postseason begins.
Before that happens, Roberts said he would like to see Ohtani take somewhere between 10 and 12 at-bats before putting him in the lineup.
“I think no matter what I say, it really doesn’t matter in the sense of it’s what he feels good with, what gets him ready,” Roberts said. “So, I could say 10, but it could be 12. But I think for me, if I’m just kind of spit balling and I think that 10 to 12 would be great.”
DIAZ IS ACTIVATED
Relief pitcher Edwin Diaz returned to the bullpen for Friday’s series opener. Roberts has said the 32-year-old right-hander will be used in low-leverage situations after missing a month because of neck inflammation.
Diaz has struggled with injuries (elbow surgery) and underperformance in his first season with the team, going 2-2 with an 11.85 ERA in 16 games with 19 strikeouts and 10 walks over 13⅔ innings. He made five rehab appearances with Triple-A Oklahoma City during his second IL stint of the season, allowing six runs with four strikeouts in 4⅓ innings.
Roberts said he just wants to see Diaz have success on the mound during the nine remaining regular-season games.
“Just pitch,” Roberts said of his expectations for Diaz. “Regardless of the role, I think we just want to see him throw the baseball the way he’s capable of. And you’re talking about nine games, so you’re talking three or four outings to evaluate and that should be adequate.”
To create a roster spot for Diaz, right-hander Landon Knack was optioned to Triple-A Oklahoma City, a day after throwing four scoreless innings in a victory over the Cincinnati Reds.
HELP ON THE HORIZON
Outfielder Andy Pages is set to return on Tuesday against the Padres after missing a month because of a hand fracture, but the news isn’t as hopeful for backup catcher Dalton Rushing.
Pages got hit by a pitch in a game last month against the Pittsburgh Pirates and subsequently had surgery to place a screw in his fifth metacarpal. He has been steadily increasing his baseball activity.
While Rushing is progressing from right elbow trouble, Roberts didn’t have a date for his return.
Rushing appeared in four games off the bench before going back on the 10-day injured list after missing significant time because of a slight tear in the UCL of his right elbow.
UP NEXT
Giants (TBA) at Dodgers (LHP Tarik Skubal, 10-7, 2.70 ERA), Saturday, 6:10 p.m., SNLA, 570 AM

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Dodgers injury updates: Where Shohei Ohtani, other stars stand entering final stretch
item.dc:creator: Andrés Soto; USA TODAY
item.description: LOS ANGELES — Dodgers manager Dave Roberts was in good spirits as he sat at the podium beneath Dodger Stadium on Friday, Sept. 18. His team returned home as National League West champions for the 13th time in 14 years after their 8-2 rout of the Cincinnati Reds to end their road trip. They also entered Friday's series opener against the San Francisco Giants with a four-game lead over the Atlanta Braves for the No. 2 seed in the NL and sat just two games behind the Milwaukee Brewers for the top s
item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES — Dodgers manager Dave Roberts was in good spirits as he sat at the podium beneath Dodger Stadium on Friday, Sept. 18. His team returned home as National League West champions for the 13th time in 14 years after their 8-2 rout of the Cincinnati Reds to end their road trip.
They also entered Friday's series opener against the San Francisco Giants with a four-game lead over the Atlanta Braves for the No. 2 seed in the NL and sat just two games behind the Milwaukee Brewers for the top seed with just nine games to go before October.
But perhaps taking priority over chasing playoff positioning, Roberts expressed confidence that the Dodgers could finish the season relatively healthy with both Shohei Ohtani and Blake Snell progressing well in the final two weeks of the regular season.
"I think it's about winning games, all the while ... getting our players back to health. But I think they can go hand in hand," Roberts said. "We have a lot of good players that are more than capable of helping us win baseball games and at the same time, making sure we try to get our best players to optimum health when the postseason starts."
Ohtani, who has been rehabbing at home while the Dodgers were on the road, swung a bat for the second time since landing on the 15-day injured list on Sept. 8. The two-way superstar took another step forward in his hitting progression as he took batting practice off of coach pitch and came away feeling good, per Roberts. While the Dodgers' skipper acknowledged "he's not there yet" as far as facing live pitching, that would be the next hurdle for Ohtani to clear before returning to the lineup.
In an ideal world, Roberts said he'd like for Ohtani to take somewhere around 10-12 at-bats in live batting practice before he gets activated, but acknowledged that it's really dependent on Ohtani himself.
"It's been a really productive three-to-four-to-five days. He's in a good spot," Roberts said. "No matter what I say, it really doesn't matter in the sense of it's what he feels good with, what gets him ready."
Snell, who exited his last start in Cincinnati after pitching just one inning with left groin tightness, continues to feel good and the overall sense is that he avoided a serious injury. Snell threw 90 feet on Friday while wearing a wrap around his left groin area, and Roberts is "very hopeful" that the former Cy Young winner can make one more regular season start.
Roberts is not sure when exactly that would be but did say that it would be a full start to ramp Snell up for the postseason rather than an abbreviated one.
"It'd be more of a normal start, maybe not pushing him a ton given we don't know how the season's going to play out," Roberts said. "But this will be his last regular season start, so I think it'd be more of a regular start."
The Dodgers' depleted bullpen does get some reinforcements back with closer Edwin Díaz being activated from the IL. He's available to pitch on Friday night if needed, and Roberts didn't rule out using him in low leverage situations to try and get him into a rhythm ahead of October.
Roberts also said that he expects outfielder Andy Pages to be activated at some point in the final home series against the San Diego Padres and catcher Dalton Rushing has also been progressing well, though there's no timeline on his return just yet.
This article originally appeared on USA TODAY: Dodgers injury updates: Where Shohei Ohtani, other stars stand entering final stretch

item.content:encoded:
LOS ÁNGELES -- Mientras Shohei Ohtani avanza en su recuperación de lesiones en la rodilla izquierda y el bíceps derecho, los Dodgers reafirmaron que sigue encaminado a regresar antes de que termine la temporada regular. El viernes dio el siguiente paso hacia ese objetivo, cuando tomó práctica de bateo ante lanzamientos de un coach.
“Salió bien de la sesión”, dijo el manager Dave Roberts. “Creo que, por mi parte, simplemente estoy esperando saber cuándo va a salir al terreno, ni hablar de tomar práctica de bateo en vivo o enfrentar a Trajekt. Y todavía no ha llegado a ese punto. Pero por todo lo que he escuchado, han sido tres, cuatro o cinco días realmente productivos. Está en un buen momento”.
Ohtani está aumentando su carga de trabajo exclusivamente como bateador, ya que no se espera que vuelva a lanzar esta temporada, luego de su última presentación en la lomita el 3 de julio. Su estadía en la lista de lesionados de 15 días es retroactiva al 8 de septiembre, por lo que podría ser activado, como muy pronto, el miércoles. Eso le daría un máximo de cinco juegos para recuperar el ritmo ante pitcheo de Grandes Ligas antes del inicio de la postemporada.
A los Dodgers les ha ido bastante bien sin Ohtani, con marca de 6-3 y 48 carreras anotadas, para un promedio de 5.3 por juego, aunque todos esos encuentros fueron contra equipos fuera de la contienda. Por supuesto, su alineación está en su mejor versión con el cuatro veces Jugador Más Valioso como primer bate... siempre y cuando esté saludable.
Durante buena parte de la temporada, Ohtani volvió a registrar números dignos del JMV, incluso mientras lidiaba con una serie de lesiones. Bateó .296 con 26 jonrones y OPS de .952 en sus primeros 110 juegos. Pero en los siguientes 24 encuentros antes de ingresar a la lista de lesionados, bateó .198 (de 96-19), con OPS de .690 y 34 ponches, un tramo que coincidió con un intento de aumentar progresivamente su carga de trabajo como lanzador.
Finalmente, los Dodgers decidieron que su estrella de dos vías no sólo necesitaba concentrarse exclusivamente en batear, sino que lo mejor para todos los involucrados era que Ohtani se tomara un tiempo para permitir que su cuerpo descansara y se recuperara, en lugar de intentar seguir jugando pese a las molestias.
Como Ohtani permaneció en Los Ángeles trabajando en su recuperación durante la gira más reciente de los Dodgers, no pudo celebrar con sus compañeros el jueves después de que aseguraran su 13er título del Oeste de la Liga Nacional en las últimas 14 temporadas. Eso significa que tendrá que esperar hasta que el equipo asegure otro objetivo para poder descorchar la champaña.
“Ya hicimos eso, así que vamos a ganar hoy y volveremos a brindar con ellos más adelante”, dijo Roberts. “Pero no, no voy a hacer un brindis especial, porque también hay muchos otros jugadores que fueron parte de esto”.

item.title: [MLB.com] Ohtani continues hitting progression as regular-season return remains in play

And he's not there yet. But everything I've heard, it
item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES -- As Shohei Ohtani works his way back from left knee and right biceps injuries, the Dodgers affirmed that he remains on pace to return before the regular season ends. His next step toward that goal came on Friday, when Ohtani hit coach-pitch batting practice.
“He came out of it well,” said manager Dave Roberts. “I think for me, I'm just really waiting to hear when he's going to get on the field, let alone take live BP or Trajekt. And he's not there yet. But everything I've heard, it's been a really productive last three to four to five days. He's in a good spot.”
Ohtani is building up exclusively as a hitter, as he is not expected to pitch again this season, having last appeared on the mound on July 3. His 15-day injured list stint is backdated to Sept. 8, so the earliest he can be activated is Wednesday -- giving him, at most, five games to find his footing against Major League pitching before the postseason gets underway.
The Dodgers have fared well enough with Ohtani out, going 6-3 while scoring 48 runs, good for 5.3 runs per game (albeit exclusively against non-contending teams). Of course, their lineup is at its best with the four-time MVP hitting leadoff … provided that he’s healthy.
For most of the season, Ohtani was once again putting up MVP-caliber numbers, even as he battled a spate of injuries, batting .296 with 26 homers and a .952 OPS through his first 110 games. But over the next 24 games ahead of landing on the IL, he hit .198 (19-for-96) with a .690 OPS and 34 strikeouts, a stretch coinciding with an attempted pitching ramp-up.
Ultimately, the Dodgers decided that their two-way star needed not only to focus exclusively on hitting, but that the best thing for everyone involved was Ohtani taking some time to let his body rest and recover rather than trying to continue to play through it.
Since Ohtani remained in L.A. to work on his recovery during the Dodgers’ most recent road trip, he missed out on celebrating with his teammates on Thursday after they clinched their 13th NL West title in the past 14 seasons. That means he’ll have to wait for another clinch in order to pop some champagne.
“We already did that, so we're gonna win today, and we'll re-toast with them going forward,” said Roberts. “But no, I'm not going to do a special toast, because there's a lot of other players that were part of this, too.”

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Dodgers hopeful to avoid worst-case scenario with injured star pitcher
item.dc:creator: Jack Harris
item.description: So far, so good in Blake Snell's bid to make another start before the end of the regular season. Despite leaving his last outing on Wednesday in Cincinnati after just one inning due to tightness in his left groin, Snell arrived at Dodger Stadium on Friday already feeling better, saying his groin was back up to an "8 out of 10" before heading out for a session of flat-ground catch play in the outfield. Dodgers manager Dave Roberts also offered an optimistic outlook on Snell's status, saying he wa
item.content:encoded:
So far, so good in Blake Snell's bid to make another start before the end of the regular season.
Despite leaving his last outing on Wednesday in Cincinnati after just one inning due to tightness in his left groin, Snell arrived at Dodger Stadium on Friday already feeling better, saying his groin was back up to an "8 out of 10" before heading out for a session of flat-ground catch play in the outfield.
Dodgers manager Dave Roberts also offered an optimistic outlook on Snell's status, saying he was "very hopeful" in the left-hander's chances to get back on the mound before the beginning of the playoffs.
"Happy that we caught it early," Roberts said of Snell's injury.
Indeed, when Snell exited Wednesday's game after 19 pitches, it raised immediate concerns about the state of the Dodgers' rotation.
Given the injuries the team is dealing with in its bullpen and its offense's inconsistent form through the second half of the season, the Dodgers will almost certainly need to lean on their starters during the playoffs — similar to the way they did last year, when a rotation of Snell, Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Tyler Glasnow and Shohei Ohtani (who will effectively be replaced by Tarik Skubal this year) carried the pitching staff to a second consecutive World Series title.
Losing Snell — who was already sidelined for three months earlier this season following an elbow procedure and has a history of left groin injuries throughout his career — would have dealt a massive blow to those plans.
However, the Dodgers are at least initially optimistic they've avoided anything close to a worst-case scenario.
While Roberts acknowledged that there is still "a little bit of uncertainty" regarding Snell, and no exact date for when he might pitch again, the skipper also noted that the two-time Cy Young Award winner didn't require medical imaging; another sign of the team's confidence that his injury was not more severe.
It's possible that, even if Snell continues to feel better, the Dodgers could elect to rest him for the remainder of the regular season to ensure he doesn't suffer any further setbacks before the playoffs.
But, they are also wary of giving Snell too long of a layoff entering the postseason.
"It's not just kind of plug-and-play," Roberts said, "[to] sit it out for two weeks and pitch in a playoff game."
Thus, the team will continue to monitor Snell's progress in the coming days, hopeful that a potential pitching crisis has been averted.
"We feel confident," Roberts said.

item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers could be getting one of their All-Stars back from injury. Dodgers manager Dave Roberts told Dodger Insider that Andy Pages will return when the club hosts the San Diego Padres.
It had been previously reported that Pages would return on the Dodgers’ final homestand of the 2026 season. This update gives a firmer timeline for when the 2026 All-Star will return to the lineup.
Pages has been a huge boost to the Dodgers’ lineup. The 25-year-old has slashed .272/.358/.458 with 21 home runs and a 119 wRC+ in 127 games this season. He also provides elite center field defense, rated at +18 Defensive Runs Saved and +9 Outs Above Average.
Dodgers Provide Andy Pages Return Timeline
With a return date set for Andy Pages, that means he’ll get roughly six games of action to prepare for the postseason. Ideally, the Dodgers center fielder can shake off a month’s worth of rust, since he won’t have the luxury of a rehab assignment.
Pages suffered a fracture of his left hand when he got hit by a 100 MPH fastball from the Pirates‘ Bubba Chandler. The club has turned to Alek Thomas and Tommy Edman in center field in his absence.
Edman is currently penciled in as the everyday center fielder after Thomas struggled in a short stint. The former Diamondback was later DFA’d, then outrighted to Triple-A after seven games in the lineup.
With Pages returning, the Dodgers have some tough lineup decisions. Edman will most likely return to the infield, bumping Alex Freeland off second base and off the roster. With Teoscar Hernandez on a hot streak, the club is unlikely to take him out of the lineup.
Dodgers Right Now
At 93-60, the Dodgers are currently up four games in the loss column over the Atlanta Braves, meaning they’re in great position to earn a bye for the Wild Card round.
They’ve already taken care of the first step by securing their fifth straight National League West division title. Now it’s just setting themselves up for the best chance to make a run in the postseason.
There are a lot of injuries the club needs to navigate. Shohei Ohtani, Roki Sasaki, and Edgardo Henriquez are the big ones to follow. Getting Ohtani back and healthy is going to be important if the Dodgers want to finish their three-peat bid.
Los Angeles will finish their 2026 season in California. They host the San Francisco Giants and San Diego Padres on their final homestand. Then they’ll finish out the year in San Francisco.
The Dodgers will send right-hander Tyler Glasnow for the series opener against the Giants. First pitch at Uniqlo Field at Dodger Stadium is set for 7:15 p.m. PT, with the game being broadcast on Apple TV+.

item.title: [Sports Illustrated] Dodgers Injury Updates: Shohei Ohtani, Blake Snell, Andy Pages and More

item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers are beginning their final homestand of the season on Friday night against the San Francisco Giants.
The Dodgers have just nine more games in the regular season. After clinching the National League West for the 13th time in the last 14 years, they're still battling for playoff positioning with the Milwaukee Brewers and Atlanta Braves.
If the Dodgers clinch one of the top two seeds, they'll secure a first-round bye. That is especially crucial this season as the team deals with injuries to a handful of key players.
Here's the latest updates on six of those players.
Shohei Ohtani Injury Update
Dodgers manager Dave Roberts told reporters on Friday that Ohtani is continuing to progress in his swinging progression.
“Everything I’ve heard it’s been a really productive last three, four, five days," Roberts said. "He’s in a good spot.”
Ohtani has not yet progressed to hitting in live batting practice or off the Trajekt machine. Thus, a return doesn't appear to be imminent.
Ohtani is eligible to return on Wednesday, just five days before the final day of the regular season.
Blake Snell Injury Update
Snell gave the Dodgers a major scare when he exited his Wednesday start after one inning with left groin tightness.
Fortunately, Snell said the exit was more precautionary than anything, as he didn't want to make it worse by staying in the game.
Snell expressed optimism he'd be able to make another start before the end of the regular season. On Friday, Roberts struck a similar tone, saying he was "more confident" the left-hander would be able to make a normal start sometime next week in his regular season finale.
Snell didn't undergo imaging on his groin.
Andy Pages Injury Update
Pages has been out since Aug. 21 when he suffered a fractured hand that forced him to undergo surgery.
However, he rejoined the team at home on Friday, and is expected to be activated at some point during the homestand that goes through Thursday.
Pages told David Vassegh of AM570 that he's hoping to be activated by Tuesday's series opener against the San Diego Padres.
Dalton Rushing Injury Update
Rushing told Fabian Ardaya of The Athletic that he had a PRP injection to address his elbow injury that forced him to go back on the IL in early September.
The catcher remains hopeful he'll be able to return as a pinch-hit option off the bench for the postseason, but will know more after hitting off a machine in the coming days.
Roki Sasaki Injury Update
Sasaki threw four simulated innings this week and is expected to start "soon," per Roberts.
The team initially planned to move Sasaki to the bullpen, but will instead keep him stretched out as a starter as an insurance option.
Edgardo Henriquez Injury Update
Henriquez surprisingly went on the IL with a low-grade back strain this past week, ending his regular season.
The Dodgers remain "hopeful" he'll be able to return in the postseason, per Roberts.
Sign up for our free newsletter and follow us on X/Twitter and Facebook for the latest news.
Noah Camras graduated from the University of Southern California in 2022 with a B.A. in Journalism and a minor in sports media studies. He was born and raised in Los Angeles and has extensively covered Southern California sports in his career. Noah is the publisher of Dodgers on SI after contributing as a writer and editor over the last three years.

Giants vs Dodgers Predictions, Picks & Props
- Los Angeles holds a massive pitching advantage with Tyler Glasnow on the mound in the Giants vs Dodgers predictions
- San Francisco’s decimated infield makes me lean towards the over (O 7.5, 54¢) in Giants vs Dodgers odds
- Read on to find my best Giants vs Dodgers predictions and picks for Friday’s MLB action
The San Francisco Giants (64-89) travel to face the postseason-bound Los Angeles Dodgers (93-60) in a late-night divisional clash. First pitch is scheduled for 10:15 PM EST on September 18 at UNIQLO Field at Dodger Stadium, broadcasting nationally on Apple TV+.
I approach this matchup strictly from a betting perspective. Los Angeles enters as a heavy home favorite, backed by a potent lineup and an elite starting arm in Tyler Glasnow. San Francisco looks overmatched as the road underdog, deploying a decimated roster against a superior opponent.
Finding value requires sifting through the statistical noise. I will isolate the clearest mismatches, analyze the public betting splits, and highlight the most profitable angles for this contest. Let us dive into the metrics.
Giants vs Dodgers Picks & Predictions
I evaluate multiple markets to find the absolute best prices, and prediction markets offers the premier payouts for my primary targets in this matchup.
Runline Pick: Los Angeles -1.5 Runs (55¢ on Polymarket)
At 56 cents per contract on Polymarket, I am laying the runline with the home favorites. The Dodgers boast a 3.64 team ERA compared to San Francisco’s 4.35 mark. The pitching discrepancy alone justifies this position. Tyler Glasnow features a dominant 0.97 WHIP and an exceptional 11.24 strikeouts per nine innings. He should easily carve up a struggling Giants lineup.
Total Runs Pick: Over 7.5 Runs (54¢ on Kalshi)
I am taking the Over 7.5 runs based on the massive situational mismatch. San Francisco starter Cesar Perdomo carries a 1.36 WHIP, meaning he constantly navigates traffic on the basepaths. Los Angeles averages 4.59 runs per game at home and features power hitters eager to capitalize on extra baserunners.
Best Player Prop: Glasnow Over 6.5 Ks (-137 at Kalshi)
Glasnow possesses elite swing-and-miss stuff. Averaging 11.24 K/9, he clears this number with ease during a standard five-inning outing. BetMGM offers the best price on this prop.
Giants vs Dodgers Odds & Public Betting
The traditional betting market heavily favors the home team. Early splits show staggering support for Los Angeles. They command 95.6% of the moneyline tickets and 93.2% of the overall financial stake.
San Francisco draws virtually zero action as the road underdog. Bettors see no value in backing a struggling squad against an elite arm. You can view wider market consensus by checking the MLB public betting trends before first pitch.
The total runs market displays a similar consensus. The Over pulls in 86.5% of tickets and 87.2% of the total handle. Serious bettors expect the Dodgers to inflict heavy damage against an overmatched pitching staff.
Giants vs Dodgers Pitching Matchup
The Giants vs Dodgers pitching matchup is Cesar Perdomo vs Tyler Glasnow. These are two pitchers who have been trending in opposite directions lately.
This pitching duel presents a massive imbalance. Glasnow brings an electric arsenal, evidenced by his 2.93 FIP and microscopic 0.97 WHIP. He routinely limits hard contact while generating premium whiff rates. Over his last 55.2 innings and 10 starts, he maintained an 11.5 K/9 ratio.
Perdomo relies heavily on pitching to contact, generating just 5.91 K/9. That strategy spells disaster against a lineup capable of punishing mistakes. His 1.36 WHIP indicates he allows too many free passes and base hits, which creates high-leverage situations early in games.
Giants vs Dodgers: Stats Comparison & Betting Trends
Note: The number in parentheses denotes the team’s ranking among all 30 MLB clubs.
Los Angeles owns superior season-long metrics across the board. They strike the ball harder, posting an 89.4 mph average exit velocity at home. Their pitching staff limits baserunners effectively, yielding a stellar 1.16 WHIP.
San Francisco frequently struggles to strand runners. Their 4.35 overall ERA highlights a persistent inability to escape jams. Checking MLB starting lineups reveals exactly how outmatched the Giants look on paper tonight.
Looking at situational trends, Los Angeles thrives in this exact spot. They boast a 61.5% win rate when listed as the betting favorite (88-55).
San Francisco struggles immensely when bookmakers expect them to lose. They win just 38.8% of their games as the underdog (40-63). Furthermore, the Over hits at a 70.0% clip across their last 10 contests, aligning perfectly with my total runs projection.
Giants vs Dodgers Injury Report & Weather Impact
San Francisco attempts to compete without a functional starting infield. Missing Rafael Devers and Matt Chapman evaporates their offensive ceiling. Relying on replacement-level bats against an elite strikeout arm is a losing proposition.
Los Angeles navigates the loss of Shohei Ohtani smoothly thanks to stars like Mookie Betts. Their depth prevents major downgrades to their overall team projections.
Finally, bettors should monitor the MLB weather report closer to first pitch. Wind patterns in Chavez Ravine heavily influence whether routine fly balls leave the yard. I always verify atmospheric conditions before finalizing my card.
Juan Pablo is a sports writer and betting analyst with over 15 years' experience in the industry. He is an expert in European and Latin American soccer, as well as NBA, MLB, NHL, NFL, college sports, and EuroLeague. He was born and raised in Chile and is fluent in Spanish, English, and Portuguese.

item.content:encoded:
On Friday night, the Dodgers return to Los Angeles for a six-game homestand, which includes this series against the San Francisco Giants.
The Dodgers just secured their fifth consecutive NL West crown on Thursday with a win over the Reds.
But there is still more baseball to be played before the postseason starts, and Los Angeles will be fighting for playoff positioning with the Milwaukee Brewers, who currently hold a two-game lead for the top seed in the NL.
If the Dodgers want to cut into Milwaukee’s lead, however, they will need to do so without superstar Shohei Ohtani, who remains on the injured list while recovering from several minor issues.
Fortunately, Ohtani is expected to return before the end of the regular season, but the Dodgers will need Freddie Freeman, Mookie Betts and the rest of the lineup to carry the offense against San Francisco.
Tyler Glasnow will get the start for Los Angeles tonight after posting a strong 4-1 record and 3.50 ERA this season, while San Francisco will counter with left-hander Cesar Perdomo (0-1, 3.68 ERA).
The stakes of this rivalry matchup would normally be higher, but with the Giants well outside of the playoff picture, their only real motivation is trying to complicate Los Angeles’ final stretch before the postseason.
Giants vs. Dodgers Game Details:
- Matchup: San Francisco Giants vs. Los Angeles Dodgers
- Date: Friday, September 18, 2026
- First pitch: 10:15 p.m. ET / 7:15 p.m. PT
- Venue: UNIQLO Field at Dodger Stadium
- San Francisco probable starter: Cesar Perdomo, 0-1, 3.68 ERA
- Los Angeles probable starter: Tyler Glasnow, 4-1, 3.50 ERA
- TV: Apple TV
On paper, Glasnow gives Los Angeles the more established arm, while Perdomo enters with only a small major league sample and is coming off his roughest outing.

Cesar Perdomo gave up five runs in 4 2/3 innings in his last outing, and he will now be up against one of the best lineups in the league.
The Dodgers rank fourth in total runs and third in batting average this season.

Los Angeles has several advantages here, beginning with Glasnow and extending to a deeper lineup even with Ohtani unavailable.
The Dodgers also arrive home immediately after clinching the NL West and have an opportunity to close the gap on Milwaukee for the top spot in the NL.
Meanwhile, San Francisco is merely playing out the final weeks of a disappointing season.

Dodgers’ president of baseball operations Andrew Freidman told reporters on Thursday that Shohei Ohtani (knee, biceps) is expected to return before the end of the regular season.

When pressed to see how many at-bats he’s expected to receive before the postseason, Friedman just shrugged his shoulders. It sounds like the Dodgers want to get him a handful of at-bats next weekend, if possible, but their priority is to have him healthy and ready to go for the start of the postseason.

item.content:encoded:
Mookie Betts: “Nos queda un largo camino por recorrer”
El campocorto de los Dodgers coloca en perspectiva la participación de la novena en la postemporada por decimotercera vez en los últimos 14 años.
PUBLICIDAD
Cincinnati. Los Dodgers de Los Ángeles aseguraron su quinto título consecutivo de la División Oeste de la Liga Nacional y el 13ro en las últimas 14 temporadas al vencer el jueves 8-2 a los Reds de Cincinnati.
“Es algo muy importante. Creo que mucha gente piensa que es solo un rito de paso (pero) no es fácil”, declaró el mánager de los Dodgers Dave Roberts. “Así que es algo de lo que todos estamos muy orgullosos, pero entendemos claramente que ese no es el objetivo final”.
Los Dodgers (93-60) disputarán los playoffs por 14 temporada consecutiva, con lo que igualan el récord que los Bravos de Atlanta establecieron de 1991-2005.
Sights and sounds from the clubhouse. 👀 pic.twitter.com/0UTzHdvvpK
— Los Angeles Dodgers (@Dodgers) September 18, 2026
“Es el primer paso”, dijo Mookie Betts mientras se secaba el champán de los ojos. “Nos queda un largo camino por recorrer”.
La celebración en el terreno de juego fue algo calmada tras el último out el jueves. Pero los jugadores se soltaron en el vestuario, donde el champán y la cerveza salpicaron desde el suelo hasta el techo.
“Creo que es una de esas situaciones en las que, como en el béisbol se juega a diario, los jugadores se centran en rendir”, dijo Roberts. “Así que no hay muchos momentos para celebrar. Por eso es agradable ver a los chicos soltarse un poco”.
A pesar de todos sus laureles, los Dodgers creen que todavía tienen algo que demostrar.
El año pasado, el equipo pulverizó el récord de gasto de las Grandes Ligas con una nómina total de 515 millones de dólares, dando alas a críticas de que tienen una supuesta ventaja injusta.
“Lo que estamos creando aquí es especial”, afirmó Max Muncy. “Definitivamente no se le da el reconocimiento que merece. Todo el mundo se fija en la nómina, pero nunca hablamos de cómo hacemos las cosas bien, de cómo nos preparamos adecuadamente o de cómo cuidamos todos esos pequeños detalles. De eso no se habla”.
Doc and the boys are ready for October. pic.twitter.com/krnwXYR7ap
— Los Angeles Dodgers (@Dodgers) September 17, 2026
Los bicampeones defensores de la Serie Mundial aún pujan por el primer puesto de preclasificación de la Liga Nacional, que actualmente está en posesión de los Cerveceros de Milwaukee. Los Ángeles comenzó el día con una ventaja de tres juegos y medio sobre los Bravos (89-64) por el segundo puesto, pero está por detrás de los Cerveceros (95-57).
“Seguimos luchando por uno de los dos primeros puestos”, dijo Roberts. “Creo que hacemos bien celebrando, pero sin dejar que eso afecte a lo que sigue. Tenemos que tomar el vuelo y jugar contra los Gigantes mañana”.
Los Dodgers buscan convertirse en el primer equipo en conquistar tres campeonatos consecutivos de la Serie Mundial desde que los Yankees lo lograron de 1998 a 2000.
Este es el cuarto título divisional asegurado más temprano para los Dodgers. Aseguraron el Oeste de la Liga Nacional el 10 de septiembre de 2019, el 13 de septiembre de 2022 y el 16 de septiembre de 2023.
Los Ángeles aprovechará ese tiempo para recuperar lesionados. Eso empieza con Shohei Ohtani.
El cuatro veces Jugador Más Valioso ha estado en la lista de lesionados de 15 días desde el 8 de septiembre por una inflamación en el bíceps derecho y les dijo a los reporteros a principios de este mes que ya no lanzará más en lo que resta de temporada. La estrella de dos vías hizo swings desde un tee por primera vez el martes y se sintió bien. Se espera que regrese como bateador antes de que termine la temporada regular, aunque no está claro si podrá llegar al 100% de salud antes de octubre.
Roki Sasaki, en la lista de lesionados por una ampolla en el dedo medio, lanzó en una práctica de bateo en vivo el miércoles en Cincinnati y salió bien. Roberts indicó que su próxima aparición será como abridor.
Blake Snell salió prematuramente de la apertura del miércoles después de un inning por rigidez en la ingle izquierda. Su situación es incierta.
Se espera que el cerrador puertorriqueño Edwin Díaz, quien ha estado en la lista de lesionados desde agosto por una inflamación en el cuello, sea activado el viernes. El venezolano Edgardo Henríquez, un preparador de mesa en el bullpeb, está en la lista de lesionados por molestias en la parte baja de la espalda. Se le realizó una resonancia magnética en Los Ángeles el miércoles, que reveló una distensión lumbar, y su rehabilitación se pausará por unos días.
El primera base Freddie Freeman, aquejado por dolor en la rodilla derecha, regresó a la alineación el martes y cortó una mala racha de 3 hits en 30 turnos con tres imparables. Sumó otros dos hits el jueves.
Los Dodgers protagonizaron el mayor impacto de la fecha límite de cambios al adquirir a Tarik Skubal, ganador en dos ocasiones del premio Cy Young de la Liga Americana, procedente de los Tigres. Skubal tiene marca de 3-2 con efectividad de 2.52 en ocho aperturas con los Dodgers.
La incorporación de Skubal convirtió a los Dodgers en los grandes favoritos en las apuestas para ganar la Serie Mundial. Pero después de comenzar la temporada con marca de 61-36, los Dodgers tienen registro de 31-24 desde la pausa del Juego de Estrellas.
Los Dodgers dejaron a 12 corredores en base y se fueron de 0 en 11 con corredores en posición de anotar en la derrota del miércoles ante los Reds, algo que, según Roberts, necesita mejorar.
“Se trata de poder rematar a los equipos cuando tenemos oportunidades. En la postemporada no se presentan muchas oportunidades. Hay que saber aprovecharlas”, dijo Roberts.
___

item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers are under the biggest microscope in baseball as the regular season comes to a close. With October right around the corner, all eyes are on LA to see if they will win three consecutive championships for the first time in MLB in a quarter-century.
Superstar Shohei Ohtani has not been fully healthy essentially since the All-Star break, when he was scratched from not only his final start of the first half, but from all All-Star-related activities. After being shut down from pitching in early July, the concern has only grown coming out of an August where he only attained a .241 batting average for the month.
After Ohtani was placed on the injured list, Josue De Paula appeared to be the answer for the lack of Ohtani in the lineup.
Though it is obvious that De Paula will not be pitching, his offense has the potential to start to fill the enormous Ohtani-sized shoes. In Double-A, the 21-year-old slashed .303/.401/.547 with 27 home runs and 104 RBIs, leading to a call-up that preceded any Triple-A action.
De Paula was hitless during the first two games of his MLB career, but earned his first hit via a towering fourth-inning home run last Sunday.
Due to his astounding minor league track record, his 92.6 mph exit velocity at the MLB level thus far, and the fact that the organization didn't feel the need for him to move up to Triple-A, there have been murmurs as to what his spot on a postseason roster may be.
Manager Dave Roberts spoke on if De Paula should be under consideration for a roster spot, even though he will have less than a month of MLB knowledge come October.
“Yeah, he should be [under consideration],” Roberts said. “This is more of a trial run, no promises. Just obviously having Shohei down and giving a guy that’s performed well an opportunity. Then you just sort of see where it takes us.
"I think right now that’s kind of where we’re at and take it day to day. I just hope he continues to perform and take those at-bats and then we’ll kind of see where we’re at in September.”
Roberts also clarified that the rookie's status for the postseason even being a potential storyline says more about the maturity and talent of De Paula.
“It’s been good that you can even bring that question up,” Roberts said. “But it’s still very early as far as however many at-bats or plate appearances he has taken. But in this small sample, yeah, it’s been good. But it’s certainly a much different level of focus with the postseason. But baseball is still baseball. I hope he makes our decision hard.”
Across seven games thus far, De Paula is 3-for-18 (.167) with one home run, four RBIs, seven walks and an OPS of .789.
Sign up for our free newsletter and follow us on X/Twitter and Facebook for the latest news.
Gabe Smallson is a sportswriter based in Los Angeles with a focus in sports and entertainment content. Gabe has previously worked at Newsweek and Dodgers Nation. He graduated from San Francisco State University in 2020 and received his Masters of Science at the University of Southern California in 2025.
