item.content:encoded:
Why Dodgers' top rookie of 2026 is not Josue De Paula originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.
The Los Angeles Dodgers have no shortage of talent.
Even with Shohei Ohtani on the injured list, the NL West club has one of, if not the best, rosters in the Majors.
Concerns about the bullpen are warranted. But a starting three in the rotation of Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Tarik Skubal, and one of Blake Snell, Tyler Glasnow, and Justin Wrobleski is dominant.
With Ohtani on the IL, the Dodgers promoted a new talented prospect to replace him at designated hitter: slugger Josue De Paula.
De Paula promptly hit a homer just a few games into his first taste of the Majors and has a .789 OPS through 25 plate appearances.
But Bleacher Report's Kerry Miller believes it's too soon to label him the best Dodgers rookie of the season. Instead, Miller awarded that distinction to a middle infielder.
"There's already a case to be made for Josue De Paula in this spot, even though he just made his MLB debut as Shohei Ohtani's fill-in last Friday," Miller wrote.
"However, [Alex] Freeland spent much of the season as the Dodgers' primary second baseman, providing decent value with his glove while hitting just well enough to earn regular playing time."
Freeland doesn't have eye-popping offensive numbers, hitting .230 with four home runs and a 79 OPS+.
But he has +3 outs above average while playing at three infield spots, mainly second base.
De Paula could change Miller's mind during the final week of the regular season. Manager Dave Roberts should give him plenty of playing time.
For now, Freeland has done enough to warrant the title as the Dodgers' best rookie of the year.

item.content:encoded:
Welcome to the California Post's weekly Dodgers recap, where we review the week that was, hand out very official awards and take stock of the state of the season.
PLAYER OF THE WEEK
Kyle Tucker (12-for-29 since Sept. 9; triple shy of the cycle on Thursday)
Off the bat, it appeared history was afoot.
Already on Thursday afternoon, Kyle Tucker had kicked his slow late-season turnaround into a suddenly more hopeful gear, hitting a two-run home run in the first, an RBI double in the second and a single that aided a three-run rally in the fourth.
Now, standing at the plate just a triple shy of the cycle in the eighth, he laced a line drive that made the feat feel possible.
With yet another squared-up swing, the $240 million slugger shot a ball into the left-center field gap. As two Reds outfielders converged on it, the entire Dodgers dugout rose in anticipation.
Alas, the 11th cycle in Dodgers history would have to wait.
The Reds turned a clean relay play. Tucker wisely — although, somewhat disappointingly, given the lopsided score — pulled up at second. And on the bench, all his teammates could do was razz him by mimicking send signs with their arms helplessly waving.
"I tried my best, but I don't think I was gonna get there," he told SportsNet LA afterward. "I probably would've been thrown out halfway."
Oh, well.
For this year's Dodgers, Tucker's 4-for-5, three-RBI game was still hugely encouraging, continuing what is now a weeklong surge in which the four-time All-Star has finally looked like himself.
Even before this stretch, the Dodgers committed to keeping Tucker as a key part of their lineup.
They hoped a breakthrough he made with his mechanics could salvage something from an otherwise disastrous debut campaign with the team.
Well, in his last eight games, Tucker has batted .414 with seven extra-base knocks, 10 RBIs and more walks (five) than strikeouts (four).
He has hit five home runs in his last 13 games, after collecting just 11 in his first 132 games this year.
It is the version of Tucker that the Dodgers will need in the playoffs, especially with fellow left-handed bats like Shohei Ohtani and Freddie Freeman battling ongoing injuries.
After a season that once seemed so lost, signs of revival have arrived just in time.
PITCHERS OF THE WEEK
Tarik Skubal and Yoshinobu Yamamoto (seven scoreless innings from each)
We are going with a tandem honor this week, from a pair of pitchers who will likely have the biggest influence on the Dodgers' World Series chances.
With Blake Snell battling a groin injury, and Tyler Glasnow entering a Friday start having recently regressed in his return from the injured list, the Dodgers' rotation doesn't feel quite as formidable as it once did.
Then again, if Skubal and Yamamoto keep pitching like they did this week — when they spun consecutive scoreless seven-inning outings in Cincinnati — those other question marks might not feel so daunting.
Both pitchers have sterling postseason track records: Yamamoto with a 7-1 record and 2.25 ERA in 10 playoff outings (including last year's World Series heroics) and Skubal with a 2-1 record and 2.04 ERA in six October appearances of his own (all with the Tigers the last two years).
Either could anchor a pitching staff on their own capable of making a run to the Fall Classic.
Together, they give the Dodgers arguably the best 1-2 punch in the majors. This week, they delivered the club's first pair of back-to-back scoreless seven-inning outings since 2022 when Tyler Anderson and Clayton Kershaw did it.
Granted, dominating the Reds in mid-September is not the same as producing gems in the playoffs.
But with so many other concerns mounting at the moment, Skubal and Yamamoto at least represent a pillar of potential pitching excellence to lean on, one that could compensate for other shortcomings in the Dodgers' three-peat bid.
PROSPECT OF THE WEEK
The entire Dodgers' minor-league system
The Dodgers' big-league club hasn't been the only one popping bottles in beer-soaked clubhouse celebrations recently.
This year, all four of the organization's minor-league affiliates also clinched places in their respective playoffs, with Triple-A Oklahoma City completing the quad-fecta by winning the second-half title in the Pacific Coast League on Wednesday.
It marks the first time the Dodgers have had four affiliates make the playoffs since 2019 (and that year included their now-defunct rookie-ball outpost in Ogden, Utah).
It's also the latest reminder about the strength of depth they boast in their highly touted farm system.
"I know people don't care about minor-league win percentages, but we kind of do," Dodgers general manager Brandon Gomes told the California Post earlier this season. "I think it's a good proxy of how well your farm system is performing and how to understand what it takes to win."
Three of the club's affiliates have already been eliminated, with Double-A Tulsa, High-A Great Lakes and Single-A Ontario all losing in their division championship series.
OKC, meanwhile, will begin its postseason push next week in the best-of-three PCL Championship Series against the Athletics' Las Vegas affiliate. If they win that, they will remain in Vegas for the Triple-A National Championship Game against the winner of the International League.
QUESTION OF THE WEEK
Who should Dodgers hope to see in the first round of the playoffs?
With the NL West crown secured, the Dodgers still have work to do over the season's final nine games.
Given their injury problems, they've never needed a first-round bye so badly.
The good news: They remain four games up on the Braves for the NL's No. 2 seed, with their magic number down to six for securing passage straight to the NL Division Series.
And though they remain two games back of the Brewers for the best record in the majors — and home-field advantage throughout the playoffs — conventional wisdom in recent weeks has suggested that the playoff through the postseason might be better from the 2-seed anyway.
Now, however, the NL playoff field is getting muddied, with the red-hot Padres sitting just one game back of the Cubs and Phillies.
So, who should Dodgers fans root to see in a potential first-round matchup? Well, it depends on what kind of matchup you think suits the Dodgers best.
The Cubs and Phillies had seemed like tougher draws than the Braves or Padres, thanks to Chicago's deep and homer-happy lineup and the Phillies' powerhouse starting rotation trio.
But this week, Philadelphia lost one of its star pitchers, Jesús Luzardo, to a shoulder injury that has put his playoff availability in doubt. The Cubs, meanwhile, have seen their offense cool off and still face questions with an unimposing starting rotation.
The Braves have their own flaws (they've been a middle-of-the-pack offense since the All-Star break) but still boast Chris Sale at the top of their rotation.
The Padres, on the other hand, are making a familiar late-season surge and have a habit of playing the Dodgers tough in the playoffs.
It will all make for a fascinating final few days of scoreboard watching, with a slew of new postseason permutations now on the table.
The Dodgers, of course, won't be overly worried about who they might square off against. Their focus is on continuing to play a better brand of all-around baseball — and making sure they avoid the best-of-three wild-card round.

item.title: [New York Post] Move over, Lakers. Not so fast, Rams. Dodgers are NL West champions again — and still LA’s team
item.dc:creator: Dylan Hernandez
item.description: The Dodgers are the National League West champions. Again. They have won their division 13 times in the last 14 seasons, and the one time in that period in which they didn’t, they won a then-club-record 106 games. Somewhere along the way, the Dodgers did the impossible: They met the requirements to become the sports franchise Los Angeles demanded. item.content:encoded:
The Dodgers are the National League West champions.
Again.
They have won their division 13 times in the last 14 seasons, and the one time in that period in which they didn’t, they won a then-club-record 106 games.
Somewhere along the way, the Dodgers did the impossible: They met the requirements to become the sports franchise Los Angeles demanded.
Appreciating what this means requires an understanding of how Shaquille O’Neal and Kobe Bryant transformed this city in the early 2000s,
With O’Neal and Bryant as their stars, the Lakers didn’t just win championships.
They were unbeatable.
This image was reinforced by the play of O’Neal, a 7-foot-1, 325-pound freak of nature who literally couldn’t be stopped.
By the time the Lakers completed their three-peat in 2002, championships were no longer something Los Angeles hoped for.
They became something the city expected.
This is the standard used to measure teams with aspirations of becoming a cultural touchstone in this congested market. With plenty of other entertainment options, casual fans won’t invest too much of their time and money in a team unless they believe it will create the kind of citywide pride O’Neal’s Lakers once did.
The Lakers haven’t been that team for some time. The Rams are producing a worthy on-field product, but they remain in the process of winning back fans they lost over the two decades they spent in St. Louis.
The Dodgers are the one team in town that is clearing the bar.
“What’s funny is Los Angeles has always been looked at, as far as sports, (as) a Laker town,” manager Dave Roberts said. “I think we might have the market share right now in Los Angeles. It’s great. I think we draw more fans than anyone in the world, obviously, with the home dates we have. But it’s 40,000, 50,000 every night. We travel well. I do think the guys see it. They feed off it.”
The Dodgers managed to do this despite playing a sport that is particularly hard to dominate. The Lakers could dump the ball into O’Neal 30 times a game. The Dodgers have employed a number of Hall of Famers over the years, but as great as Shohei Ohtani is, he can only hit four times a game, maybe five.
The Dodgers have become a different kind of juggernaut.
With substantial investment from their owners, they have built some of the deepest rosters in baseball history. In its first season operating the team, Guggenheim Baseball Management signed All-Star outfielder Andre Ethier to an $85 million extension, picked up a then-unknown Yasiel Puig for $42 million, traded for All-Star infielder Hanley Ramirez and assumed more than $260 million in contract obligations in a blockbuster trade for Adrian Gonzalez, Carl Crawford and Josh Beckett.
Season after season, the Dodgers fielded one of the most expensive teams in the major leagues — if not the most expensive team.
Which is why at some point in each of the last 14 seasons, the Dodgers were considered favorites to win the World Series.
They are well into their second decade as baseball’s model franchise — or, depending on the perspective, Evil Empire. The last time they didn’t reach the playoffs, the world was a completely different place. LeBron James had just won his first NBA championship. “Gangnam Style” was a global phenomenon. The recreational use of marijuana was still outlawed in every jurisdiction of the United States.
There’s an entire generation of fans who don’t know what it’s like for the Dodgers to not be legitimate contenders.
Consistency by itself didn’t turn the Dodgers into the Dodgers of today. Actually winning championships was important, of course, and doing that required them to adjust how they built their rosters.
President of baseball operations Andrew Friedman used to operate as if the playoffs were a crapshoot. The organization’s focus was on the regular season, on just reaching the postseason. Because depth is required to survive a 162-game schedule, quantity was emphasized over quality.
The approach didn’t produce any championships. The Dodgers reached the World Series twice in their first eight seasons under Guggenheim ownership but lost both times.
The failures prompted them to pursue real difference-makers.
Mookie Betts, who was the catalyst of the championship team in 2020. Freddie Freeman, the home run hero of the 2024 World Series. Yoshinobu Yamamoto, the Most Valuable Player of the 2025 World Series. And, of course, Ohtani, the franchise’s most transformative player since Fernando Valenzuela, or maybe even Jackie Robinson.
The Dodgers have won three of the last six World Series.
Even with Ohtani dealing with right arm and left knee injuries, they will open the postseason as the odds-on favorites to win their third consecutive championship.
As fragmented as Los Angeles can be, most of the city can get behind that.

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] With another NL West title in hand, the prospect of October without Shohei Ohtani looms large for the Dodgers
item.dc:creator: Jake Mintz

item.content:encoded:
CINCINNATI — As the celebrating Los Angeles Dodgers drenched one another in various carbonated boozes, the team's most important character was bone dry and most likely quite sober roughly two thousand miles away.
Shohei Ohtani, that baseballing mover of mountains, is injured. A laundry list of ailing body parts — biceps, knee, neck — first kept the two-way dynamo from pitching, then frayed his offensive impact and finally rendered him physically incapable of taking the field. Last week, the Dodgers placed him on the IL, with just a few weeks left for him to recover before the start of the postseason and only five games between his earliest eligible return date and the end of the regular season.
Publicly, the club has maintained an optimistic tone, describing his issues as manageable, not season-ending. A return before the end of the regular season is still in play, skipper Dave Roberts reaffirmed this week. Yet nobody around the game would be shocked if the Dodgers opt for caution and keep Ohtani sidelined until October. Los Angeles' worst-case scenario, of course, would be a postseason without its main man.
So when the Dodgers embarked on their recent two-city swing, their $700 million slugger stayed back in Southern California. He rested, received treatment and hit off a tee — or, as Roberts vaguely put it, "continued his progression."
"Overall, [his] body feels normal-ish," Roberts said before Thursday's clincher. "Then it's kind of getting his body, his knee, his arm, biceps, whatever, back to full strength."
This marked the first time in the Dodgers' Ohtani Era that the man himself did not accompany the team for the entirety of a road trip. In fact, the most recent occurrence of a Dodgers club flying home without Ohtani came in October 2023, after the team's sweep loss to the Diamondbacks in that year's NLDS. Lance Lynn, Austin Barnes and a decade of frustration were on board that plane. Ohtani was still technically an Angel. In other words, it's been a while.
With the two-way superstar now the center of the Dodgers' solar system — and, to a large extent, the league's extended universe — Ohtani's absence this week in Cincinnati was easy to sense, impossible to avoid. Throughout the week, all about the yard, were reminders both big and small.
The blue bat bags lined up outside the locker room in numerical order went right from Will Smith's No. 16 to Kyle Tucker's No. 23, with no No. 17 to be found. Dodgers head security guard Al Garcia, typically within eyesight of Ohtani at all times, floated around the clubhouse with an uncharacteristically laid-back comportment buoyed by his relatively light list of duties.
A group of passionate Dodgers fans recognized the star's absence with a homemade sign that read "Feel Better Shohei, Give Decoy A Hug," making reference to Ohtani's dog. Even Yoshinobu Yamamoto admitted that it was odd not having Ohtani around, delivering one of his funnier and more cutting lines of the season.
"It's been a weird feeling because I talk to him all the time in the clubhouse," Yamamoto said via interpreter Yoshihiro Sonoda. "Although I have Roki [Sasaki], he doesn't really talk to me."
The Dodgers' lineup missed Ohtani, too, averaging less than four runs per game on the road trip before Thursday's eight-run outburst against a bottom-five Cincinnati pitching staff. Utilityman Tommy Edman got the bulk of leadoff duties, with Mookie Betts and rookie call-up Josue De Paula getting a day each in the one-hole. Edman went just 1-for-23 on the trip. Freddie Freeman's power dip continued, with five singles and nothing else. Will Smith has yet to really pop off since his return from the IL on Sept. 1.
"It feels different because he's such a presence when he's on the field," Roberts admitted Monday.
Therein lies the lingering concern. The Dodgers and Ohtani have all but accepted that he won't pitch again this season. That's not the end of the world; Los Angeles has the arms to solve that problem. On the other hand, navigating October without Ohtani at full-go would be a difficult proposition.
Ohtani's health, too, is not binary. Even if he plays, which at this point feels likely, he's unlikely to be completely healed. That dynamic could very well hamper his performance. Ohtani, overly cautious as they come, revealed that concern the last time he spoke to reporters on Sept. 8.
"I should have enough experience to address any kinks or injuries or anything like that with the swing," Ohtani said. "I'm going to use this as an opportunity to add on to the experience that I've had previously and address it regardless."
It's not exactly the most reassuring explanation — Ohtani implying that he'll need to manage his various discomforts for the rest of the season. How that process transpires and how productive Ohtani proves to be in October could determine how many Champagne celebrations he'll get to participate in this year.

item.title: [Dodgers Nation] Shohei Ohtani Expected to Return Before Dodgers Regular Season Ends
item.dc:creator: Nelson Espinal
item.description: Los Angeles Dodgers superstar Shohei Ohtani may play again this season, according to baseball operations president Andrew Friedman. While taking a ton of champagne and celebrating a 13th National League title in 14 years, Friedman took a question about Ohtani and his outlook. “He’s doing well,” Friedman said. “He’s progressing well. I expect him back in the regular season.” Ohtani was not with the team in Cincinnati to celebrate the NL West title; instead, he was in Los Angeles continuing his re
item.content:encoded:
Los Angeles Dodgers superstar Shohei Ohtani may play again this season, according to baseball operations president Andrew Friedman.
While taking a ton of champagne and celebrating a 13th National League title in 14 years, Friedman took a question about Ohtani and his outlook.
“He’s doing well,” Friedman said. “He’s progressing well. I expect him back in the regular season.”
Ohtani was not with the team in Cincinnati to celebrate the NL West title; instead, he was in Los Angeles continuing his rehabilitation on his injured right bicep and his left knee.
According to manager Dave Roberts, Ohtani had a day off on Wednesday, though he did hit off a tee and will do some hitting from a coach’s pitches at some point this week.
“There’s no pain. He’s doing everything he needs to do,” Roberts said. “I still don’t know when [the] time to return to play is. But everything that I hear is really positive.”
Does Ohtani need to play in the regular season?
The Dodgers will play Ohtani in the postseason, regardless of whether he plays in the regular season again, general manager Brandon Gomes said, focusing on how he feels rather than his season participation.
“The most important thing is that he’s healthy and in good shape. Whether it’s during the regular season or after that, as long as he’s fully prepared and ready to go, we’re fine with it,” Gomes said, per Japanese reporter Masaya Kotani.
Ohtani has mentioned in the past that he doesn’t get better from playing; rather, rest is the best medicine.
If that is the case and Ohtani can sharpen up a bit with batting practice, sitting him may ensure the Dodgers see the best version of their best player.
Ideally, fans get to see him take some swings over the next week and look better than he did before landing on the injured list.
In his last plate appearances, Ohtani struggled to rotate his body into swings and generate full extension.
He looked to wince after swings, suffering from visible pain in his right arm.
If he can swing fully and tune up his vision for the postseason, it is worth rolling him out, but the Dodgers will err on the side of caution no matter what.

item.content:encoded:
CINCINNATI -- Heralded by the thumping beat of "Bailalo Rocky," Roki Sasaki opened eyes and electrified Chavez Ravine as the postseason closer during the Dodgers' run to back-to-back championships. The 24-year-old could be poised for a return to the 'pen for L.A.'s three-peat bid -- but he'll make at least one more start before the end of the regular season.
Sasaki has been sidelined since exiting his Aug. 26 start in Atlanta due to a blister on his right middle finger, and he should be activated from the 15-day injured list during the Dodgers' final homestand, likely in next week's series against the Padres.
The Dodgers had been considering getting Sasaki reacclimated to the bullpen before the postseason, but they kept the option of him starting open. Sasaki has remained stretched out during his time on the IL, most recently throwing four simulated innings on 48 pitches on Wednesday afternoon in Cincinnati.
"There's benefits both ways," manager Dave Roberts said. "One can argue it's best to take down a couple starts, keep him built up. Because if something does happen, he's built up. The other side is you can assimilate him into the 'pen and get comfortable in that role -- if that is the role. And so again, that's why we have to be really thoughtful with that."
On Wednesday night, the benefit of having additional rotation depth in Sasaki became clear when Blake Snell exited his start against the Reds after just one inning due to left groin tightness. Removing him from the game was seen as more of a precautionary move, but it exposed the somewhat tenuous state of the Dodgers' starting pitching at present.
If the projected postseason rotation of Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Tarik Skubal, Snell and Tyler Glasnow remain healthy, then the Dodgers will be in a great place. But there are question marks behind the Big Four. Shohei Ohtani will not pitch again this season. Justin Wrobleski moved to the bullpen and has been much shakier in the second half. Emmet Sheehan, who's currently with Triple-A Oklahoma City, is trending upward after his two most recent starts in the Majors -- but has been inconsistent overall.
Yamamoto is the only member of L.A.'s rotation who has not missed a start this season. Both Skubal and Snell had surgery to remove loose bodies from their left elbows. Glasnow spent more than three months on the IL due to lower back spasms, a recurring issue for him. The Dodgers have been proactive with managing Glasnow's back, as Roberts said he flew back to L.A. early to cut out an additional flight segment in between last Saturday's start in Miami and his next scheduled start on Friday.
Should anything happen to those four, Sasaki would figure to be the next arm up in the rotation. Sasaki has broken out in his second Major League season, even though his 5-5 record and 4.60 ERA may seem underwhelming at first glance. After a shaky start to the campaign, Sasaki introduced a new splitter and began to consistently throw his fastball harder, helping him achieve sustainable success as a starter. He posted a 2.63 ERA in seven starts before the blister issue arose.
Because Sasaki is returning from an injury, there may be some rust for him to knock off. He is still pitching with the blister, but Roberts said he felt good after covering it with Dermabond in his most recent bullpen session and simulated game.
"It's playable," Roberts said. "Given the Dermabond, the time that he'll have in between this next outing, the hope is that it's dang near close to being healed."
The Dodgers expect Sasaki to play an important role on their postseason pitching staff, even though they're not sure which role he'll fulfill -- but it is easier to shorten him up to pitch in relief rather than have to build him back up to start. After the latest injury concern, opting to keep starting on the table for Sasaki has already proven wise.

item.content:encoded:
LOS ÁNGELES (AP) — Tarik Skubal lanzó hasta la octava entrada, Teoscar Hernández conectó un sencillo que impulsó la carrera de la ventaja en la quinta y los Dodgers de Los Ángeles resistieron ante los Rojos de Cincinnati para imponerse el martes 3-2 e hilar su sexto triunfo.
El dominicano Hernández se fue de 3-3 con una base por bolas y batea para .484 en sus últimos nueve juegos. Will Smith conectó un jonrón temprano por los líderes del Oeste de la Liga Nacional.
El astro de los Dodgers, Shohei Ohtani, tuvo la noche libre para descansar por persistentes molestias en la rodilla y el bíceps. Freddie Freeman se fue de 4-0 con tres ponches como bateador designado en lugar de Ohtani.
Skubal (9-7) permitió dos carreras y cuatro hits en 7 1/3 entradas. Ponchó a cinco y dio dos bases por bolas.
Los Dodgers han ganado en cada una de sus últimas cuatro aperturas.
Desde que se unió al club justo antes de la fecha límite de canjes del 3 de agosto, el pitcher ganador en dos ocasiones del Premio Cy Young de la Liga Americana tiene marca de 2-2 con efectividad de 2,84 y 48 ponches contra 10 bases por bolas en siete aperturas.
Tanner Scott lanzó la novena para acreditarse su 22º salvamento.
Deportes AP: https://apnews.com/hub/deportes

item.title: [sports.yahoo.com] Andrew Friedman Comments on Shohei Ohtani’s Injury Recovery Ahead of MLB Playoffs
item.dc:creator: Miracle Dimwesh
item.description: The Los Angeles Dodgers received an encouraging update on Shohei Ohtani as they prepare for the postseason. Dodgers president of baseball operations Andrew Friedman said Ohtani is "progressing well" after recently resuming light baseball activities. Friedman also said he expects the two-way star to return during the regular season. Ohtani has been sidelined since the Dodgers placed him on the 15-day injured list with right biceps inflammation and left knee swelling. The move was backdated to Sep
item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers received an encouraging update on Shohei Ohtani as they prepare for the postseason.
Dodgers president of baseball operations Andrew Friedman said Ohtani is "progressing well" after recently resuming light baseball activities. Friedman also said he expects the two-way star to return during the regular season.
Ohtani has been sidelined since the Dodgers placed him on the 15-day injured list with right biceps inflammation and left knee swelling. The move was backdated to Sept. 8, making him eligible to return Sept. 23.
#Dodgers Andrew Friedman said Shohei Ohtani is “progressing well” since starting to swing a bat earlier this week. Ohtani will be eligible to come off IL on Wednesday.
Friedman: “I expect him back in the regular season.”
How many ABs? Friedman shrugged
Ohtani took his first swings off a tee earlier this week without discomfort. The next steps in his progression are expected to include tracking pitches and eventually facing live pitching as he works to regain his timing.
The Dodgers have reason to be cautious with the veteran as they prepare for October. Ohtani has already made 14 starts as a pitcher this season, going 8-2 with a 1.79 ERA and 95 strikeouts in 85.2 innings.
He has also remained a major part of Los Angeles' lineup when healthy. Ohtani is batting .277 with 30 home runs, 80 RBI, 11 stolen bases and a .380 on-base percentage through 130 games.
His absence has come at an important point in the season, but the Dodgers now have some flexibility after clinching the National League West with an 8-2 win over the Cincinnati Reds.
That gives Los Angeles an opportunity to prioritize Ohtani's recovery rather than rushing him back. Friedman did not provide a specific number of at-bats Ohtani will receive before the postseason.
For now, the Dodgers will continue monitoring his progress while gradually increasing his baseball activities. Ohtani's potential return before October gives the club another important storyline to follow during the final days of the regular season.
ALSO SEE: NRFI and YRFI MLB Bets Today: Best First-Inning Predictions for Thursday, Sept. 17

Edwin Díaz is expected to be activated on Friday, and Andy Pages may not be far behind. Dodgers manager Dave Roberts did not specify a date for his All-Star outfielder but said Pages was “very likely” to return during the homestand. Pages has been on the injured list since Aug. 22 due to a left hand fra
item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers are returning for their final homestand of the 2026 regular season as National League West champions and on the verge of getting reinforcements back from the injured list.
Edwin Díaz is expected to be activated on Friday, and Andy Pages may not be far behind. Dodgers manager Dave Roberts did not specify a date for his All-Star outfielder but said Pages was “very likely” to return during the homestand.
Pages has been on the injured list since Aug. 22 due to a left hand fracture. He underwent a procedure that involved inserting a screw into his left hand to accelerate the recovery process without extending the recovery timeline.
Thus, the expectation remained Pages would be back with the Dodgers in four to five weeks from the time of suffering the injury. An additional note is that Pages will forego a rehab assignment prior to getting activated.
The 25-year-old has been swinging a bat over the past several days and took a step forward on Tuesday by hitting off a pitching machine. He then advanced to taking at-bats against the Trajekt machine.
Tommy Edman stepped up in place of Andy Pages
Alek Thomas initially received the bulk of starts in center field but was removed from the roster on Sept. 1 as part of multiple moves.
Since then Tommy Edman has been an effective replacement in center field, but getting Pages back lets the Dodgers get their best nine players in the lineup just in time for the postseason.
Edman’s ability to play all over the field has long been valued by the Dodgers. It was a strong motivation for his acquisition from the St. Louis Cardinals at the 2024 trade deadline and a subsequent contract extension that offseason.
But Edman’s versatility has been even more so valuable lately with Shohei Ohtani and Pages sidelined. Roberts lauded Edman for his ability to impact a game with his glove and bat.
The 31-year-old said he takes pride in doing his best to fill the void left by Pages’ absence.
Now with Pages on the verge of returning, the Dodgers will likely move Edman back to second base but also have the option of further leveraging his positional versatility if needed.

item.title: [True Blue LA] Dodgers notes: Kyle Tucker, Shohei Ohtani, Tarik Skubal

item.content:encoded:
The NL West continues to run through Los Angeles, as the Dodgers clinched their 13th division title over the last 14 seasons with an 8-2 victory over the Cincinnati Reds on Thursday.
The Dodgers secured their 93rd win— matching their regular season total from last year— thanks in large part to a huge game from Kyle Tucker. Tucker launched his second home run of the four-game set in Cincinnati and collected four hits in five at-bats, finishing just a triple shy of the cycle. For what has undoubtedly been a disappointing first year with his new team, Tucker gave fans a prelude for what they can potentially see from him in October.
Tucker spoke with David Vassegh of SportsNet LA while celebrating their division-clinching win about settling for a double in his final at-bat, noting he wouldn’t have made it safely to third base in his cycle pursuit.
“I tried my best. I don’t think I was going to get there. I probably would’ve been thrown out halfway, but it’s all good.”
Tucker also spoke about the challenges and hurdles he faced repeatedly this season, expressing gratitude for his teammates continuing to stick with him throughout the highs and lows.
“This group is awesome. Everyone supports each other through the ups and downs. We all know where we want to be at the end of the year, and we all just try to help each other out to get there. This is a great group to play with, to play behind, so everyone is super supportive. Everyone knows what we gotta get done.”
With only nine games left for the Dodgers in the regular season, team president of baseball operations Andrew Friedman gave an optimistic update on Shohei Ohtani, noting that they expect him to return from the injured list before their season finale, per Jack Harris of the California Post.
“He’s doing well,” Friedman said, as the team celebrated another National League West title around him at Great American Ball Park. “He’s progressing well.”
“I expect him back in the regular season,” Friedman declared.
Two months ago, Tarik Skubal was still the ace of a Detroit Tigers team on a downward trajectory. On Thursday, Skubal was celebrating the opportunity to pitch in the postseason for a third consecutive season, this time for the reigning two-time World Series champions.
Skubal hopes that the celebrations from Thursday were the first of many more to come as the march for the three-peat is officially in motion, per Maddie Lee of the Los Angeles Times.
“First of many,” he said. “… This is checking a box, and once we get to postseason baseball and doing all that stuff, I think it’s going to be a ton of fun.”
Skubal also reflected on the resiliency of this year’s Dodgers, noting their ability to bounce back after a rough month of August with a current record of 11-5 in the month of September, per Sonja Chen of MLB.com.
“I think there was no panic from this group,” Skubal said. “I think that’s why in big moments, pressure doesn’t really get to these guys.”

item.content:encoded:
Happy Friday, everyone! Lots of little news bites to keep you busy this morning while you’re pretending to do work, or just enjoying your coffee. We look at some of the Mets’ woes, from terrible offseason choices, to their fanbase missing Pete Alonso, to a new and rough-looking injury. We also check in on some injured superstars, as Shohei Ohtani is feeling a little closer to normal, while Aaron Judge was pulled from a game. Uh oh.
We’ll also see which MLB managers might want to start refreshing their resumes, update you on the WPBL postseason, and share the cutest first pitch ever.
Let’s just get right into it.
- Davy Andrews has a fun article that aims to help the TV action character Reacher find better baseball aliases to use at shady motels. Fans of the show will get a kick out of this.
- Tom Verducci spotlights Tarik Skubal and how he’s going to be a difference-maker for the Dodgers this postseason.
- Verducci also looks at a change the Dodgers made to Skubal’s approach on the mound.
- It’s not time to start worrying about Jesus Luzardo’s arm… yet. Story by Michael Baumann.
- The Dodgers have clinched their 13th NL West title in 14 years. Story by Sonja Chen.
- Jessica Camerato reports that the Nationals are in extension talks with Cade Cavalli.
- Fabian Ardaya shares that Shohei Ohtani is feeling “normal…ish”. (The Athletic subscription required.)
- Karl Rasmussen breaks down seven terrible offseason moves the Mets made that could ruin their future.
- Food for thought, what if divisions were arranged by payroll?
- The return of Pete Alonso to Citi Field has Mets fans turning against their own team. Story by Jay Jaffe.
- Kiri Oler keeps us up to date on the advancing WPBL postseason.
- Keith Law admits which prospects he was wrong about. (The Athletic subscription required.)
- The Phillies have claimed Jose Urquidy off waivers from the White Sox. (MLB)
- Brian Murphy looks at six numbers that have defined the Rays’ tremendous season.
- Karl Rasmussen looks at the 10 biggest breakout stars of the 2026 season.
- The Yankees pulled Aaron Judge in the sixth inning of Thursday’s game against the Twins due to lower leg tightness. (ESPN)
- Ken Rosenthal thinks these six managerial positions are the ones most at risk right now. (The Athletic subscription required.)
- Most adorable first pitch EVER.
- Jared Greenspan shares that A’s prospect Ryan Lasko, who was paralyzed in an outfield collision, has been released from his rehab facility, receiving a standing ovation from the clinic’s staff.
- Davy Andrews explains why we won’t be seeing a pitcher join the 120 club this season.
- Ben Clemens tries to make sense of Fernando Tatis Jr’s up and down season.
- Keegan Matheson looks at the personal connection behind George Springer’s Clemente Award nomination.
- How Tommy Pham made a literal elevator pitch to get activated by the White Sox and then immediately made it worth their while. Story by Karl Rasmussen.
- Mets’ Jared Young was carted off the field last night following a collision with one of his teammates. (ESPN)
- Brittany Ghiroli and Sam Blum explain why the sale of the Angels will be unlike anything else we ever see again. (The Athletic subscription required.)
- This is tremendous.
And tomorrow will be a better day than today, Buster. Make it so.

item.title: [Yardbarker] 'Something Special': Dave Roberts’ Clear Message After Dodgers Secure 5th Straight Title
item.dc:creator: Sourav Kumar Ghatak
item.description: “Before this season started, they said the Dodgers were ruining baseball. Let’s get four more wins and really ruin baseball!” Dave Roberts set the tone after the Dodgers won the 2025 NLCS to enter the World Series. item.content:encoded:
“Before this season started, they said the Dodgers were ruining baseball. Let’s get four more wins and really ruin baseball!” Dave Roberts set the tone after the Dodgers won the 2025 NLCS to enter the World Series. This time, Roberts didn’t ask to ruin baseball but hoped for something that, incidentally, would be a first in franchise history.
The New York Yankees and the Oakland Athletics are the only two teams in MLB to have a three-peat record. Despite recent dominance of the Dodgers, including winning the NL West title for five straight seasons, a three-peat record is what they still manifest. Winning the World Series in 2026 would thus get the last two seasons’ winners into the exclusive club, and Roberts may just have communicated the same emotion.
“To win 11 games in October, you never know who is gonna be the guy, what that moment is gonna fall to, and many people have lived it in this clubhouse. So my ask is, be ready to be that guy. And like I said, we’re the most talented, we’re the smartest players, we’re the toughest players, and we’re the most hungry. Again, we have something to do unprecedented, and again, 2026 is gonna be something special. So let’s keep the blinders on and celebrate this,” FOX Sports: MLB quoted Roberts after the win over the Reds on Thursday.
The Dodgers secured the 2026 NL West title on Thursday, which was incidentally their 13th in the last 14 seasons. No wonder the team had a champagne bath to celebrate their achievement, but not before their manager took the stage to set the tone for their playoff run.
Achieving a three-peat was what the Dodgers targeted before entering the 2026 season. The 2024 and 2025 World Series winners had no other motivation than to win their third straight. Hence, achieving what would be a first in franchise history would understandably make this season special.
The Dodgers ended their 2025 regular season with a 93-69 record compared to a 93-60 record this season. So, the team is already dominating much better than last season, and what makes it even more special is how the struggling stars were performing in clutch time.
Since the Dodgers splashed $240 million to sign Kyle Tucker in 2026, criticisms have followed him. A .232 season was not what was expected from him in white and blue. However, the former Astros star is surging just at the right time. On Thursday, his four-hit performance helped the Dodgers get over the Reds and clinch their NL West title. Tucker is now 12-for-29 (.414) with four homers over his last eight games.
Furthermore, after a positive update about Shohei Ohtani’s injury, the Dodgers couldn’t ask for more.
“He is back to progress today,” Roberts said Thursday. “He should be getting some coach pitch this week. He’s progressing well; there’s no pain. He’s doing everything he needs to do. I still don’t know when he’ll return, but everything that I hear is really positive.”
The Dodgers fans thus have all the reasons to hope for a three-peat record in 2026.

item.title: [mlb.com] Tucker's near-cycle clinches LA's 5th straight NL West title, 13th in 14 years

item.content:encoded:
CINCINNATI -- Try as they might to view 2026 as its own season, everything the Dodgers have done this year is impossible to separate from the larger context of what they have accomplished in more than a decade of excellence.
The Dodgers hit another key milestone in their title defense by reclaiming the NL West crown with an 8-2 victory over the Reds on Thursday afternoon at Great American Ball Park. Three days after their traditional champagne toast in honor of clinching a postseason berth, winning the West brought on a wild clubhouse celebration -- which they hope will be the first of many over the next several weeks.
"You get so mired in each year, it’s hard to have any perspective," president of baseball operations Andrew Friedman said. "We’ve had our share of troubles this year. Things where we had to work harder than we expected on a couple of fronts. But the important thing is how we finish and how we go into October."
In their record-tying 14 consecutive postseason appearances, the Dodgers have 13 division titles. The only team to unseat them was the 2021 Giants, who edged them in one of the most highly contested NL West races in recent memory.
Since divisional play began in 1969, the Dodgers lead all big league teams with 24 division titles, one more than the Braves -- currently in line to win the NL East -- and three more than the Yankees. Each year's achievements raise the bar for every ensuing year. The expectations facing the Dodgers have become nearly impossible to meet. But they've embraced them gladly.
"There is certainly a higher expectation when, if you don't win the World Series, you fail," manager Dave Roberts said. "But that's kind of part of what you signed up with the Dodgers.”
The Dodgers' offense, whose inconsistency has been a perpetual concern over the course of the season, provided plenty of early support to back a scheduled bullpen game. Kyle Tucker led the way with a four-hit, three-RBI showing, finishing a triple shy of the Dodgers’ first cycle since 2017. Freddie Freeman, Max Muncy, Josue De Paula and Miguel Rojas also knocked in runs.
Justin Wrobleski opened the bullpen game with three perfect innings, and while Blake Treinen surrendered a solo home run in the fourth, Landon Knack pitched four scoreless frames before Seth Halvorsen allowed a run in the ninth.
With nine games remaining in the regular season, the Dodgers are far from full strength. Their best hitter, Shohei Ohtani, is on the 15-day IL, as is first-time All-Star Andy Pages. The six-man rotation they carried for most of the season has been reduced to four fully stretched-out starters on the active roster, necessitating Thursday's bullpen game.
"It's been the same thing the last couple years," Muncy said. "We've had guys go down. We've had guys step up in their place. … That's all that we ask, and we've been able to survive a lot."
The Dodgers are expecting reinforcements back before the postseason, and would greatly benefit from securing a first-round bye to advance directly to the NL Division Series -- giving them five days off after the end of the regular season. They hold a four-game lead over the Braves for the No. 2 seed in the National League.
This edition of the Dodgers is not without its flaws, but then again, neither were the back-to-back champion teams in 2024 and '25. After becoming the first team in a quarter-century to defend their title last year, they will vie for the Majors' first three-peat since the 1998-2000 Yankees.
While the talk of a three-peat began almost from the moment the Dodgers became back-to-back champions last November, Roberts urged his team to stay focused on the present while keeping the larger goal in mind. In his annual speech on the first day of full-squad workouts during Spring Training, he delivered the following message: Be a greyhound, looking forward with blinders on.
Tarik Skubal was not a Dodger when Roberts gave his spring address, but he saw the message play out after he was dealt to L.A. ahead of the Trade Deadline. He arrived at the beginning of a season-high seven-game losing streak -- and the tough stretch gave him a feel for the culture that has led to his new team's sustained success.
"I think there was no panic from this group," Skubal said. "I think that’s why in big moments, pressure doesn't really get to these guys."
The Dodgers have a long road ahead as they look to get back to the World Series, but it bears similarities to the roads they have traveled before. The slate might be wiped clean every year, but they have experience weathering the challenges along the way to the promised land.
"It's a different year, but I think it's kind of the same," Mookie Betts said. "The same group of guys. We know what to expect. We know what to expect from each other. It's the same goal every year. Getting here, you can't really get too focused on how, as long as you get there."

漢字サイン、「ゴールドMLBロゴマン」のパッチ付き
米オークション会社「ザ・リアレスト」は17日、ドジャースの大谷翔平投手が2025年3月18日に東京ドームで行われた東京シリーズ開幕戦で着用したユニホームをオークションに出品すると発表した。大谷にとって日本でプレーした初のメジャー公式戦の実使用品で、近代の野球ユニホームとして史上最高額、数億円規模での落札が見込まれている。
ユニホームには、前年のMVP受賞者らにのみ着用が許される公式戦初の「ゴールドMLBロゴマン」パッチが付いているほか、背番号付近には直筆の漢字サイン（大谷翔平）や「Opening Day Tokyo Series」「NL MVP」などの手書きの添え書きが施されている。
同社によると、入札は専用サイトですでに開始されており、10月17日に締め切られる。大谷に関連するメモラビリアを巡っては、同試合で着用したスパイクが約44万ドル（約6500万円）で落札されるなど、世界的な高値取引が続いている。
（Full-Count編集部）

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Dodgers take down Reds to capture fifth consecutive NL West crown, 13th in past 14 seasons
item.dc:creator: Andy Backstrom

item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers were already playoff-bound for the 14th straight season. But after taking down the Cincinnati Reds 8-2 on Thursday, they're winners of the NL West for the 13th time in that span and for the fifth season in a row.
Of course, the streak LA cares about most will be at stake in the postseason. The Dodgers are aiming to become the first team to three-peat as World Series champions since the fabled New York Yankees of 1998-2000.
With the victory Thursday, the Dodgers (93-60) have the second-best record in the NL, behind only the Milwaukee Brewers (95-58), who clinched the NL Central earlier this week but dropped their series finale to the Pirates on Thursday. The Dodgers and Brewers will jockey for the NL's top seed over the final week of the regular season.
Meanwhile, LA will do its best to sort out an injury-riddled roster before the calendar flips to October. Most notably, the status of Shohei Ohtani will be acutely monitored, as the two-way star has been juggling issues with his biceps, left knee and neck.
Then there's lefty starting pitcher Blake Snell, who's dealing with a groin injury that ended his start Wednesday versus the Reds after just one inning.
Andy Pages is expected back in the Dodgers' outfield soon. However, only time will tell how quickly he returns to form after healing from a fractured left hand.
A bullpen game and a flurry of early scoring sealed the NL West in Cincy
LA didn't need one of its aces to secure the division title on Thursday. Manager Dave Roberts, who has overseen 10 of the Dodgers' NL West crowns amid this memorable run, opted for a bullpen game.
Lefty Justin Wrobleski spun three innings of shutout ball. He was the first to punch out Reds shortstop Elly De La Cruz, who clocked out with three Ks on the day. Cincinnati's lone run came in the fourth, when Sal Stewart homered off Dodgers right-handed hurler Blake Treinen.
Then righty Landon Knack registered four scoreless innings while allowing four hits. Seth Halvorsen finished the game while allowing one more Reds run to score in the ninth.
That merely made a dent in LA's commanding lead. The Dodgers built that in large part thanks to a trio of extra-base hits. Kyle Tucker went yard in the first inning, depositing a two-run dinger. He also hit an RBI double in the second. In the fourth, Max Muncy drove home a pair of runs with a two-bagger.
The Reds and Dodgers traded runs in the ninth, with Miguel Rojas taking one deep to put the exclamation point on LA's division-clinching victory.

item.title: [Sports Illustrated] Es hora de que Shohei Ohtani renuncie al pitcheo de manera definitiva
item.dc:creator: Ryan Phillips
item.description: Lo que hace de Shohei Ohtani el jugador más extraordinario en la historia de MLB podría ser también su único defecto fatal. item.content:encoded:
Lo que hace de Shohei Ohtani el jugador más extraordinario en la historia de MLB podría ser también su único defecto fatal.
A diferencia de cualquier jugador que haya existido antes que él, Ohtani puede dominar en el plato y en el montículo, pero ha llegado el momento de decidir si lanzar vale la pena por el desgaste que ha provocado en su cuerpo.
Te puede interesar: La decisión de los Dodgers de descansar a Shohei Ohtani como pitcher es la correcta
Los Dodgers colocaron a Ohtani en la lista de lesionados la semana pasada debido a lesiones en la rodilla y el bíceps que han persistido durante meses. Los problemas de rodilla comenzaron oficialmente el 11 de junio, mientras que el problema en el bíceps existe desde algún momento de mayo. No ha realizado una apertura desde el 3 de julio y cada vez que intentaba aumentar su carga de trabajo para regresar, el problema de rodilla generaba un estrés adicional en el bíceps, frenando su progreso. Es muy poco probable que vuelva a subir al montículo esta temporada.
Francamente, no deberíamos volver a verlo lanzar.
Sería una decisión difícil, por decir lo menos. En 14 aperturas esta temporada, Ohtani ha sido dominante. Tiene marca de 8–2, con efectividad de 1.79, WHIP de 0.95 y 95 strikeouts contra 26 bases por bolas en 85 ⅔ innings. Generó 2.9 fWAR como pitcher esta temporada, su mayor cifra desde 2022, cuando realizó 28 aperturas, la mayor cantidad de su carrera. Se nos ha recordado la increíble capacidad que lo convirtió en la primera auténtica estrella de dos vías de este deporte. Desafortunadamente, mantener esa capacidad ha tenido un costo en repetidas ocasiones.
Ohtani ha sufrido una larga lista de lesiones a lo largo de los años mientras intentaba ser un pitcher abridor de tiempo completo y un bateador de todos los días. Esos esfuerzos anteriormente no habían afectado sus capacidades en el plato, pero ahora que tiene 32 años, parece que eso ha comenzado a suceder.
Ohtani ha estado intentando regresar al montículo desde aquella apertura del 3 de julio y su producción como bateador ha disminuido desde entonces. En 49 partidos, registra una línea ofensiva de .259/.342/.518, con 12 home runs, 30 carreras impulsadas y un wRC+ de 127. La mayoría de los demás jugadores de MLB estarían encantados con esos resultados, pero su OPS de .860 durante ese periodo está muy por debajo de las marcas superiores a 1.000 que registró en cada una de las tres temporadas anteriores. Su wRC+ en ese periodo sería el más bajo desde 2020 y casi 50 puntos menor que el de la temporada pasada (172). La lesión de rodilla también ha limitado la velocidad que lo ayudó a robar 59 bases hace dos años. Este año solo suma 11 en 14 intentos.
Las lesiones relacionadas con el pitcheo ya se estaban acumulando durante las primeras temporadas de Ohtani en Estados Unidos. Después de 10 aperturas en 2018, sufrió un desgarro del ligamento colateral ulnar de su brazo derecho y necesitó una cirugía Tommy John. No lanzó en absoluto en 2019 y, cuando regresó al año siguiente, sufrió una distensión del flexor después de dos aperturas y no volvió a lanzar.
En 2021 y 2022 estuvo mayormente saludable y realizó 51 aperturas combinadas sin problemas importantes. A eso le siguieron 23 aperturas en 2023 antes de volver a sufrir un desgarro del UCL y someterse a su segunda cirugía importante de codo en cinco años. No lanzó al año siguiente y regresó al montículo después de casi dos años en 2025, cuando lanzó 47 innings en 14 aperturas. Esta temporada, ni siquiera llegó a los 90 innings antes de volver a ser apartado.
Ohtani está en su novena temporada en MLB y ha lanzado 614 ⅓ innings en su carrera; 428 ⅓ llegaron durante un periodo de tres años entre 2021 y 2023. Eso significa que casi 70% de sus innings de carrera se produjeron durante esas tres temporadas. En sus otras seis campañas combinadas, solo ha lanzado 186 innings.
Cuando Ohtani no está en el montículo, sigue siendo uno de los dos bateadores más valiosos del planeta, junto con Aaron Judge. Cuando está saludable, destroza a los pitchers rivales. Ganó un MVP en 2024 sin lanzar un solo pitch y volvió a ganarlo en 2025 a pesar de lanzar apenas 47 innings. ¿La lección? No necesita estar en el montículo para ser uno de los mejores jugadores del beisbol.
A medida que envejece, el desgaste físico de continuar lanzando se vuelve cada vez más difícil de justificar. Esta temporada es simplemente el ejemplo más reciente. Sigue siendo un jugador de nivel All-Star, pero no ha sido sobrehumano. Los Dodgers no le pagaron $700 millones para ver cómo su mayor habilidad se deteriora mientras persigue inútilmente más innings.
Ohtani lanzó a nivel de as esta temporada cuando estuvo en el montículo y, de haber mantenido ese ritmo, habría estado en la pelea por el Cy Young de la Liga Nacional. En lugar de perseguir un nuevo reconocimiento, el cuatro veces MVP ahora está en la lista de lesionados mientras se acercan los playoffs. Es la misma historia que hemos visto una y otra vez, con pequeñas variaciones, desde que debutó en MLB. Las exigencias físicas de ser tanto pitcher abridor como bateador de todos los días simplemente podrían ser demasiado para que su cuerpo las soporte.
A estas alturas, la única solución es que Ohtani deje de lanzar y se concentre en ser bateador. Incluso si los Dodgers encontraran de alguna manera la forma de reducir su carga de trabajo como pitcher, todavía tendría que prepararse como lanzador todos los días. Ohtani tendría que realizar sesiones de bullpen, mantener su programa habitual de pitcheo y preparar su codo derecho, operado quirúrgicamente en dos ocasiones, para lanzar a 100 mph cada pocos días. Esa es la carga que repetidamente ha descarrilado su carrera como pitcher.
Los Dodgers no necesitan que Ohtani lance. Tienen una rotación repleta de talento encabezada por Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Blake Snell, Tyler Glasnow y, por el momento, Tarik Skubal. Snell y Glasnow han tenido problemas para mantenerse en el montículo, pero ambos tienen contrato al menos hasta la próxima temporada. Mientras tanto, jugadores como Justin Wrobleski, Emmet Sheehan y Roki Sasaki proporcionan profundidad adicional para la rotación. El pitcheo de Ohtani es un lujo del que Los Angeles puede darse el lujo de prescindir.
Durante años, Ohtani ha maravillado al beisbol con sus enormes home runs, velocidades de salida de otro mundo y actuaciones ofensivas que el juego nunca había visto antes. Su capacidad para lanzar lo hizo único, pero ya no vale la pena correr el riesgo. Su experimento de dos vías fue una de las hazañas más impresionantes en la historia del deporte. Continuarlo no vale la pena si eso significa perder la magia que puede crear con un bat en las manos.
En el plato, Ohtani es un superhéroe. En el montículo, es frágil. Ya no tiene sentido arriesgar al Ohtani bateador por tener la posibilidad de contar con el Ohtani pitcher.
Ohtani podría ser el Ícaro del beisbol. Aquello que lo hizo milagroso podría terminar siendo lo que lo haga volver a tocar tierra.
La diferencia es que Ohtani puede alejarse de su defecto fatal antes de que se convierta en su caída.
Publicado originalmente en www.sportsillustrated.com el 15/09/2026, traducido al español para SI México.

item.title: [sports.yahoo.com] When is Shohei Ohtani coming back? Dodgers reveal injury update
item.dc:creator: Gabe Lacques; USA TODAY
item.description: Andrew Friedman, the Los Angeles Dodgers' president of baseball operations, told reporters in Cincinnati that he expects Shohei Ohtani will return during the club's final nine games of the regular season. item.content:encoded:
Andrew Friedman, the Los Angeles Dodgers' president of baseball operations, told reporters in Cincinnati that he expects Shohei Ohtani will return during the club's final nine games of the regular season.
Speaking after the champagne celebration that followed the club's 8-2 victory over the Cincinnati Reds that clinched the National League West, Friedman said of Ohtani, "I expect him back in the regular season."
The four-time MVP and two-way superstar will not pitch this season due to right biceps and left knee injuries, and he has not been in the Dodgers lineup since Sept. 7, after which he was placed on the 15-day injured list. Ohtani sat out five games before giving that one a go, and he had just six hits in 49 at-bats (.122) with no home runs in his final 61 plate appearances.
Much of that span was spent trying to also return as a pitcher, before a bullpen session on Aug. 28 was cut short. The club is hoping his focus on playing one side of the ball enables his body not only to heal, but hold up as the Dodgers aim for a third consecutive World Series title.
For the season, Ohtani is batting .277 with 30 home runs and a .902 OPS, and will likely cede his two-year reign as NL MVP to the Chicago Cubs' Pete Crow-Armstrong.
This article originally appeared on USA TODAY: When is Shohei Ohtani coming back? Dodgers reveal injury update

item.content:encoded:
Los Dodgers vuelven a reinar en el Oeste de la Nacional y buscan un tricampeonato pese a lesiones
CINCINNATI — Los Dodgers de Los Ángeles aseguraron su quinto título consecutivo de la División Oeste de la Liga Nacional y el 13ro en las últimas 14 temporadas al vencer el jueves 8-2 a los Rojos de Cincinnati.
“Es algo muy importante. Creo que mucha gente piensa que es solo un rito de paso (pero) no es fácil”, declaró el mánager de los Dodgers Dave Roberts. “Así que es algo de lo que todos estamos muy orgullosos, pero entendemos claramente que ese no es el objetivo final”.
Los Dodgers (93-60) disputarán los playoffs por 14 temporada consecutiva, con lo que igualan el récord que los Bravos de Atlanta establecieron de 1991-2005.
“Es el primer paso”, dijo Mookie Betts mientras se secaba el champán de los ojos. “Nos queda un largo camino por recorrer”.
La celebración en el terreno de juego fue algo calmada tras el último out el jueves. Pero los jugadores se soltaron en el vestuario, donde el champán y la cerveza salpicaron desde el suelo hasta el techo.
“Creo que es una de esas situaciones en las que, como en el béisbol se juega a diario, los jugadores se centran en rendir”, dijo Roberts. “Así que no hay muchos momentos para celebrar. Por eso es agradable ver a los chicos soltarse un poco”.
A pesar de todos sus laureles, los Dodgers creen que todavía tienen algo que demostrar.
El año pasado, el equipo pulverizó el récord de gasto de las Grandes Ligas con una nómina total de 515 millones de dólares, dando alas a críticas de que tienen una supuesta ventaja injusta.
“Lo que estamos creando aquí es especial”, afirmó Max Muncy. “Definitivamente no se le da el reconocimiento que merece. Todo el mundo se fija en la nómina, pero nunca hablamos de cómo hacemos las cosas bien, de cómo nos preparamos adecuadamente o de cómo cuidamos todos esos pequeños detalles. De eso no se habla”.
Los bicampeones defensores de la Serie Mundial aún pujan por el primer puesto de preclasificación de la Liga Nacional, que actualmente está en posesión de los Cerveceros de Milwaukee. Los Ángeles comenzó el día con una ventaja de tres juegos y medio sobre los Bravos (89-64) por el segundo puesto, pero está por detrás de los Cerveceros (95-57).
“Seguimos luchando por uno de los dos primeros puestos”, dijo Roberts. “Creo que hacemos bien celebrando, pero sin dejar que eso afecte a lo que sigue. Tenemos que tomar el vuelo y jugar contra los Gigantes mañana”.
Los Dodgers buscan convertirse en el primer equipo en conquistar tres campeonatos consecutivos de la Serie Mundial desde que los Yankees lo lograron de 1998 a 2000.
Este es el cuarto título divisional asegurado más temprano para los Dodgers. Aseguraron el Oeste de la Liga Nacional el 10 de septiembre de 2019, el 13 de septiembre de 2022 y el 16 de septiembre de 2023.
Los Ángeles aprovechará ese tiempo para recuperar lesionados. Eso empieza con Shohei Ohtani.
El cuatro veces Jugador Más Valioso ha estado en la lista de lesionados de 15 días desde el 8 de septiembre por una inflamación en el bíceps derecho y les dijo a los reporteros a principios de este mes que ya no lanzará más en lo que resta de temporada. La estrella de dos vías hizo swings desde un tee por primera vez el martes y se sintió bien. Se espera que regrese como bateador antes de que termine la temporada regular, aunque no está claro si podrá llegar al 100% de salud antes de octubre.
Roki Sasaki, en la lista de lesionados por una ampolla en el dedo medio, lanzó en una práctica de bateo en vivo el miércoles en Cincinnati y salió bien. Roberts indicó que su próxima aparición será como abridor.
Blake Snell salió prematuramente de la apertura del miércoles después de un inning por rigidez en la ingle izquierda. Su situación es incierta.
Se espera que el cerrador puertorriqueño Edwin Díaz, quien ha estado en la lista de lesionados desde agosto por una inflamación en el cuello, sea activado el viernes. El venezolano Edgardo Henríquez, un preparador de mesa en el bullpeb, está en la lista de lesionados por molestias en la parte baja de la espalda. Se le realizó una resonancia magnética en Los Ángeles el miércoles, que reveló una distensión lumbar, y su rehabilitación se pausará por unos días.
El primera base Freddie Freeman, aquejado por dolor en la rodilla derecha, regresó a la alineación el martes y cortó una mala racha de 3 hits en 30 turnos con tres imparables. Sumó otros dos hits el jueves.
Los Dodgers protagonizaron el mayor impacto de la fecha límite de cambios al adquirir a Tarik Skubal, ganador en dos ocasiones del premio Cy Young de la Liga Americana, procedente de los Tigres. Skubal tiene marca de 3-2 con efectividad de 2.52 en ocho aperturas con los Dodgers.
La incorporación de Skubal convirtió a los Dodgers en los grandes favoritos en las apuestas para ganar la Serie Mundial. Pero después de comenzar la temporada con marca de 61-36, los Dodgers tienen registro de 31-24 desde la pausa del Juego de Estrellas.
Los Dodgers dejaron a 12 corredores en base y se fueron de 0 en 11 con corredores en posición de anotar en la derrota del miércoles ante los Reds, algo que, según Roberts, necesita mejorar.
“Se trata de poder rematar a los equipos cuando tenemos oportunidades. En la postemporada no se presentan muchas oportunidades. Hay que saber aprovecharlas”, dijo Roberts.
___

But while speaking to reporters Thursday after the Dodgers clinched their fifth straight NL West title, Friedman said Ohtani is on the me
item.content:encoded:
Although the Los Angeles Dodgers are playing without star Shohei Ohtani for the near future, Dodgers president of baseball operations Andrew Friedman thinks it won't be too long before Ohtani is able to make his return.
Ohtani landed on the injured list for the first time in his Dodgers tenure last week, going on the 15-day IL due to right biceps inflammation. But while speaking to reporters Thursday after the Dodgers clinched their fifth straight NL West title, Friedman said Ohtani is on the mend.
"He's doing well," Friedman said, via Jack Harris of the California Post. "He's progressing well."
When asked if Ohtani would be back in time to join the Dodgers in the playoffs, Friedman pointed to the two-way player returning even sooner: "I expect him back in the regular season," he said.
However, Friedman did not provide an answer when asked how many at-bats Ohtani is expected to take, via the Orange County Register's Bill Plunkett.
Because Ohtani's IL stint was backdated to Sept. 8, the earliest he's able to return to the Dodgers' lineup is Sept. 23. Los Angeles will have five games left in the regular season at that point.
Earlier this week, Ohtani took a few hits off a tee in his first swings since going on the IL. Dodgers manager Dave Roberts, like Friedman, said at the time that Ohtani was feeling "good" but that the team planned to give him a "consistent build-up."
Roberts did not have a specific return timetable in mind but, like Friedman, said he was hopeful that Ohtani could return before the postseason.
"Whether it happens or not is to be determined, but I do expect him to be back to play in some regular-season games," Roberts said. "I don't know how many."
With an 8-2 win over the Cincinnati Reds on Thursday, Los Angeles won the NL West for the 13th time in a 14-year span. The Dodgers had clinched a postseason berth earlier this week, marking the team's 14th consecutive year in the playoffs.

item.content:encoded:
Redacción FOX Deportes
Sin Shohei Ohtani, los Dodgers amarraron su quinto título divisional
El equipo angelino derrotó a los Cincinnati Reds y se colocó en una posición privilegiada
Los Angeles volvió a teñirse de fiesta al vencer 8-2 a los Cincinnati Reds. Con este triunfo, los Dodgers aseguraron su quinto título consecutivo de la División Oeste de la Liga Nacional. La ofensiva brilló gracias a Kyle Tucker, quien pegó home run y produjo tres carreras, junto a cuadrangulares de Miguel Rojas y producciones de Freddie Freeman, Max Muncy y Josué De Paula.
La hazaña cobra un valor aún más especial por las complejas circunstancias que rodeaban al equipo en el terreno. La superestrella japonesa Shohei Ohtani tuvo que ver la celebración desde la banca, marginado del line up tras ingresar a la lista de lesionados por molestias físicas. Sin la imponente presencia de su bateador designado titular, la alineación angelina tuvo que reinventarse y responder con contundencia en el momento exacto.
Ante la ausencia del fenómeno japonés, la profundidad del plantel asumió la responsabilidad de dar la cara por el proyecto. Bateadores de experiencia y jugadores de rol enlazaron turnos de alta calidad para sostener a la ofensiva en los momentos más tensos de la jornada. Paralelamente, el pitcheo dictó cátedra desde la loma para silenciar los bates rivales y mantener el control del encuentro de principio a fin.
Al caer el último out de la tarde, el vestidor estalló en júbilo para dar inicio al ya tradicional baño de champán. Este quinto banderín divisional al hilo confirma la jerarquía de una organización construida para sobreponerse a cualquier adversidad. Con el billete a octubre garantizado, Los Angeles envía un mensaje contundente a toda la liga de cara a la postemporada.
LO MÁS VISTO

item.title: [New York Post] Dodgers exec sets definitive expectation for Shohei Ohtani’s return
item.dc:creator: Jack Harris
item.description: CINCINNATI — Amid a champagne-spraying, speaker-blaring, beer-soaked clubhouse scene on Thursday afternoon, there was one matter of on-field business for Dodgers president of baseball operations Andrew Friedman to address. How was Shohei Ohtani doing in his recovery from right arm and left knee injuries? “He’s doing well,” Friedman said, as the team celebrated another National League West title around him at Great American Ball Park. “He’s progressing well.” Well enough for the two-way star — wh
item.content:encoded:
CINCINNATI — Amid a champagne-spraying, speaker-blaring, beer-soaked clubhouse scene on Thursday afternoon, there was one matter of on-field business for Dodgers president of baseball operations Andrew Friedman to address.
How was Shohei Ohtani doing in his recovery from right arm and left knee injuries?
“He’s doing well,” Friedman said, as the team celebrated another National League West title around him at Great American Ball Park. “He’s progressing well.”
Well enough for the two-way star — who was rehabbing back in Los Angeles during the club’s division-clinching road trip — to return before the beginning of the playoffs?
“I expect him back in the regular season,” Friedman declared.
Indeed, by all accounts from team officials over the last couple days, Ohtani has been taking encouraging steps forward as he aims to return from the injured list when eligible next Wednesday.
On Tuesday, Ohtani took his first swings since being removed from the active roster, beginning a hitting ramp-up with reps off a batting tee.
And after a day off from activities Wednesday, manager Dave Roberts said before Thursday’s game that the four-time MVP will advance to coach-pitch batting practice later this week.
“There’s no pain. He’s doing everything he needs to do,” Roberts said. “I still don’t know when [the] time to return to play is. But everything that I hear is really positive.”
Roberts described Ohtani as feeling “normal-ish” so far in his recovery work. He noted that the slugger has reported no recurrence of discomfort in his arm as he has begun building back up to a return to the field.
That doesn’t mean Ohtani will get back to 100% in time for October.
The ship on that likely sailed after he tried playing through his injuries, at least as a hitter, during the second half of the season — until it reached the point where he was showing visible signs of pain in multiple games earlier this month.
The Dodgers already know Ohtani won’t be able to pitch in the playoffs, after he endured repeated setbacks in his pitching progression despite not making an actual start since July 3.
They know he might still have to battle through his ailments at the plate in the playoffs, as the team attempts to complete a World Series three-peat.
Still, even having a relatively healthy version of Ohtani could weigh heavily in the team’s championship ambitions.
Not until he returns to action will they know exactly where he is at healthwise, after he suffered a 6-for-52 slump leading up to his IL placement.
But for now, they remain hopeful — of not only having Ohtani back by the start of the playoffs but increasingly likely even before then.

item.title: [www.noroeste.com.mx] Los Dodgers reconquistan el Oeste de la Liga Nacional y sellan su 14ª postemporada consecutiva

item.content:encoded:
Los Dodgers reconquistan el Oeste de la Liga Nacional y sellan su 14ª postemporada consecutiva
CINCINNATI._ Por más que intenten ver el 2026 como una temporada independiente, todo lo que los Dodgers han hecho este año es imposible de separar del contexto más amplio de lo que han logrado en más de una década de excelencia.
Catorce clasificaciones consecutivas a la postemporada. Cinco títulos divisionales seguidos. La inusual oportunidad de luchar por un tricampeonato de la Serie Mundial.
Los Dodgers alcanzaron otro hito importante en la defensa de su título al recuperar la corona del Oeste de la Liga Nacional con una victoria de 8-2 sobre los Rojos la tarde del jueves en el Great American Ball Park. Tres días después de su tradicional brindis con champaña para celebrar que aseguraron un lugar en la postemporada, conquistar el Oeste desató una eufórica celebración en el clubhouse, que esperan sea la primera de muchas durante las próximas semanas.
En sus 14 participaciones consecutivas en la postemporada, igualando un récord, los Dodgers han conquistado 13 títulos divisionales. El único equipo que logró destronarlos fueron los Gigantes del 2021, que los superaron por estrecho margen en una de las luchas por el Oeste de la Liga Nacional más reñidas de los últimos tiempos.
La ofensiva de los Dodgers, cuya inconsistencia ha sido una preocupación constante a lo largo de la temporada, brindó bastante respaldo desde temprano para apoyar un juego de bullpen programado. Kyle Tucker encabezó el ataque con cuatro hits y tres carreras impulsadas, quedándose a un triple de conseguir el primer ciclo de los Dodgers desde el 2017. Freddie Freeman, Max Muncy, el dominicano Josué De Paula y el venezolano Miguel Rojas también remolcaron anotaciones.
Justin Wrobleski abrió el juego de bullpen con tres innings perfectos, y aunque Blake Treinen permitió un jonrón solitario en el cuarto episodio, Landon Knack lanzó cuatro entradas en blanco antes de que Seth Halvorsen concediera una rayita en el noveno acto.
Con nueve juegos restantes en la temporada regular, los Dodgers están lejos de contar con todo su plantel. Su mejor bateador, Shohei Ohtani, está en la lista de lesionados de 15 días, al igual que el cubano Andy Pagés, llamado por primera vez al Juego de Estrellas. La rotación de seis abridores que utilizaron durante gran parte de la temporada se ha reducido a cuatro abridores completamente acondicionados en el róster activo, lo que hizo necesario recurrir a un juego de bullpen el jueves.
Los Dodgers esperan recuperar refuerzos antes de la postemporada y se beneficiarían enormemente de asegurar el descanso en la primera ronda para avanzar directamente a la Serie Divisional de la Liga Nacional, lo que les daría cinco días libres después del final de la temporada regular. Tienen una ventaja de 4.0 juegos sobre los Bravos por el segundo puesto de la Liga Nacional.
Esta versión de los Dodgers no está exenta de defectos, pero tampoco lo estuvieron los equipos campeones consecutivos del 2024 y 2025. Después de convertirse el año pasado en el primer equipo en un cuarto de siglo en defender con éxito su título, buscarán el primer tricampeonato de Grandes Ligas desde los Yanquis de 1998 al 2000.
“Tenemos tanta hambre como en el 2024 y 2025”, dijo el piloto Dave Roberts. “Esta es una temporada aparte. Nuestros muchachos lo entienden”.
(Con información de MLB)

item.dc:creator: TJ French

item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers, like all other 29 MLB teams, have around 10 games left on the schedule.
LA already knows it will be headed to October, but the Dodgers are still aiming to clinch the NL West, which could happen on Thursday afternoon.
As the Dodgers gear up for October, one of the biggest storylines surrounding the team is who will close games out.
Edwin Diaz was signed to be the team's closer, but he's had inconsistency problems. On Thursday, during their series with the Reds, LA revealed its plans with Edwin Diaz.
More MLB on Heavy: Los Angeles Dodgers Dealt Positive Shohei Ohtani News During Reds Series
Edwin Diaz to be Activated Off IL on Friday
According to multiple reporters who follow the Los Angeles Dodgers, Edwin Diaz will be activated from the Injured List on Friday.
"Dave Roberts said Edwin Diaz will meet team in Los Angeles. When he is activated it will be "low leverage" situations and will have to earn higher leverage spots."
So, that basically rules out the possibility that Edwin Diaz will be a closer for the Dodgers, which is a good call by Dave Roberts. Despite a few solid outings on paper, it feels like every time Diaz has pitched for the Dodgers this season, there's always been added nerves to the situation.
More MLB on Heavy: Blake Snell's Latest Injury Comments Should Not Faze Los Angeles Dodgers Fans
More on Edwin Diaz Injury….
Edwin Diaz has been sidelined since mid-August with a neck injury.
He will be eased into the bullpen fold, and the good news for LA is that they may have already wrapped up the NL West when Diaz joins the team in LA on Friday.
"Díaz signed a three-year, $69MM contract over the winter, but it's been a lost season for the All-Star closer. He's pitched in just 13 2/3 big league innings due to injury and hasn't looked anywhere close to his usual self when healthy enough to take the mound. He's been rocked for 18 runs on 25 hits and 10 walks, leading to an awful 11.85 earned run average. Díaz entered the season with a career 39.9% strikeout rate and 8.6% walk rate. Those marks have plummeted to 24.1% and 12.7% this season, and his average fastball has dropped from 97.2 mph in 2025 to 96.3 mph in 2026."
In other Dodgers news, Andy Pages could be nearing a return as well, and manager Dave Roberts did not rule out a return for Shohei Ohtani during the regular season, which has just a week and a half left.
Like HEAVY's content? Be sure to follow us.

The post Los Angeles Dodgers Reveal Edwin Diaz Plans Amid Looming Return appeared first on HEAVY.

item.content:encoded:
レッズ2－8ドジャース（17日、シンシナティ）米大リーグ、ドジャースがレッズ戦に勝利し、ナ・リーグ西地区で5年連続の地区優勝を飾った。「右上腕二頭筋の炎症」で負傷者リスト（IL）入りする大谷翔平投手（32）は遠征地のシンシナティに帯同せず、優勝の瞬間に不在だった。
2023年以来、3年ぶりに開幕二刀流で迎えたが、苦難のシーズンだった。春先は圧巻の内容で投球を続けたが、6月に左膝、7月に右上腕を負傷。例年、夏場に状態が上がる打撃も成績は伸びず、7月10日の登板を回避し、オールスター辞退を発表。12日に左膝潤滑剤注射を受けた。
後半戦は投手復帰のリハビリを進めながら、打者専念で出場するも患部の状態は一進一退で、計3度の投球中断を経た。8月30日の復帰に向け、28日に敵地デトロイトでブルペン入りしたが、患部の状態は思わしくなく復帰を断念。シーズン最終盤で打者専念の決断を下すも、スイングする際に右上腕の違和感も拭えず、9月9日にドジャース移籍後初となる負傷者リスト（IL）入りとなった。
15日に打撃練習を再開するも、依然復帰時期は不透明で、ポストシーズンの出場も危ぶまれている。今季は投手として8勝2敗、防御率1.79、95奪三振。打者として打率・277、30本塁打、80打点、11盗塁の成績。昨季まで3年連続4度受賞していたMVPの獲得は絶望的。ワールドシリーズ3連覇に照準を定める。
