item.title: [New York Post] Yoshinobu Yamamoto rounds into playoff form as Dodgers move to cusp of NL West title
item.dc:creator: Jack Harris
item.description: CINCINNATI –– There’s not much the Dodgers can do, manager Dave Roberts said Tuesday afternoon, to get their all-important rotation ready for the added workload that will come in the postseason. Over the final couple weeks of the regular season, they have to just keep running their starters out there, and counting on them to round into elevated October form. That’s what appeared to happen with Yoshinobu Yamamoto on Tuesday night at Great American Ball Park, in what was the right-hander’s most do
item.content:encoded:
CINCINNATI –– There’s not much the Dodgers can do, manager Dave Roberts said Tuesday afternoon, to get their all-important rotation ready for the added workload that will come in the postseason.
Over the final couple weeks of the regular season, they have to just keep running their starters out there, and counting on them to round into elevated October form.
That’s what appeared to happen with Yoshinobu Yamamoto on Tuesday night at Great American Ball Park, in what was the right-hander’s most dominant performance of at least the last couple months.
In the Dodgers’ 4-0 win over the Cincinnati Reds, Yamamoto threw a one-hit masterpiece over seven scoreless innings, flashing the kind of ruthless efficiency that defined his heroics during last year’s playoffs.
After walking his first two batters in the first inning, he retired 21 of the 22 after with seven strikeouts and virtually no stress.
“After the first two hitters, it was vintage Yama,” Roberts said. “Just attacking, not trying to be too fine.”
The reigning World Series MVP hadn’t exactly been struggling lately, of course. Just last week, he held the Reds to one run over seven innings with 10 strikeouts back in Los Angeles.
But what Yamamoto did on Tuesday was different, keyed by quick and easy outs on soft and harmless contact.
It’s what he did as the ace of last year’s postseason staff, and what he will need to do again as the Dodgers go for a World Series three-peat this fall.
“I’d like to carry this,” Yamamoto said through an interpreter of his renewed stuff, “into October.”
The Dodgers are hoping they won’t have to ask as much out of Yamamoto this time around; that they need him to pitch back-to-back complete games (like he did in Game 2 of the NLCS and Game 2 of the World Series) or provide back-to-back nights of season-saving heroics (following up a victorious Game 6 start in the Fall Classic with a winning three-inning appearance out of the bullpen in Game 7).
But in a postseason environment, it’s impossible to know what exactly will be required.
“You can’t just try to create that during the regular season because you want these guys as strong and healthy for the October run [as possible],” Roberts said pregame. “But it’s one of those things that, once we get to the postseason, all bets are off and everyone is going to do what they can to contribute.”
It would help, of course, if the Dodgers’ currently Shohei Ohtani-less offense can keep turning a corner, with Tuesday bringing more positive –– albeit subtle –– signs.
The biggest development: Freddie Freeman returned to the lineup amid his ongoing right knee injury, and finally snapped out of a 3-for-30 slump by collecting three singles in the first, fifth and seventh innings.
“Feels better today than he did yesterday,” Roberts said, after Freeman missed his third game in the last week on Monday, “which is a good thing.”
The Dodgers’ scoring, meanwhile, came from elsewhere.

Hunter Feduccia laced an RBI single in the second off Reds starter Rhett Lowder, maintaining his unexpected status as the Dodgers’ best hitter against right-handed pitching since being re-acquired at the trade deadline (with a team-leading .292 average in such splits since the start of August).
Teoscar Hernández continued his late-season surge with a two-run homer in the third, giving him four home runs, eight extra-base hits, 18 RBIs and a .417 average over his last 14 games.
Even Alex Freeland chipped in with a solo blast in the seventh and a double in the ninth, helping him outshine fellow rookie Josue De Paula (who went 0-for-5 with his first two strikeouts of the season after getting bumped up to the leadoff spot).
That was all enough to help the team lower its magic number to clinch the National League West to one.
Still, when it comes to October, no position group will be more important than the Dodgers’ rotation.
That’s why, right now, outings like the one Yamamoto made on Tuesday, or Tarik Skubal spun the night before (also seven scoreless innings) are the most promising ways the Dodgers can ramp up toward the playoffs.
Once they get there, they’ll need their starters to be on.

item.content:encoded:
Dodgers news: Shohei Ohtani, Andy Pages get big injury updates before playoffs appeared first on ClutchPoints. Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here.
With a spot in the MLB playoff locked up, the Los Angeles Dodgers have one major goal for the rest of September: get healthy.
Sure, there are sub-storylines to follow, from Josue De Paula filling in at DH, which bullpen arms are getting hot at the right time, and Kyle Tucker figuring it out down the stretch, but for the most part, the Dodgers simply want to take the field in October with their best guys all available for Dave Roberts to call upon.
Fortunately, on Tuesday, Roberts provided fans with some positive updates on that very front, noting that Shohei Ohtani and Andy Pages are trending in the right direction, as reported by The Athletic's Fabian Ardaya.
Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)
"Some more from Dave Roberts: Shohei Ohtani hit in the cage today. Hope is still for him to return before the end of the regular season," Ardaya wrote. "Andy Pages hit off the machine today. Plan is for him to do Trajekt next. Bullpen game on Thursday."
After breaking his hand in mid-August in a game against the Pittsburgh Pirates, Pages has missed almost a month as he works back from surgery. And as for Ohtani? Well, after missing four games earlier in the month, he returned for one but didn't ultimately look right, landing on the IL to allow him to recover from a series of injuries that have hampered his production down the stretch.
Without Pages and Ohtani, the Dodgers still found a way to manufacture offense, ripping off their longest win streak of the season, but folding that duo back into the fray, especially with De Paula proving he deserves a spot on the bench as a power-hitting pinch hitter, makes LA all the more dangerous down the stretch.
Related: Bobby Miller gets brutally honest on returning to Dodgers
Related: Why Dodgers' Dave Roberts is leading off Josue De Paula vs. Reds

item.dc:creator: Sonja Chen

Ohtani is not on the road with the Dodgers, but he hit off a tee in L.A. and came away feeling good afterward, Roberts said. It was Ohtani's first time swinging since his lingering right biceps and left knee injuries led him to be shut down starting last Wednesday. "I don't k
item.content:encoded:
CINCINNATI -- Shohei Ohtani resumed swinging on Tuesday for the first time since landing on the 15-day injured list last week, manager Dave Roberts said before the Dodgers' game against the Reds at Great American Ball Park.
Ohtani is not on the road with the Dodgers, but he hit off a tee in L.A. and came away feeling good afterward, Roberts said. It was Ohtani's first time swinging since his lingering right biceps and left knee injuries led him to be shut down starting last Wednesday.
"I don't know what's in store for tomorrow, but I know that there's going to be a consistent buildup," Roberts said. "Don't know when the time of return to play is, but today was positive, and hopefully we can just keep building towards that."
Ohtani's 15-day IL placement is backdated to Sept. 8, meaning that the earliest he can be activated is Sept. 23, with five regular-season games remaining for the Dodgers. Roberts believes that Ohtani will be back in action before the end of the regular season.
"Whether it happens or not is to be determined, but I do expect him to be back to play in some regular-season games," Roberts said. "Don't know how many of them."
In his last 24 games, a span that coincided with an attempt to ramp up as a pitcher, Ohtani hit .198 (19-for-96) with a .690 OPS and 34 strikeouts. Toward the end of that stretch, he began to look physically compromised at the plate, leading the Dodgers to leave him out of the lineup for four straight games. He returned to the lineup on Sept. 7 but did not come away from that game feeling good.
At that point, the Dodgers opted to place Ohtani on the IL with the aim of getting him right for the postseason. He will return only as a hitter, with his two-way duties shelved until 2027.
The Dodgers have fared well without their best hitter, entering Tuesday having won nine of the 11 games they played since Ohtani was first held out of the lineup on Sept. 3. They clinched their record-tying 14th consecutive postseason berth on Monday and are close to winning their 13th NL West title in that span, all while remaining in position to secure a first-round bye.
The understanding is that Ohtani will probably not feel 100 percent in the postseason, but he'll use the weeks ahead to feel as good as he can, both physically and with his swing. While the Dodgers have gotten by without him, they know they'll need whatever they can get from him as they bid for a three-peat.

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Josue De Paula Gets Love From Future Hall of Famer
item.dc:creator: Cameron Kiszla
item.description: Los Angeles Dodgers rookie Josue De Paula may be known for his big bat, but it's the times he doesn't swing that are drawing comparisons to a future Hall of Famer. De Paula has only two hits in his young MLB career — granted, one of them was a huge home run — but he's walked five times, recording at least one in each of his four games, without even a single strikeout. That kind of plate discipline — and De Paula's funny reaction to pitches outside of the strike zone — have an unexpected supersta
item.content:encoded:
Los Angeles Dodgers rookie Josue De Paula may be known for his big bat, but it's the times he doesn't swing that are drawing comparisons to a future Hall of Famer.
De Paula has only two hits in his young MLB career — granted, one of them was a huge home run — but he's walked five times, recording at least one in each of his four games, without even a single strikeout.
That kind of plate discipline — and De Paula's funny reaction to pitches outside of the strike zone — have an unexpected superstar showing love to the young Dodger.
Rival player supports Josue De Paula
New York Met Juan Soto, who's battled the Dodgers as a member of the San Diego Padres and New York Yankees, took to Instagram to shout out his fellow Dominican slugger.
Sharing MLB's video of De Paula shaking his head at a pitch below his knees in a moment reminiscent of the "Soto shuffle," Soto gassed up the young slugger.
In Spanish, Soto praised De Paula, whom he called "my crazy friend," for "staying locked in at the plate."
As Dodgers Nation's Noel Sanchez pointed out, the two truly are friends, and their shared history goes beyond just the ability to take a walk or hit a home run.
"These two both attended El Niche Baseball Academy early in their respective careers and they've trained together in the past," Sanchez said. "In a sports world where comparison can be the thief of joy, it's so nice to see Soto co-signing De Paula after his early success."
Of course, Dodgers faithful probably aren't huge fans of Soto.
He and the Padres knocked the Dodgers out of the playoffs in 2022, and he spurned the Boys in Blue to sign with the Mets on a contract even bigger than that of superstar Shohei Ohtani.
That said, Soto's ability to recognize the talents of a younger player — even on another NL team — is worth celebrating, Sanchez said.
"A lot of Dodger fans don't show him love but like I said, everyone should respect this," he said.
What do you think of Juan Soto showing love to Josue De Paula?

item.title: [Sports Illustrated] Dodgers' Dave Roberts Sent Kyle Tucker Clear Message in One-on-One Meeting
item.dc:creator: J P Hoornstra; Unknown
item.description: Kyle Tucker's home run Monday in Cincinnati was his third in his last five games. In that span he's raised his slugging percentage from a season-low .350 on Sept. 8 to .376 entering Tuesday's rematch against the Reds. September is halfway through, and it's shaping into Tucker's best month of the season. If it seems like he's stopped pressing at the plate, perhaps Tucker let up on himself after getting some needed reassurance in a one-on-one meeting with Los Angeles Dodgers manager Dave Roberts.
item.content:encoded:
Kyle Tucker's home run Monday in Cincinnati was his third in his last five games. In that span he's raised his slugging percentage from a season-low .350 on Sept. 8 to .376 entering Tuesday's rematch against the Reds.
September is halfway through, and it's shaping into Tucker's best month of the season. If it seems like he's stopped pressing at the plate, perhaps Tucker let up on himself after getting some needed reassurance in a one-on-one meeting with Los Angeles Dodgers manager Dave Roberts.
“I told him, I’m gonna ride or die with him,” Roberts said (via Jack Harris of the California Post). “That was my young term phrase.”
It's been a rough ride for Tucker in his first season in Los Angeles. The Dodgers signed the four-time All-Star to a four-year, $240 million contract over the winter. Despite being baseball's highest-paid player this season, Tucker hit only one home run in his first 17 games of the season.
Things didn't get much better from there. Among 138 qualified hitters through the end of August, Tucker's .683 OPS ranked 116th.
"I was prepared, the organization was prepared, to give him as much leash as we possibly could to work through some things, and I do think that now we’re starting to see the fruits,” Roberts said. “So I see no other reason why we would pivot from running him out there every day.”
Fans might beg to differ.
At Triple-A Oklahoma City, outfielder James Tibbs III has 29 home runs and 101 RBIs to go with a .417 on-base percentage. Prospect Josue De Paula, who's played right field in the minors, was promoted to take Shohei Ohtani's place on the active roster.
Since his debut, the 21-year-old has reached base in half of his first 14 plate appearances. Sunday, he hit his first career home run. Perhaps Roberts needed to reassure Tucker that De Paula wasn't coming for his job to unlock his production, a curious case of reverse psychology.
It will be hard for the Dodgers to take De Paula out of the lineup if he maintains his current level of production. Roberts said prior to Ohtani's IL stint that the team wasn't considering using him in the outfield.
Tucker, for his part, can reduce the Dodgers' temptation to use Ohtani or De Paula in right field if he continues to hit like a $60 million All-Star.

J.P. Hoornstra is an On SI Contributor. A veteran of 20 years of sports coverage for daily newspapers in California, J.P. covered MLB, the Los Angeles Dodgers, and the Los Angeles Angels (occasionally of Anaheim) from 2012-23 for the Southern California News Group. His first book, The 50 Greatest Dodgers Games of All-Time, published in 2015. In 2016, he won an Associated Press Sports Editors award for breaking news coverage. He once recorded a keyboard solo on the same album as two of the original Doors.

And yet, that wasn’t the biggest surprise in the team’s new-look batting order. Instead, rookie designated hitter Josue De Paula got an auspicious bump up for the club, getting the chance to serve as leadoff hitter for Tuesday’s matchup against Reds right-hander Rhett Lowder. Tuesday only marked De Paula’s fifth game in the majors, following his call-up directl
item.content:encoded:
CINCINNATI –– Despite Freddie Freeman’s ongoing right knee injury, the veteran first baseman was back in the Dodgers’ lineup on Tuesday.
And yet, that wasn’t the biggest surprise in the team’s new-look batting order.
Instead, rookie designated hitter Josue De Paula got an auspicious bump up for the club, getting the chance to serve as leadoff hitter for Tuesday’s matchup against Reds right-hander Rhett Lowder.
Tuesday only marked De Paula’s fifth game in the majors, following his call-up directly from double-A Tulsa last week.
He is still serving as DH on only a temporary basis, with Shohei Ohtani on the injured list nursing left knee and right arm injuries.
However, the 21-year-old top prospect has already made a positive impression, drawing five walks in his first 14 plate appearances while collecting his first two MLB hits on Sunday in Miami with a home run and a double. He is suddenly vying for a potential role in the postseason plans, as well.
Thus, the Dodgers are giving the promising left-handed hitter another new opportunity now, seeing how he looks as the leadoff man in their batting order –– one that was also vacated once Ohtani went on the IL.
“I like the at-bats. I like the at-bat quality,” manager Dave Roberts said. “I understand it’s a small sample, but that’s kind of who he is as a hitter. For me, it’ll be a good opportunity for him to get five at-bats tonight.”
For Freeman, meanwhile, Tuesday marks an important opportunity in its own right, as he tries to show progress with his right knee injury.
Freeman has been out for three of the Dodgers’ last five games because of the ailment, and only DH’d in the game before that.
Since the start of September, he has gone only 3-for-30 at the plate.
Roberts continues to insist an injured list stint won’t be needed for the newly-turned 37-year-old. Both he and Freeman voiced hopes of the injury being resolved (or, at least, not as much of an impediment) by the time the playoffs begin.
“I don’t see him getting to his front side as much as he normally does, which causes him to get a little bit underneath,” Roberts said. “So I know that the hitting guys are on it. He’s working through it, so we’ll see how he comes in today.”
Until he starts to hit again, however, concerns over his health will linger.
On Tuesday, he is batting directly after De Paula in the No. 2 hole.

item.title: [Dodgers Way] Edgardo Henriquez injury just flipped the Dodgers' season upside down
item.dc:creator: Jordan Campbell
item.description: The Los Angeles Dodgers are in familiar territory with the playoffs less than two weeks away. They are once again looking for answers in their bullpen. The Dodgers have placed Edgardo Henriquez on the IL with lower back discomfort, and he has been ruled out for the remainder of the regular season. item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers are in familiar territory with the playoffs less than two weeks away. They are once again looking for answers in their bullpen. The Dodgers have placed Edgardo Henriquez on the IL with lower back discomfort, and he has been ruled out for the remainder of the regular season.
Henriquez has been placed on the 15-day IL, but there remains a path for him returning during the playoffs if all goes well. While the Dodgers made Edwin Diaz a priority this past offseason, it has been Henriquez who has kept the bullpen together.
Through 61 appearances, Henriquez had a 2.85 ERA while striking out over 29% of the hitters he's faced. If he's unable to return to LA's bullpen during the playoffs, the unit is suddenly facing a problem.
Edgardo Henriquez injury leaves Dodgers facing reality they desperately wanted to avoid
While the Dodgers have a healthy amount of left-handed options in the bullpen — considering Tanner Scott once again becoming an effective option at the end of games — as well as Alex Vesia and Jack Dreyer, they don't really have an established option among righties.
Brock Stewart hasn't looked bad this season, but injuries have limited him to just 22 innings pitched this season. Evan Phillips is back in the bullpen, and while he has 3.68 ERA through 27 appearances, his FIP of 4.65 makes him a regression candidate ahead of the playoffs.
It also doesn't help matters that the Dodgers aren't viewing the return of Diaz as a potential solution. He is currently on a minor-league rehab assignment, but the results simply haven't been there. It's forced Dave Roberts to offer a blunt assessment on Diaz earlier this week, suggesting there's a chance he's left off the playoff roster if he can't overcome his current struggles.
That is why Henriquez's injury is such a blow. He was a clear answer for what the Dodgers lacked in the bullpen, and coupling that with Diaz's struggles, Roberts and Co. are back at the drawing board. Perhaps Kris Bubic could be an answer. Bubic is with the Dodgers after a successful rehab assignment earlier this month and is expected to be reinstated from the IL in the coming days.
If there is a silver lining for the Dodgers, outside of Shohei Ohtani, their starting rotation is healthy and that could ultimately prove to be the difference-maker during the playoffs.

item.content:encoded:
Los Angeles Dodgers star first baseman Freddie Freeman does not look like himself right now.
Freeman, who is hitting .293 this season with 16 home runs and an OPS of .818, is dealing with right knee tendinitis.
Since the start of August, the 10-time All-Star is hitting .252 with just one home run and an OPS of .651
Dodgers manager Dave Roberts touched on the injury this past weekend and said that while Freeman is feeling fine enough to play, he's far from the player the team is accustomed to seeing.
“Just talking to him today, he said he felt good,” Roberts said on Sunday, before adding: “Obviously, the swings don’t indicate that, don’t kind of validate that … The last week, it’s pretty obvious that he’s not himself in the box.”
Freeman's knee issue compromises his front side during swings, which has caused extra swing-and-miss at the plate and limited his mobility on defense.
On Monday for the team's series opener against the Cincinnati Reds, Freeman was out of the lineup for the fourth time in the last week.
Roberts said Freeman's injury is one they'll have to manage for the rest of the season.
“I think it’s one of those things where we’ve got to manage it … just pick spots to give him an off day here or there,” Roberts said. “Again, we’ve just got to make sure he’s at optimal health when we finish the season. So I think that he might not love it, but giving him a day off here or there might be beneficial.”
Freeman is expected to avoid an IL stint and remains day-to-day. It remains to be seen if he's back on Tuesday.
"I just think right now, with where we’re at in the season, an IL is not an option in the sense of — I personally don’t think we have a better option," Roberts said. "I don’t think it needs to be 10 days. But could it be more than one? That’s a fair question."
Shohei Ohtani Working His Way Back From Injury
Freeman's injury is just another in a long list of injuries that the Dodgers are dealing with as the regular season winds down.
Freeman is not the only All-SAtar missing time, as Shohei Ohtani is far from healthy as the season winds down.
Ohtani is currently on the 15-day IL with knee, biceps and neck injuries. Roberts said that Ohtani will hit off a tee on Tuesday as he begins his ramp-up.
The 32-year-old is looking to quickly get back as he is eligible to return to the lineup on Sept. 23, just five days before the end of the regular season.
In the meantime, the Dodgers' top prospect, Josue De Paula, has replaced Ohtani as the everyday designated hitter.
If the Dodgers want any chance of completing the three-peat, though, Freeman and Ohtani will need to be healthy and producing at their usual levels.
Thus, the Dodgers will look to get them as close to 100% as possible over the next two weeks.
Sign up for our free newsletter and follow us on X/Twitter and Facebook for the latest news.
Ricardo Sandoval is a freelance writer with On SI. He is a graduate of California State University, Northridge, and specializes in sports writing, particularly in MLB, NBA and NFL. He previously served as an Associate Editor for Dodgers Nation and has worked with Newsweek and The Sporting News.
Follow @_RicardoSand

He's producing a movie titled "Cannon Street All-Stars." Los Angeles clinched a playoff berth the same day, beating the Cincinnati Reds 4-1. The win pushed them to 91-59 with 12 games left. item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers shortstop Mookie Betts is producing a new movie. On Monday, he announced the project away from the field. He's producing a movie titled "Cannon Street All-Stars."
Los Angeles clinched a playoff berth the same day, beating the Cincinnati Reds 4-1. The win pushed them to 91-59 with 12 games left. It marks the Dodgers' 14th straight postseason appearance.
However, Betts did little to contribute to that win. He went 0-for-4. No hits, home runs or RBIs.
He is having a down year by his standards.
Betts is batting .248 with 20 home runs, 62 RBIs and 108 hits this season. His career average sits at .288. Betts won AL MVP in 2018 and has made eight All-Star teams.
Off the diamond, however, he is excelling in his projects.
More on Mookie Betts' Latest Project
Betts is producing the film alongside Golden State Warriors star Stephen Curry, Deadline reported in an exclusive Monday.
Director Reggie Rock Bythewood and his wife, Gina Prince-Bythewood, are developing the project through their company, Undisputed Cinema. Bythewood will write and direct.
The film tells the true story of the Cannon Street YMCA All-Stars. The all-Black Little League team from Charleston, South Carolina, tried to enter the 1955 state tournament.
Little League baseball in the South remained segregated at the time, eight years after Jackie Robinson broke MLB's color line. The team's push sparked forfeits and national attention. The Jackie Robinson Foundation backs the project.
Bythewood called the film overdue recognition. Surviving players were honored at last year's Little League World Series. "Now it is time to honor them on film," Bythewood said.
Betts produces through his company, OMG Entertainment, alongside Cam Lewis and Omar Bradford. Curry produces through Unanimous Media with Sharla Sumpter Bridgett. Debra Martin Chase and E. Monique Floyd also produce.
Shohei Ohtani, Freddie Freeman Latest Updates
Despite clinching the postseason, few key pieces remain uncertain.
Shohei Ohtani is on the 15-day injured list with left knee and right biceps issues. He landed there Sept. 11.
Manager Dave Roberts said Monday that Ohtani could begin swinging off a tee as early as this week. The Dodgers expect Ohtani back as a hitter in late September. He won't pitch again this season. Ohtani is batting .277 with 30 home runs and 80 RBIs this year.
Freddie Freeman sat out Monday's game to rest a sore right knee, described as patellar tendinitis. The team does not plan to place him on the injured list. Freeman is expected back in the lineup Tuesday.

item.content:encoded:
Dodgers celebran 14to pase seguido a los playoffs con discreto brindis e igualan récord
CINCINNATI — Los Dodgers de Los Ángeles celebraron su 14ta clasificación consecutiva a la postemporada de las Grandes Ligas, para igualar un récord, con un brindis de champán tras la victoria del lunes por la noche por 4-1 sobre los Rojos de Cincinnati.
Las celebraciones más grandes llegarán después.
“Es difícil decir que alguna vez se sienta rutinario, pero esa es la expectativa aquí. Siempre me río cuando aseguramos un lugar en la postemporada: simplemente hacemos un brindis pequeño y agradable”, dijo el tercera base Max Muncy. “Los muchachos que no han estado aquí ven eso y esperan un poco más. Eso pasa cuando aseguras la división”.
Los bicampeones defensores de la Serie Mundial, que se unieron a Milwaukee y Tampa Bay como equipos que ya aseguraron un lugar en los playoffs, redujeron su número mágico a tres para un quinto título consecutivo del Oeste de la Liga Nacional y el 13ro en 14 temporadas.
Los Ángeles igualó la racha de postemporadas de los Bravos de Atlanta de 1991 a 2005. Los Bravos alcanzaron cinco veces a la Serie Mundial durante ese lapso, pero la única vez que se consagraron fue en 1995.
“Por suerte lo estamos haciendo un poco mejor que eso”, dijo Muncy sobre los tres títulos de los Dodgers y sus cinco participaciones en el Clásico de Otoño durante esta racha.
Tarik Skubal —quien lanzó siete entradas sin permitir carreras y concedió apenas tres hits— señaló que la manera en que los Dodgers manejaron el hecho de asegurar un lugar en la postemporada fue definitivamente distinta en comparación con las situaciones de clasificación que vivió las dos temporadas anteriores con Detroit.
“Creo que eso habla de la gente que está en este vestuario y de lo que esperan de este equipo. Eso estuvo genial. Un pequeño brindis y a seguir. Olvidar que pasó. Tenemos más por lograr esta temporada”, expresó.
Dave Roberts, quien cumple su 11ma temporada como mánager, dijo que su mensaje durante el brindis fue que los Dodgers han logrado mucho hasta este punto, pero aún no se han acercado a jugar su mejor béisbol.
“Cada año pasan muchos jugadores por aquí, y los muchachos encuentran la manera de dar un paso al frente, y eso es de lo que probablemente me siento más orgulloso: la consistencia de ganar a largo plazo. Cualquier equipo, cualquier organización puede ganar en un año determinado cuando las cosas se alinean, pero hacerlo todos los años, cuando se espera que lo hagas, dice algo sobre toda la organización”, dijo Roberts.
Los Dodgers (91-59) actualmente son el segundo sembrado en la Liga Nacional. Están dos juegos y medio por delante de Atlanta y están dos juegos detrás de Milwaukee por el primer puesto.
Un pase directo en la primera ronda es importante en cualquier momento, pero especialmente este año para los Dodgers, que no están a plena capacidad. El primera base Freddie Freeman arrastra molestias en la rodilla derecha y Shohei Ohtani, dos veces Jugador Más Valioso de la Liga Nacional, está en la lista de lesionados de 15 días debido a una inflamación en el bíceps derecho.
“Dado cómo están nuestros muchachos en términos de salud, conseguir esa semana sería enorme. Aun así, tenemos que jugar bien para cerrar la temporada y llegar a ese punto”, dijo Roberts antes del juego del lunes.
___

item.title: [Field Level Media] Dodgers' Tarik Skubal looks to duplicate recent outing vs. Reds

item.content:encoded:
The two-time reigning World Series champion Los Angeles Dodgers are closing in on the National League West title and still have their sights on the NL’s top seed.
Despite the positives, the Dodgers are limping into the opener of a three-game series against the host Cincinnati Reds on Monday.
Los Angeles (90-59) enters play having dropped two straight against the Miami Marlins, including a 6-4 loss on Sunday that saw the club allow four runs in the ninth and a walk-off homer.
Maybe even more concerning is the injury status of manager Dave Roberts’ star players. After placing Shohei Ohtani on the injured list on Friday with knee and biceps ailments, Roberts announced plans to keep first baseman Freddie Freeman out of the lineup on Monday as he deals with right knee tendinitis.
“(Freddie) is obviously not moving as well as he’s used to,” Roberts said. “I’ll give him a chance to recover and then he’ll be back in there on Tuesday. He’s doing everything he can to prepare, but it’s been obvious the last week that he’s not himself in the box.”
Freeman, 37, sat on Wednesday and Friday before returning to the lineup and going 0-for-8 the last two games. The 10-time All-Star is batting .293 with 16 home runs and 66 RBIs this season.
Tarik Skubal (9-7, 2.84 ERA) will make his eighth start since being traded from Detroit to the Dodgers and his second against the Reds in as many appearances. The 29-year-old tossed 7 1/3 innings of two-run, four-hit ball against Cincinnati on Tuesday. The left-hander struck out five and walked two in a 3-2 win.
Skubal has a 2.93 ERA with the Dodgers and has surrendered two earned runs or fewer in four of his last five starts. Still, the two-time American League Cy Young Award winner believes he has more to give. Coming off the longest outing of his short Los Angeles career, Skubal is beginning to live up to his lofty expectations.
“I think that’s ultimately the job of a starting pitcher,” Skubal said of his longest start with the Dodgers on Tuesday. “One, to give your team a chance to win every time you’re out there, and two, to eat as many innings as you can. … I don’t think I’ve thrown the ball as well as I know I’m capable of yet.”
Skubal is 2-0 with a 1.88 ERA in two career starts against the Reds.
With only a few starts left in what’s been a lackluster year, Nick Lodolo (3-4, 5.12) is hoping to correct an inconsistent personal stretch for the Reds (70-79). The 28-year-old has battled through a pair of stints on the injured list due to a blister on his left index finger.
Since returning on Aug. 11, Lodolo has failed to complete five innings in four of six starts. The left-hander faced Skubal and the Dodgers in a losing effort on Tuesday, when he allowed three runs on five hits across 4 2/3 frames. He struck out six and walked three, extending a seven-start stretch without a win.
“I thought early, he wasn’t commanding the ball,” Reds manager Terry Francona said of Lodolo’s last start. “When he got into the third, fourth and fifth (inning), I actually thought he got better. I really wanted him to get through that fifth. I thought it would have been good for him.”
In three career starts against Los Angeles, Lodolo is 0-2 with a 5.52 ERA.
–Field Level Media

item.title: [voz.us] Los Dodgers se aseguran el pase a los playoffs y aspiran a su tercera Serie Mundial consecutiva
item.dc:creator: AFP
item.description: Los Dodgers se aseguran el pase a los playoffs y aspiran a su tercera Serie Mundial consecutiva El equipo de Los Ángeles se encuentra actualmente en posición de asegurarse uno de los dos primeros puestos de la Liga Nacional junto a los Milwaukee Brewers, que también tienen garantizada una plaza en la postemporada. En la Liga Americana, los Tampa Bay Rays ya se han clasificado. Los Dodgers de Los Ángeles, que aspiran a su tercer título consecutivo de la Serie Mundial, aseguraron el lunes su plaza
item.content:encoded:
Los Dodgers se aseguran el pase a los playoffs y aspiran a su tercera Serie Mundial consecutiva
El equipo de Los Ángeles se encuentra actualmente en posición de asegurarse uno de los dos primeros puestos de la Liga Nacional junto a los Milwaukee Brewers, que también tienen garantizada una plaza en la postemporada. En la Liga Americana, los Tampa Bay Rays ya se han clasificado.
Los Dodgers de Los Ángeles, que aspiran a su tercer título consecutivo de la Serie Mundial, aseguraron el lunes su plaza en los playoffs tras imponerse por 4-1 a los Reds de Cincinnati. Con un récord de 91-59 y 12 partidos por disputar en la temporada regular, los Dodgers tienen ahora asegurada, como mínimo, una plaza en la serie de comodines.
Los Dodgers se encuentran actualmente en posición de asegurarse uno de los dos primeros puestos de la Liga Nacional —lo que les da derecho a saltarse la primera ronda y a la ventaja de jugar en casa en la serie divisional— junto con los Milwaukee Brewers, que también tienen asegurada su plaza en la postemporada. En la Liga Americana, los Tampa Bay Rays ya se han clasificado.
Los Dodgers, con su generosa inversión, vencieron a los Yankees de Nueva York en la Serie Mundial de 2024 y se impusieron a los Blue Jays de Toronto el año pasado.
Los fichajes de Skubal y Kyle Tucker convierten a los Dodgers en favoritos aún más claros
Tras incorporar al jardinero Kyle Tucker durante la temporada baja y al lanzador Tarik Skubal —ganador en dos ocasiones del Premio Cy Young— el mes pasado, los Dodgers son los favoritos para completar su triplete.
Podrían convertirse en el primer equipo de la Liga Nacional en ganar la Serie Mundial tres años seguidos y el primero desde los Yankees de 1998 a 2000. Pero llegar a los playoffs por decimocuarta temporada consecutiva no ha sido precisamente un camino de rosas.
Una temporada de altibajos
Tras llegar al parón del All-Star con una ventaja de 11,5 partidos sobre Arizona en la división Oeste de la Liga Nacional —con diferencia, el mayor margen de cualquier líder de división—, los Dodgers sufrieron un bajón de forma. La superestrella polivalente Shohei Ohtani ha estado de baja por lesiones, y no se espera que vuelva a lanzar esta temporada; su rendimiento al bate también ha bajado.
Sin embargo, una racha reciente de ocho victorias consecutivas —la mejor de la temporada— ha restablecido la considerable ventaja de los Dodgers al frente de la División Oeste de la Liga Nacional. Sus rivales más cercanos por uno de los dos primeros puestos son los Atlanta Braves de la División Este de la Liga Nacional.
Kyle Tucker y Teoscar Hernández conectaron sendos jonrones en la cómoda victoria de los Dodgers el lunes por la noche en Cincinnati.

item.title: [Los Angeles Times] Dodgers might be forced to leave Edwin Díaz off postseason roster
item.dc:creator: Maddie Lee
item.description: Dodgers might be forced to leave Edwin Díaz off postseason roster - Click here to listen to this article - - Edwin Díaz struggled in his rehab start Sunday, and Dave Roberts is making it clear the Dodgers “got to see something” from the closer to put him on the playoff roster. - The Dodgers placed reliever Edgardo Henriquez on the 15-day injured list and recalled Bobby Miller and Paul Gervase. CINCINNATI — Even as the Dodgers clinched a postseason berth with their 4-1 win over the Reds on
item.content:encoded:
Dodgers might be forced to leave Edwin Díaz off postseason roster
- Click here to listen to this article
-
- Edwin Díaz struggled in his rehab start Sunday, and Dave Roberts is making it clear the Dodgers “got to see something” from the closer to put him on the playoff roster.
- The Dodgers placed reliever Edgardo Henriquez on the 15-day injured list and recalled Bobby Miller and Paul Gervase.
CINCINNATI — Even as the Dodgers clinched a postseason berth with their 4-1 win over the Reds on Monday, bullpen uncertainty loomed.
When they get to the playoffs, who’s going to take the ball in high-leverage situations?
Their options are dwindling. Edgardo Henriquez landed on the 15-day injured list Monday with low back discomfort, ruling him out for the rest of the regular season. Edwin Díaz was so shaky in his rehab assignment Sunday that a spot on the postseason roster isn’t guaranteed.
“We have to go with our best pitchers, as far as performance, talent, all that stuff,” manager Dave Roberts said before the Dodgers opened a four-game series against the Reds. “So my bet is that he will be [on the roster]. But there’s got to be some kind of evidence or something for us to sort of bet on. And so my bet is, yes, but we’ve still got to see something.”
The Dodgers clinch a playoff berth with their 4-1 victory over the Cincinnati Reds, reaching the postseason for a record-tying 14th consecutive year.
Díaz (neck) had the worst outing of his triple-A rehab assignment, surrendering five runs and issuing two walks in two-thirds of an inning. The dud put his return timeline in doubt. His next rehab appearance is scheduled for Wednesday.
“I think the world of him, the baseball card looks great,” Roberts said. “But where we’re at, there’s got to be something for us to be able to hang our hat on. And he knows that. He knows that. He wants to pitch well. So for me, Wednesday, we’ll be watching closely.”
So, who’s still in play?
Tanner Scott remains Roberts’ go-to in save situations. And Alex Vesia, Evan Phillips, Brock Stewart, Jack Dreyer and Blake Treinen all have experience in late innings.
On Monday, starter Tarik Skubal gave the group a much-needed break with seven shutout innings. He limited the Reds to three hits and a walk, cruising through their lineup almost three times in 90 pitches.
The Dodgers pulled ahead by four runs, on home runs from Kyle Tucker and Teoscar Hernández, who have both broken out of slumps, and an RBI single from Kiké Hernández.
With the game still relatively tight, Vesia entered in the bottom of the eighth to face the left-handed heavy bottom of the order. He retired the side.
Phillips and Treinen both were warming in the ninth when the Dodgers got a runner to second base with one out. When they failed to score him, Phillips jogged in to face the top of the order. He surrendered a high-flying solo homer to Elly De La Cruz on a fastball above the zone but avoided further damage.
Before the game, the Dodgers added two fresh arms to the bullpen. They recalled right-handers Bobby Miller and Paul Gervase, as they put Henriquez on the IL and optioned right-hander Emmet Sheehan.
Henriquez will undergo imaging on the area, which Roberts said stretched to his side near his oblique.
“The hope is we’ll get him back in the postseason,” Roberts said.
Roberts said he didn’t know what the move meant for Sheehan, who in his past two starts limited opponents to one run and recorded 15 strikeouts in a combined 11 ⅔ innings.
“Some of it’s probably contingent on Roki [Sasaki], and we’ve got another start coming up down the road here, as far as a bullpen kind of situation,” Roberts said. “So I don’t know, but Emmet’s done everything he can do in his power to force our hand, which I love. The last two have been really good.”
Sasaki (right middle finger blister) could start Thursday. His bullpen session Monday marked the first time he had tested covering the sensitive area on his finger with Dermabond, Roberts said.
“We just can’t put him in a position to go backward,” Roberts said.
The Dodgers also have more bullpen reinforcements coming.
Another bullpen addition is left-hander Kris Bubic, who met the team in Cincinnati and is in place to make his Dodgers debut later this week. Bubic made his last rehab appearance for triple-A Oklahoma City on Sunday, so Roberts said the Dodgers likely won’t activate him off the 60-day injured list until Wednesday at the earliest.
The Dodgers acquired Bubic from the Kansas City Royals at the trade deadline this year. He’d been on the IL since May, first with a low-grade flexor strain in his left forearm, and then a shoulder impingement setback.
In six triple-A rehab appearances over 5⅔ innings, Bubic didn’t yield a run and he limited opponents to two hits and two walks.
Roberts was noncommittal about Bubic being a high-leverage option.
“Seems like all of our games are leverage these days,” he said.
By not putting Shohei Ohtani on the injured list in July or in August, the Dodgers may have compromised the two-way star’s ability to be healthy for the playoffs.

item.content:encoded:
Claves: La rodilla de Freeman, el bate de Ohtani y el cálculo de octubre de Dodgers
CINCINNATI — Freddie Freeman no estuvo en la alineación de los Dodgers de Los Ángeles para el juego del lunes por la noche contra los Rojos de Cincinnati mientras lidia con molestias en la rodilla derecha.
Aunque el primera base no ha estado en la alineación en tres de los últimos cinco juegos, el mánager Dave Roberts manifestó que poner a Freeman en la lista de lesionados de 10 días para dejarlo listo para la postemporada —algo similar a lo que hicieron con Shohei Ohtani— no es una opción en este momento.
“No creo que (el descanso) tenga que ser de 10 días, pero ¿podría ser más de uno? Esa es una pregunta válida. Tengo que hablar un poco con el cuerpo de preparadores, con Freddie, y al final tomar esa decisión. Pero no creo que la lista de lesionados tenga sentido”, comentó Roberts.
Roberts señaló que no creía que Freeman fuera a tener problemas persistentes con la rodilla durante la postemporada si se puede manejar adecuadamente. Freeman batea para .293, pero está de 3 en sus últimos 30 turnos, con nueve ponches.
Los campeones defensores de la Serie Mundial por segundo año consecutivo llegaron al lunes por la noche con un número mágico de cuatro para asegurar su 13er título del Oeste de la Liga Nacional en 14 años. Su mayor preocupación es asegurarse de amarrar uno de los dos primeros puestos de preclasificación y un pase directo en la primera ronda.
Los Dodgers (90-59) llegaron al lunes con una ventaja de 2 1/2 juegos sobre Atlanta por el segundo puesto. Milwaukee (93-57) tiene la mejor marca de la Liga Nacional.
“Dado cómo están nuestros muchachos en cuanto a salud, conseguir esa semana sería enorme. Aun así, tenemos que jugar bien para cerrar la temporada y llegar a ese punto”, expresó Roberts.
Ohtani, quien ha estado en la lista de lesionados de 15 días desde el 8 de septiembre debido a una inflamación en el bíceps derecho, hará swings desde un tee en Los Ángeles el martes. Serán sus primeros swings desde que ingresó a la lista de lesionados. Roberts indicó que Ohtani ha estado levantando pesas, entrenando y recibiendo tratamiento en los últimos días.
Con Ohtani fuera del viaje de siete juegos, definitivamente ha habido un ambiente distinto en el clubhouse.
“Se siente diferente porque él tiene mucha presencia cuando está en el campo. La última serie no fue indicativa, pero creo que en general estamos jugando buen béisbol. Sabemos que somos mejores con Shohei. Probablemente los aficionados estén decepcionados, pero no creo que nosotros realmente lo hayamos sentido”, dijo Roberts.
La mayor preocupación podría estar con el relevista Edwin Díaz, quien ha permitido seis carreras limpias en 3 1/3 entradas en cuatro apariciones de rehabilitación con Triple-A Oklahoma City.
Díaz no solo está lidiando con una inflamación en el cuello, sino también con problemas de control. Díaz firmó un contrato de 59 millones de dólares por tres años durante la temporada baja y ha tenido dificultades en su primer año en Los Ángeles.
El derecho tendrá otra salida el miércoles, pero Roberts sí dejó abierta la posibilidad de que Díaz quede fuera de los rosters de postemporada.
“Necesita lanzar mejor. No ha sido bueno. La tarjeta de béisbol se ve genial. Pero, tal como estamos, tiene que haber algo a lo que podamos aferrarnos. Y él lo sabe. Quiere lanzar bien”, afirmó Roberts.
__

item.content:encoded:
Dodgers news: Edgardo Henriquez placed on regular season-ending IL appeared first on ClutchPoints. Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here.
The Los Angeles Dodgers placed right-hander Edgardo Henriquez on the 15-day injured list Monday with low back discomfort, ending his 2026 regular season. Los Angeles recalled Bobby Miller from Triple-A Oklahoma City as the corresponding roster move.
Henriquez had developed into a regular bullpen option during his first full major league season, making 61 appearances. MLB.com's Sonja Chen took to X, formerly Twitter, shortly after the club announced the transaction and noted the calendar implications of Henriquez's IL placement.
"Henriquez going on the 15-day IL ends his regular season."
Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)
Henriquez last pitched Sunday vs. the Miami Marlins, allowing two earned runs on three hits and one walk over two-thirds of an inning. He also recorded one strikeout and received credit for a hold in Los Angeles' 6-4 loss.
The 24-year-old right-hander finishes the regular season with a 4-1 record and 2.85 ERA across 61 games, including one start. The right-hander struck out 71 and walked 25 over 60 innings while posting a 1.03 WHIP. His 61 appearances ranked 24th in the National League.
The timing of the move prevents Henriquez from returning before the regular season concludes September 27. A 15-day placement Monday makes him eligible to return September 29, when the Wild Card Series begins. The move does not automatically rule him out for the postseason if he recovers and earns a roster spot.
The Dodgers have not announced an MRI result, structural diagnosis, or surgery related to Henriquez's back discomfort. His absence removes another pitcher from a Dodgers staff already dealing with multiple injuries, including Shohei Ohtani's right biceps inflammation.
Miller joins the active roster as Los Angeles continues its four-game road series against the Cincinnati Reds. Henriquez's regular season is over, but the Dodgers could still have the right-hander available for the postseason depending on his recovery.
Related: Dodgers tie historic streak with Reds series opener takedown
Related: Tarik Skubal helps Dodgers clinch 14th-straight playoff berth

item.title: [MLB.com] Freeman (knee soreness) out of lineup again, though likely to avoid IL
item.dc:creator: Sonja Chen
item.description: CINCINNATI -- Freddie Freeman was out of the Dodgers' starting lineup for Monday night's series opener against the Reds at Great American Ball Park as the star first baseman continues to manage soreness in his right knee, which he has described as patellar tendinitis. It marked the third time in the Dodgers' past five games that Freeman was not in the starting nine. Manager Dave Roberts reaffirmed that he does not believe Freeman will go on the injured list, and he's expected to return to the li
item.content:encoded:
CINCINNATI -- Freddie Freeman was out of the Dodgers' starting lineup for Monday night's series opener against the Reds at Great American Ball Park as the star first baseman continues to manage soreness in his right knee, which he has described as patellar tendinitis.
It marked the third time in the Dodgers' past five games that Freeman was not in the starting nine. Manager Dave Roberts reaffirmed that he does not believe Freeman will go on the injured list, and he's expected to return to the lineup on Tuesday.
"I just think right now, with where we’re at in the season, an IL is not an option in the sense of -- I personally don’t think we have a better option," Roberts said. "I don’t think it needs to be 10 days. But could it be more than one? That’s a fair question."
Freeman is essentially day to day moving forward. Roberts believes that Freeman's knee has impacted his offensive performance lately, as the 37-year-old is hitting 3-for-30 (.100) with just one extra-base hit in September.
There is some evidence that the knee has been hindering Freeman for longer, as his power numbers have dropped off over the past couple months. He only has one home run in his past 55 games, and he's slugging .350 in that span.
For most of his power drought, Freeman was still hitting for average and consistently getting on base. But when his overall performance took a dip earlier this month, the Dodgers opted to rest him, knowing how important he will be to their offense in the postseason. Freeman is hitting .293 with an .818 OPS in 142 games this season.
Roberts is hopeful that giving Freeman time off now will make it less likely that he'll have to manage his knee throughout the postseason.
"I think that if we can kind of manage it … depending on how the season goes, as far as the recovery," Roberts said. "And then also in the postseason, there’s more off-days. So I think that just trying to get ahold of it, I think that’s the main thing."
The Dodgers' lineup is far from full strength in mid-September, with a dozen regular-season games remaining. Shohei Ohtani is on the 15-day IL due to lingering right biceps and left knee issues and won't be eligible to be activated until Sept. 23. Andy Pages is working his way back from a fracture in his left hand and is also unlikely to return until the final week.
Freeman isn't the only active Dodger who is banged up. Miguel Rojas, who exited early on Sunday after aggravating his right shoulder, was back in the starting lineup on Monday. Rojas is sore but playable, so he'll start against the Reds' left-handed starters this week in Cincinnati.
It's commonly said that every player is dealing with some kind of physical issue, big or small, at this point in the season. Not only have the injuries piled up for the Dodgers of late, but they have affected some of their most important hitters.
But for the Dodgers, who entered Monday a win away from clinching their 14th consecutive postseason berth, the rest of the regular season is less consequential than the games that come after. They will use these final two weeks -- and if they finish with a top-two record in the NL, the bye week -- to get their injured players right in time for the postseason.
"Honestly, I think right now it's front of mind, it's not great," Roberts said. "But I will say this: Once you get to October, athletes have a magical way of feeling better. It happens every single year, where there's that extra adrenaline that athletes get when you get to the postseason.”

item.title: [Diario AS] ¿Cuáles son las lesiones de Shohei Ohtani?
item.dc:creator: Rodrigo Serrano
item.description: Shohei Ohtani se ha perdido seis de los últimos siete partidos de Los Angeles Dodgers debido a las lesiones que ha venido arrastrando esta temporada. item.content:encoded:
Shohei Ohtani se ha perdido seis de los últimos siete partidos de Los Angeles Dodgers debido a las lesiones que ha venido arrastrando esta temporada. La primera fue en la rodilla, una molestia que lo alejó del montículo desde principios de julio y que, con poco tiempo para recuperarse antes de los playoffs, hace casi un hecho que no vuelva a lanzar en 2026. Una baja sensible para los Dodgers en el tramo más importante de la campaña, en el que buscan conquistar su tercera Serie Mundial consecutiva.
Shohei Ohtani to be placed on the injured list (left knee, right biceps), Dodgers manager Dave Roberts announces. pic.twitter.com/AG3VlX3TVe
— MLB (@MLB) September 10, 2026
La segunda lesión que sufrió esta temporada fue en el bíceps, una molestia que ha ido empeorando con el paso de las semanas. Ohtani comenzó a sufrir molestias en el cuello como consecuencia de este problema, lo que obligó a los Dodgers a colocarlo en la lista de lesionados y provocó que se perdiera los últimos encuentros. La buena noticia es que el japonés ha estado trabajando para regresar en este cierre de temporada regular y volver a ocupar su puesto como bateador designado de cara a los playoffs de la MLB.
Ohtani será fundamental en las aspiraciones de los Dodgers
Previo al inicio de la serie ante los Reds en Cincinnati, el mánager de los Dodgers, Dave Roberts, confirmó que Ohtani tiene programado realizar swings desde un tee antes del partido del martes. La actividad representa un paso adelante en su recuperación y mantiene abierta la posibilidad de que pueda regresar a tiempo para ayudar a Los Angeles en los playoffs.
"I think it's important that he does pitch because he has the ability to do it. He's elite."@spillygoat19 shares his thoughts on whether or not he would discourage Shohei Ohtani from pitching in the future.
MLB Network + @NewBalance pic.twitter.com/KqBg6i0pMd
Por fortuna, los Dodgers se prepararon durante la temporada ante una eventual ausencia prolongada de su superestrella. Por esa razón, adquirieron al pitcher Tarik Skubal antes de la fecha límite de intercambios para fortalecer una rotación de lanzadores que buscará llegar en las mejores condiciones a la postemporada.
Shohei Ohtani could resume swinging Monday or Tuesday as he continues recovering from lingering right biceps and left knee issues.
Ohtani is eligible to return from the IL on September 23, giving him a short window to prepare for the postseason.#Dodgers #BlueDynasty pic.twitter.com/l2vdNja7kE
Además, los Dodgers llamó a uno de los mejores prospectos de las Grandes Ligas, Josue De Paula, para aportar a la ofensiva mientras Ohtani se recupera. El pelotero impresionó en sus primeros partidos ante los Marlins, una actuación que le permite a los Dodgers darle mayor tiempo de recuperación a Ohtani con la esperanza de que esté listo para disputar el Clásico de Otoño.

item.title: [thebiglead.com] Shohei Ohtani injury; Dodgers manager Dave Roberts has an update before Reds matchup
item.dc:creator: Miracle Dimwesh
item.description: Shohei Ohtani will not be in the Los Angeles Dodgers’ lineup again as the team takes a cautious approach with its two-way superstar. item.content:encoded:
Shohei Ohtani will not be in the Los Angeles Dodgers’ lineup again as the team takes a cautious approach with its two-way superstar.
Ohtani has been dealing with soreness in his left knee, right biceps and neck. Dodgers manager Dave Roberts provided an update before Monday’s matchup with the Cincinnati Reds.
Roberts described the decision to rest Ohtani as “proactive.” He also indicated that Ohtani would likely play if the Dodgers were preparing for a postseason game instead.
That distinction explains the Dodgers’ approach. Los Angeles has a comfortable position in the NL West, giving the team more freedom to protect its biggest star.
Ohtani’s season has still been impressive despite the physical issues. He is hitting .277 with 30 home runs, 80 RBIs and a .902 OPS in 130 games.
His pitching season is already over, though. Ohtani went 8-2 with a 1.79 ERA and 144 strikeouts over 85.2 innings in 14 starts before the Dodgers shut him down on the mound.
Now, Los Angeles must manage his workload on offense as well. Ohtani returned to the lineup earlier this month but struggled during his final stretch before landing on the injured list.
The timing makes the decision easier for the Dodgers. Los Angeles entered Monday with a 90-59 record and a strong lead in the NL West.
The Dodgers are also competing with the Milwaukee Brewers for the best record in the National League. That makes every game important, but keeping Ohtani healthy for October carries even greater value.
The Reds entered the matchup at 70-79 and are no longer in the NL Central race. They can still create problems for a Dodgers lineup missing its biggest offensive threat.
For now, Roberts appears more concerned with the bigger picture. Ohtani does not need to push through September discomfort if the Dodgers can give him time to recover.
That could mean more rest days in the coming weeks. The Dodgers would rather have a healthy Ohtani in October than risk making his current issues worse in September.
If this were a postseason game, Roberts suggested the decision might be different. For now, the Dodgers are choosing to protect their biggest weapon.

item.title: [Diario Libre] De Brooklyn a Santo Domingo y de Doble-A a los Dodgers: la ruta de Josué De Paula
item.dc:creator: Omar Santana
item.description: El jardinero de 21 años abandonó Nueva York durante la pandemia para intentar firmar como profesional en República Dominicana. Los Dodgers lo contrataron por US$397,500 y cuatro años después se saltó Triple-A para llegar a Grandes Ligas. item.content:encoded:
El jardinero de 21 años abandonó Nueva York durante la pandemia para intentar firmar como profesional en República Dominicana. Los Dodgers lo contrataron por US$397,500 y cuatro años después se saltó Triple-A para llegar a Grandes Ligas.
El primer hit de Josué De Paula en las Grandes Ligas no fue un sencillo para guardar discretamente en una vitrina. Fue un cuadrangular de tres carreras.
El domingo, en Miami, el joven jardinero de los Dodgers encontró una recta de Eury Pérez y la envió al segundo nivel del jardín derecho del loanDepot park. La pelota recorrió unos 416 pies y salió del bate a 108.2 millas por hora. Más tarde agregó un doble y terminó de 2-2 en la derrota 6-4 de Los Ángeles ante los Marlins.
Era apenas su tercer día como jugador de Grandes Ligas.
La imagen resume una historia que comenzó de manera poco convencional. De Paula nació el 24 de mayo de 2005 en Brooklyn, Nueva York. Creció en Estados Unidos, asistió a Benjamin N. Cardozo High School, en Queens, y pertenece a una familia con antecedentes deportivos: es primo segundo de los exjugadores de la NBA Stephon Marbury y Sebastian Telfair.
Pero su camino hacia el béisbol profesional no pasó inicialmente por el sistema estadounidense de escuelas secundarias, universidades y draft.
Pasó por República Dominicana.
La pandemia cambió el camino
De Paula apenas había disputado su primer partido de béisbol con Cardozo cuando la pandemia de COVID-19 paralizó el deporte escolar en 2020.
Durante ese período, según relató posteriormente el propio jugador, su padre le planteó una alternativa: trasladarse a República Dominicana y tratar de abrirse paso por la ruta que cada año siguen cientos de prospectos latinoamericanos que entrenan para conseguir contratos con organizaciones de Grandes Ligas.
La familia se trasladó al país en 2021. De Paula tenía 15 años.
En Santo Domingo entrenó en El Niche Baseball Academy. El cambio era considerable: había nacido y crecido en Nueva York, pero entraba ahora al competitivo sistema dominicano de desarrollo de prospectos internacionales.
La apuesta tardó apenas unos meses en producir resultados.
US$397,500 y una firma que terminó pareciendo barata
El 15 de enero de 2022, cuando tenía 16 años, De Paula firmó con los Dodgers como agente libre internacional por un bono de US$397,500. Aunque nació en Estados Unidos, fue captado y firmado desde República Dominicana.
No era el nombre principal de aquella clase internacional de Los Ángeles. Los Dodgers anunciaron alrededor de 30 firmas y la atención se concentraba entonces sobre todo en otros prospectos de mayor cotización.
Con el tiempo, esos US$397,500 comenzaron a parecer una inversión muy favorable para la organización.
Su primera prueba profesional ocurrió precisamente en el país donde había buscado la firma.
En 2022 jugó para DSL Dodgers Bautista en la Dominican Summer League. Bateó .349, tuvo porcentaje de embazarse de .448 y slugging de .522 en 53 partidos, con cinco jonrones, 30 carreras impulsadas, 42 anotadas y 16 bases robadas. Fue seleccionado al equipo Todos Estrellas de postemporada de la liga.
El experimento dominicano había funcionado.
El difícil salto a Estados Unidos
En 2023 comenzó el recorrido por el sistema de ligas menores de Estados Unidos con Rancho Cucamonga, sucursal Clase A de los Dodgers.
Allí apareció una de las características que después llamaría la atención de la organización: su capacidad de controlar la zona de strike. En 74 partidos bateó .284, llegó a base a ritmo de .396 y produjo 40 carreras. El poder, sin embargo, todavía no había llegado: solo conectó dos cuadrangulares.
El crecimiento se hizo más evidente en 2024.
Entre Rancho Cucamonga y Great Lakes jugó 107 encuentros y terminó con promedio de .268, OBP de .404, 10 jonrones, 62 remolcadas y 27 bases robadas. Además negoció 84 transferencias, una cifra que reflejaba su disciplina en el plato a una edad en la que muchos prospectos todavía dependen casi exclusivamente de sus condiciones físicas.
Durante una de esas temporadas muertas entrenó en Miami junto a Juan Soto y Elly De La Cruz. La atención comenzó a trasladarse hacia el desarrollo de poder en un cuerpo de 6 pies y 3 pulgadas.
Los Dodgers empezaron a hablar de él en términos poco habituales. Dentro de la organización llegó a ser considerado uno de los bateadores jóvenes más avanzados desarrollados por el club en años recientes.
El jonrón que lo puso delante de todos
La explosión mediática llegó en julio.
De Paula fue seleccionado para el Juego de Futuras Estrellas y encontró a dos corredores en circulación frente al zurdo Noah Schultz, otro de los principales prospectos de MLB.
Conectó un slider y mandó la pelota 416 pies por el jardín derecho-central. El batazo salió a 108.5 millas por hora, dio ventaja 3-2 a la Liga Nacional y terminó convirtiéndolo en el Jugador Más Valioso del partido.
Era el primer prospecto de los Dodgers que recibía ese reconocimiento desde Chin-Lung Hu en 2007. Entre los dominicanos que lo habían ganado anteriormente estaban Alfonso Soriano y José Reyes.
Su temporada terminó con 12 cuadrangulares y 32 robos. Tras 98 encuentros con Great Lakes recibió finalmente el ascenso a Doble-A Tulsa, pero allí tuvo un aterrizaje abrupto: se fue sin hits en 18 turnos durante cuatro partidos.
Fue una pausa, no un techo.
¿Jugó con el Escogido?
De Paula pertenece a los Leones del Escogido.
El equipo lo seleccionó en la tercera ronda del Sorteo de Novatos de Lidom de 2023, cuando todavía era un jugador de Clase A de los Dodgers.
Sin embargo, en las fuentes oficiales y registros revisados no aparece evidencia de que haya disputado hasta ahora un partido oficial de temporada regular con los Leones. Es decir, sus derechos en el béisbol otoño-invernal dominicano pertenecen al Escogido, pero su desarrollo competitivo se ha mantenido dentro del sistema de los Dodgers.
El año que abrió la puerta
En 2026 regresó a Tulsa y convirtió Doble-A en su plataforma de lanzamiento.
En 124 partidos bateó .303, con .401 de porcentaje de embasarse y .547 de slugging. Disparó 27 jonrones, produjo 104 carreras y robó 31 bases. En toda su trayectoria de ligas menores acumuló 460 partidos con línea ofensiva de .286/.404/.453, 56 cuadrangulares y 280 impulsadas.
Ascenso a Grandes Ligas
También mejoró una variable que suele determinar si un bateador joven puede trasladar su producción a las Mayores: redujo su porcentaje de ponches mientras aumentaba considerablemente el poder.
En los entrenamientos de primavera ya había dado señales. Bateó .375 en 14 encuentros y volvió a participar en el Juego de Futuras Estrellas durante el verano.
Todavía faltaba un escalón: Triple-A.
Los Dodgers decidieron saltárselo.
De Doble-A directamente a sustituir a Ohtani
La oportunidad apareció cuando Los Ángeles colocó a Shohei Ohtani en la lista de lesionados.
El 11 de septiembre, los Dodgers seleccionaron el contrato de De Paula desde Tulsa. Para incorporarlo al roster de 40 jugadores trasladaron al lanzador Eric Lauer a la lista de lesionados de 60 días.
El movimiento resultó especialmente significativo: De Paula se convirtió en el primer jugador de posición de los Dodgers en saltar directamente de Doble-A a Grandes Ligas en más de una década.
Ni siquiera él esperaba que ocurriera de esa manera.
Cuando el dirigente de Tulsa, Eric Wedge, lo llamó a su oficina y le informó que tomaría un avión para reunirse con "los muchachos grandes", De Paula contó que inicialmente no entendió hacia dónde lo estaban enviando. Pensaba que Triple-A era el paso siguiente.
El viernes 11 de septiembre apareció como bateador designado y séptimo en la alineación contra Miami. Tenía 21 años y 110 días, convirtiéndose en uno de los Dodgers más jóvenes en debutar durante los últimos años. No consiguió hit en tres turnos, pero recibió una transferencia.
Dos días después ocupó por primera vez los jardines.
Y entonces llegó Eury Pérez.
De Paula conectó su primer hit de Grandes Ligas, un jonrón de tres carreras, y luego agregó un doble. Cuatro años y ocho meses después de firmar por US$397,500 en República Dominicana, el muchacho que salió de Brooklyn durante una pandemia y volvió al Caribe buscando una oportunidad ya estaba produciendo carreras para los Dodgers en septiembre.
La lesión de Ohtani abrió la puerta. Sus cuatro años atravesando la Dominican Summer League, Clase A, Clase A Avanzada y Doble-A explican por qué los Dodgers decidieron que no necesitaba tocar ninguna otra antes de entrar.

item.title: [NBC Sports] Tommy Edman sits for Sunday's series finale
item.dc:creator: David Shovein; Tommy Edman
item.description:
Tommy Edman is not in the Dodgers’ starting lineup for Sunday’s series finale against the Marlins in Miami.
Edman has been a fixture atop the Dodgers’ lineup since Shohei Ohtani was shelved, so he’ll get a well-deserved day off in this one. Miguel Rojas will cover second base in his absence and will hit eighth against Marlins’ right-hander Eury Perez.
item.content:encoded:
Tommy Edman is not in the Dodgers’ starting lineup for Sunday’s series finale against the Marlins in Miami.

Edman has been a fixture atop the Dodgers’ lineup since Shohei Ohtani was shelved, so he’ll get a well-deserved day off in this one. Miguel Rojas will cover second base in his absence and will hit eighth against Marlins’ right-hander Eury Perez.
